title: PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF is a silent no-op inside the migration runner's transaction
detail: The migration runner (scripts/migrate.ts:209-213) wraps every migration in db.transaction(), so migrate010 always executes inside an open transaction. Migration 010 calls db.pragma("foreign_keys = OFF") at line 97 before the DROP/RENAME table rebuild and db.pragma("foreign_keys = ON") at line 119 after. Per SQLite semantics, PRAGMA foreign_keys is a no-op while a transaction is pending — it can only be toggled when no BEGIN/SAVEPOINT is active. Therefore the intended FK disable never happens; foreign-key enforcement stays ON throughout the table rebuild. The migration happens to still succeed because the only FK involved is guild_question -> guild_config (parent), which the copied rows satisfy, and nothing references guild_question as a parent. But the code's stated safety strategy ('disable foreign keys temporarily to rebuild the table') is silently defeated, and the final pragma at line 119 also does nothing, so FK state after the migration is whatever the runner set (ON), not something this code controls. If a future child table is added that references guild_question, the DROP at line 114 would fail unexpectedly because FKs are actually enforced.
fix: Drop the foreign_keys pragma toggling here (it cannot work inside the runner transaction). For SQLite table rebuilds that truly need FKs off, use the documented 12-step procedure: toggle PRAGMA foreign_keys OUTSIDE any transaction (e.g. have the runner expose a non-transactional path) or use PRAGMA legacy_alter_table plus a foreign_key_check after rebuild. At minimum, remove the misleading OFF/ON calls and add a `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` after the rebuild to assert integrity.

title: CREATE INDEX on action_log has no table-existence guard (crashes on fresh DB)
detail: Migration 004 creates idx_action_log_guild_action_time on action_log guarded only by indexExists(), never by tableExists("action_log"). action_log is created by src/db/ensure.ts (ensureActionLogSchema), which the standalone migration runner scripts/migrate.ts does NOT invoke. scripts/migrate.ts opens the DB with fileMustExist:false (it even warns it will 'happily create a fresh DB'), and only creates schema_migrations. If `npm run migrate` is run against a DB where action_log does not yet exist (fresh DB, or before the bot has run ensure once), CREATE INDEX ... ON action_log throws 'no such table: action_log' and aborts the migration. This is inconsistent with migrations 001/017/018/027, which explicitly guard guild_config existence for exactly this reason.
fix: Wrap the CREATE INDEX in `if (tableExists(db, 'action_log'))` (import the helper) and skip + recordMigration when absent, mirroring the guild_config guards in migrations 001/017/018.

title: References legacy TEXT column updated_at without a columnExists guard; throws on fresh-schema DBs
detail: Migration 027 backfills updated_at_s from the legacy TEXT column updated_at, querying `... WHERE updated_at_s IS NULL AND updated_at IS NOT NULL` (line 56) and updating via strftime('%s', updated_at) (line 80). It guards tableExists(guild_config) and adds updated_at_s if missing, but never checks that the `updated_at` column exists. The current src/db/ensure.ts creates guild_config with only (guild_id, logging_channel_id, updated_at_s) — there is NO updated_at TEXT column on a fresh schema. Running migration 027 on such a DB raises 'no such column: updated_at' at line 56, failing the migration. It only works on legacy DBs that still carry the old TEXT updated_at column.
fix: Guard the TEXT-backfill block with `if (columnExists(db, 'guild_config', 'updated_at')) { ... }`. When the legacy column is absent, skip the strftime backfill and only run the default-timestamp fill for NULL updated_at_s rows.

title: ALTER TABLE modmail_message with no table-existence guard (crashes on fresh DB)
detail: Migration 021 runs PRAGMA table_info(modmail_message) then ALTER TABLE modmail_message ADD COLUMN content. If modmail_message does not exist (fresh DB run through the standalone scripts/migrate.ts, which never calls ensure.ts to create base tables), PRAGMA table_info returns an empty array so hasContent is false, and the subsequent ALTER throws 'no such table: modmail_message', failing the migration. Same latent fresh-DB ordering gap as migrations 004/022/023/024; inconsistent with the table guards used in 001/017/018.
fix: Add `if (!tableExists(db, 'modmail_message')) { recordMigration(db,'021','add_modmail_message_content'); return; }` (import the helper) before introspecting/altering.

title: CREATE INDEX on transcript with no table-existence guard
detail: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_transcript_app_ts ON transcript(app_id, ts) has no tableExists('transcript') guard. The IF NOT EXISTS clause only suppresses errors when the INDEX already exists, not when the base table is missing — if transcript does not exist, SQLite raises 'no such table: transcript'. Triggers only if migrate.ts is run standalone against a DB where the transcript table has not yet been created by ensure.ts. Same class of fresh-DB ordering gap as 004/021/023/024.
fix: Guard with `if (tableExists(db, 'transcript'))` before creating the index, then recordMigration regardless.

title: CREATE INDEX on user_activity with no table-existence guard
detail: Both CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS statements target user_activity without a tableExists guard. user_activity is created by migration 005, so in normal migrate-runner ordering (005 before 023) the table exists; but if 023 is run in isolation or against a DB where user_activity was never created (e.g. only base ensure.ts tables), the statements raise 'no such table: user_activity'. IF NOT EXISTS does not cover a missing base table. Also note idx_user_activity_guild_user is already created by migration 005 (line 110); re-creating it here is harmless (IF NOT EXISTS) but redundant.
fix: Guard the index creation with `if (tableExists(db, 'user_activity'))`; optionally drop the duplicate idx_user_activity_guild_user creation already handled by migration 005.

title: CREATE INDEX on review_action with no table-existence guard
detail: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_review_action_app_time ON review_action(app_id, created_at DESC) lacks a tableExists('review_action') guard. If review_action does not exist (fresh DB via standalone migrate.ts before ensure.ts creates it), SQLite raises 'no such table: review_action'. IF NOT EXISTS protects only against a pre-existing index, not a missing table.
fix: Guard with `if (tableExists(db, 'review_action'))` before creating the index, then recordMigration regardless.

title: Migration 039 runs on a second DB connection outside the runner's transaction and never records itself (perpetual re-run, broken atomicity)
detail: Unlike every other migration in the project (which is exported as migrateNNN(db: Database) and receives the runner's connection), migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint() takes NO parameter and instead does `import { db } from "../src/db/db.js"` (line 12), operating on the singleton connection opened by src/db/db.ts. The runner in scripts/migrate.ts (lines 195-213) loads the function via name `migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint`, then runs it inside `db.transaction(() => migrateFn(db))` using ITS OWN better-sqlite3 handle (scripts/migrate.ts line 50). Three concrete consequences: (1) Atomicity is broken. All of 039's writes (the renumber UPDATEs on lines 44-48, DROP INDEX line 53, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX lines 56-59) execute on the singleton connection via autocommit, completely outside the runner's transaction. The runner's transaction stays empty (it issues no writes on its own connection), so if 039 throws partway (e.g. the UNIQUE index creation fails because a duplicate slipped through), the renumber UPDATEs are already committed and will NOT roll back. (2) recordMigration is never called (compare every other migration, e.g. 040 line 135, 038 line 33). The runner does not record versions itself (scripts/migrate.ts applyMigration has no recordMigration call), so version "039" is never inserted into schema_migrations and 039 is treated as pending on every single run -- it re-executes each time `migrate.ts` runs and forces a fresh backup every run (scripts/migrate.ts line 253 filters by appliedVersions which never contains 039). (3) Importing src/db/db.ts from inside the migration process triggers that module's large top-level schema bootstrap (tables + addColumnIfMissing + index creation, src/db/db.ts lines 113-419) to run on a SECOND WAL connection to the same file during the migration -- an unexpected, heavy side effect and a second live handle to the DB the runner is migrating.
fix: Refactor 039 to the standard signature: `export function migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint(db: Database): void` and remove the `import { db } from "../src/db/db.js"`. Use the passed-in `db` for all statements so the work runs inside the runner's transaction. Add `recordMigration(db, "039", "fix_art_job_unique_constraint")` at the end (importing it from ./lib/helpers.js) so the migration is recorded and stops re-running.

title: guild_config column-add migrations omit the tableExists guard used by 030/031, so they throw on a DB where guild_config does not yet exist
detail: 030 (lines 34-40) and 031 (lines 69-75) explicitly guard `if (!tableExists(db, "guild_config")) { recordMigration(...); return; }` before ALTERing guild_config, because guild_config is not created by any migration -- it is only created at runtime by src/db/ensure.ts (ensureActionLogSchema) / the self-heal path, which the standalone `scripts/migrate.ts` runner does not invoke. Migrations 045 (this file, line 29-31), 048 (lines 18-19), 056 (lines 55-63), 059 (lines 19-21) and 061 (lines 32-34) drop that guard: when columnExists returns false on a DB that has no guild_config table, the subsequent `ALTER TABLE guild_config ADD COLUMN ...` throws `no such table: guild_config` and aborts the migration. In the live production DB guild_config always exists (so this is latent rather than always-firing), but the divergence from the safer pattern established in 030/031 means a fresh-DB or partial-DB migration run fails on these files where it would have cleanly skipped under the 030/031 pattern.
fix: Mirror the 030/031 pattern in 045/048/056/059/061: wrap the guild_config ALTERs in `if (!tableExists(db, "guild_config")) { recordMigration(...); return; }` (or assert guild_config existence centrally before the guild_config-dependent migrations run).

title: Patreon art-grant backfill iterates role.members without fetching members → silently grants nothing
detail: After login the script does `const guild = client.guilds.cache.get(guildId)` and then iterates `role.members` (line 100) to backfill `patreon_art_granted` ticket quantities. It never calls `guild.members.fetch()`. `role.members` is a live filter over the guild member cache, which is essentially empty for a freshly-connected client (Discord only pushes a small set during READY even with the GuildMembers intent). As a result `role.members.size` is 0 (or near-0) for every tier, the inner loop never runs, and the script prints 'Processing <tier> (0 members)' followed by 'Backfill complete: 0 members, 0 grant records.' — exiting 0 as if it succeeded. Because this is the one-time economy backfill that must run after migration 062 and before enabling `patreon_art_rewards_enabled`, entitled Patreon supporters silently never get their headshot/fullbody/emoji ticket grants backfilled, and the silent success makes the gap easy to miss. The sibling scripts backfill-user-cache.ts and backfill-user-cache.mjs prove the intended pattern: they `await guild.members.fetch()` before reading members.
fix: Fetch members before reading role membership: replace `const guild = client.guilds.cache.get(guildId)` with `const guild = await client.guilds.fetch(guildId); await guild.members.fetch();` (or call `guild.members.fetch()` immediately after the cache.get null-check). This populates the cache so `role.members` is correctly populated for every tier.

title: `--limit` with a missing value yields NaN and the per-run limit is silently ignored
detail: `const LIMIT = limitArg >= 0 ? parseInt(args[limitArg + 1], 10) : Infinity;` When `--limit` is passed as the final argument with no following value, `args[limitArg+1]` is undefined and `parseInt(undefined,10)` is NaN. Later `if (runAdded >= LIMIT)` (line 153) is `runAdded >= NaN`, which is always false, so the intended smoke-test cap never triggers and the script pages the entire #general history instead of stopping. Not data-corrupting (INSERT OR IGNORE), but defeats the documented `--limit 500` smoke-test mode and can run far longer / hit far more Discord API than the operator intended.
fix: Validate the parsed value: `const n = parseInt(args[limitArg+1], 10); const LIMIT = Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : Infinity;` and error out (or warn) if `--limit` is present but the value is missing/NaN.

title: `--batch` with a missing/non-numeric value produces NaN and the LIMIT bind throws a datatype-mismatch
detail: `const MAX_BATCH = batchArg >= 0 ? parseInt(args[batchArg + 1], 10) : 5000;` If `--batch` is supplied without a following numeric value, `MAX_BATCH` becomes NaN, which is then bound as the `LIMIT ?` parameter at line 37. better-sqlite3 rejects NaN as an integer parameter with `SQLITE_MISMATCH: datatype mismatch`, so the cron-run aborts with an unhandled exception before doing any work. Fails safe (no corruption) but the scheduled context materialization silently stops making progress until someone notices the crashing cron job.
fix: Guard the parse: `const n = parseInt(args[batchArg+1], 10); const MAX_BATCH = Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : 5000;`

title: Thread-only fields serialized as undefined for non-thread channels; no null-guard on fetched channel
detail: client.channels.fetch(threadId) can resolve to a non-thread channel (or, per discord.js typings, null). The code then reads channel.type, channel.archived, channel.locked, channel.name unconditionally. For a normal text/voice channel, .archived and .locked do not exist and serialize as missing/undefined, so the script silently reports a thread as un-archived/un-locked instead of indicating it is not a thread. If fetch returns null, accessing .type throws a TypeError that is swallowed by the inner catch and mis-reported as exists:false with a generic message. Impact is limited to a developer diagnostic giving misleading output; no production path.
fix: Guard for null first (if (!channel) report not-found), then branch on channel.isThread() before reading archived/locked, e.g. report a 'notAThread' shape for non-thread channels rather than emitting undefined fields.

title: Name-resolution queries assume auxiliary tables (user_names, user_message_counts) exist; missing table throws and aborts the whole dump
detail: Sections 9, 16 and 20 query user_message_counts and user_names. These tables are not created by any migration in the repo (only referenced by the chart pipeline scripts and the test fixture schema). better-sqlite3's db.prepare() throws synchronously on 'no such table', and these queries are not wrapped in try/catch, so on a DB where the chart-pipeline auxiliary tables have not been built the entire 20-dataset dump aborts partway with an uncaught error and writes nothing to stdout. This is an operational EC2 analytics script (documented as reading pre-built tables), so impact is confined to that pipeline, but the failure mode is all-or-nothing rather than degrading the one affected dataset.
fix: Wrap the user_names / user_message_counts lookups (and ideally each numbered section) in try/catch, or probe sqlite_master for the table first and fall back to id.slice(-6) when absent, so one missing auxiliary table cannot abort the full export.

title: voiceChannelTotals counts full session duration for sessions starting in-window, inflating 30d totals
detail: Unlike voiceMinutesDaily (section 11) which splits each session across the days it spans, section 12 sums (left_at_s - joined_at_s) for every session with joined_at_s >= startS without clipping the lower bound to startS, and for still-open sessions uses nowS - joined_at_s. A long session that began just inside the 30-day window contributes its entire (possibly multi-day) length to the 30-day treemap, and a never-closed session contributes its full age. The chart therefore overstates recent voice minutes per channel. Analytics-only, no functional impact.
fix: Clip the duration to the window: SUM(MIN(COALESCE(left_at_s, ?), ?) - MAX(joined_at_s, ?)) with params (nowS, nowS, startS), mirroring the day-splitting approach used for voiceMinutesDaily.

title: Copy-swap re-runs strftime('%s', created_at) on already-INTEGER epoch values, corrupting every timestamp
detail: needsMigration() returns true if ANY of {CHECK present, created_at!=INTEGER, FK!=CASCADE, missing idx_review_action_app_time} holds (line 86). Unlike migration 028 (which early-returns the moment created_at is already INTEGER), this script has NO such guard: if the table is otherwise fully correct (created_at already INTEGER Unix epoch) but merely lacks the idx_review_action_app_time index or has a non-CASCADE FK, runMigration() still executes the full copy-swap. The INSERT...SELECT then applies CAST(strftime('%s', created_at) AS INTEGER) to the already-INTEGER epoch column (lines 128-135). I verified in better-sqlite3 that strftime('%s', 1700000000) does NOT return NULL — it treats the integer as a date-ish numeric and returns garbage (e.g. 1700000000 -> 1780244213, ~year 2026), so COALESCE keeps the corrupted value. Result: running this 'repair' on a healthy DB that is only missing an index silently rewrites EVERY review_action.created_at to a bogus timestamp, destroying the audit trail's chronology and breaking idx_review_action_app_time ordering / time-range analytics. The transaction's only integrity check is row COUNT (lines 143-145), which still matches, so the corruption passes undetected.
fix: Mirror migration 028's guard: in needsMigration(), if getCreatedAtType()==='INTEGER', do NOT trigger the destructive copy-swap solely for a missing index or FK fix — instead create the index / rebuild only when a real schema (CHECK or TEXT created_at) problem exists, and add the index via a plain CREATE INDEX when that is the only deficiency. Equivalently, in the INSERT...SELECT only apply strftime conversion when the source created_at type is TEXT; when it is already INTEGER, copy created_at verbatim.

title: Unguarded .get().sql throws opaque TypeError when source table is absent
detail: Line 13 does src.prepare(`SELECT sql ... name='general_messages_embed'`).get().sql. If the table does not exist in the source DB, .get() returns undefined and .sql throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading sql)' with no context. The sibling export-processed.mjs handles this gracefully with `?.sql` + a 'skip (not found)' message (lines 29-30). export-score.mjs and export-substantiveness.mjs share the identical defect on their line 13. Impact is limited to operator confusion on a misconfigured/empty snapshot DB; data is not corrupted.
fix: Use optional chaining and a clear error/skip: `const row = src.prepare(...).get(); if (!row?.sql) { console.error('table general_messages_embed not found in', SRC); process.exit(1); } dst.exec(row.sql);` — matching export-processed.mjs.

title: Unguarded .get().sql throws opaque TypeError when general_messages_score is absent
detail: Same defect as export-embed.mjs line 13: `src.prepare(...).get().sql` dereferences undefined and throws an opaque TypeError if the source table is missing, instead of a clear message. Trusted-local-data tool, so impact is operator confusion only.
fix: Guard with `const row = ...get(); if (!row?.sql) { ...exit with message... }` before dst.exec.

title: Unguarded .get().sql throws opaque TypeError when general_messages_substantiveness is absent
detail: Same defect as export-embed.mjs/export-score.mjs line 13: `src.prepare(...).get().sql` will throw an opaque TypeError if the table is missing rather than reporting it. Trusted-local-data tool; impact is operator confusion only.
fix: Guard the result with optional chaining and exit with a descriptive message before dst.exec.

title: Hardcoded SRC ignores DB_PATH env var honored by every sibling exporter
detail: SRC is hardcoded to 'data/data.db.processed-snapshot' (line 4) and there is no DB_PATH override, whereas export-overlay.mjs, export-processed.mjs, export-score.mjs, and export-substantiveness.mjs all use `process.env.DB_PATH || 'data/data.db'`. An operator who exports the suite with `DB_PATH=...` set will get the embed table from a different (possibly stale or wrong) database than the others, producing an inconsistent shipped bundle. The OUT is also hardcoded (line 5) unlike the siblings that accept argv[2].
fix: Make SRC consistent: `const SRC = process.env.DB_PATH || 'data/data.db.processed-snapshot';` and accept `const OUT = process.argv[2] || '/tmp/embed-export.db';` so the embed exporter participates in the same configuration contract as its siblings.

title: Division by zero produces NaN coordinates when only one week qualifies (count>=100)
detail: x0 = min(xs), x1 = max(xs) (line 75). xPx(x) = PAD.left + ((x - x0)/(x1 - x0)) * PW (line 79). If exactly one row passes the `count >= 100` filter (line 23), x0 === x1, so every xPx() evaluates 0/0 = NaN and the line/grid render to nothing (blank or garbage chart) rather than failing fast. The mini-chart grid has the same xLo===xHi hazard (lines 249-251). The non-empty guard at line 28 only checks rows.length>0, not >=2.
fix: After filtering, guard `if (rows.length < 2) { console.error('need >=2 qualifying weeks to chart'); process.exit(1); }`, or clamp the denominator: `const span = (x1 - x0) || 1;` and special-case a single point.

title: channelId parsing uses args.indexOf(a) inside find(), misbehaving on duplicate token values
detail: Line 44: `args.find((a) => !a.startsWith('--') && !args[args.indexOf(a) - 1]?.startsWith('--limit'))`. Using args.indexOf(a) returns the FIRST index of the value, not the current iteration index, so if a later positional argument has the same string value as an earlier token the predicate evaluates against the wrong neighbor. More realistically, the intent 'skip the value following --limit' is also implemented separately in positionalArgs (line 49) using the proper index parameter, so the two parsers can disagree. For normal invocations (id [output] [--limit N]) it happens to work, but the indexOf approach is incorrect and can pick the wrong channelId for unusual argument orderings (e.g. --limit before the id).
fix: Pass the index from find: `args.find((a, i) => !a.startsWith('--') && args[i - 1] !== '--limit')`, consistent with the positionalArgs filter on line 49.

title: Multi-batch message fetch produces non-chronological output (batches interleaved/mis-ordered)
detail: fetchMessagesFromChannel (lines 150-183) fetches messages 100 at a time (newest-first), sorts each batch oldest-first, then prepends each message with messages.unshift(...) (line 167), and finally calls messages.reverse() (line 182). Tracing two batches: batch1 IDs [10,9,8] -> sorted [8,9,10] -> after unshifts messages=[10,9,8]; batch2 (older) IDs [7,6,5] -> sorted [5,6,7] -> after unshifts messages=[7,6,5,10,9,8]; final reverse() yields [8,9,10,5,6,7]. Correct chronological order is [5,6,7,8,9,10]. So any channel/thread with more than 100 messages is archived with the message blocks out of order across every 100-message boundary. The header 'Total messages' count is still correct, so the corruption is silent. For channels under 100 messages (single batch) the output happens to be correct, which masks the bug in light testing.
fix: Drop the per-batch sort + unshift + final reverse entirely. Since Discord returns each batch newest-first and you page with `before: lastId` (strictly older each iteration), simply push each batch's IDs and at the very end build the array oldest-first once. Concretely: collect raw messages into one array via `all.push(...fetched.values())` per batch (newest-first overall), then do `all.sort((a,b) => a.createdTimestamp - b.createdTimestamp)` and map to formatMessage. One global sort by createdTimestamp is unambiguous and removes the interleaving.

title: Division by zero yields NaN coordinates (blank/corrupt chart) when only one week passes the count>=100 filter
detail: After the `WHERE count >= 100` filter (lines 18-25) only `rows.length === 0` is guarded (line 28). If exactly one row qualifies, then xs has one element so x0 === x1 (lines 75, 249) and the x-scaling functions xPx/xp compute `(x - x0) / (x1 - x0)` = 0/0 = NaN (lines 79, 250). Every plotted x becomes NaN, so canvas draws nothing on the X axis and the per-metric PNGs plus the combined _dashboard.png are produced but visually empty/broken, with no error emitted. This is reachable early in a deployment's life or with a high count threshold.
fix: Guard the degenerate span: after computing x0/x1, if `x1 === x0` either bail with a clear message (`console.error('need >=2 qualifying weeks to chart'); process.exit(1);`) or fall back to a 1px-wide mapping (`const span = (x1 - x0) || 1;` and divide by `span`). Apply in both the main plotMetric scope (line 79) and the mini-chart loop (line 250).

title: Non-idempotent insert with fixed audit_run_id double-counts on re-run
detail: auditRunId is the hardcoded constant "audit-20260112-manual" (line 7). Each finding is written via insertFinding(...) which runs a plain INSERT into audit_findings; that table (migrations/043_audit_findings.ts) has only an AUTOINCREMENT primary key and NO unique constraint on (audit_run_id, command_name, subcommand). Re-running the script therefore inserts a second full copy of every finding under the same run id. generateReportData() then aggregates by audit_run_id, so totalCommands, passCount, skipCount, etc. (and the generated markdown report) silently double (or triple) for that run. The script also has no pre-delete of the existing run. Impact is limited because this is a manual one-shot script, not a runtime path.
fix: Before inserting, delete existing rows for the run (DELETE FROM audit_findings WHERE audit_run_id = ?) inside a transaction, or add a UNIQUE(audit_run_id, command_name, subcommand) index and use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. At minimum, derive auditRunId from a timestamp at runtime so each run is distinct.

title: writeFileSync to docs/audits without ensuring the directory exists
detail: The report is written with writeFileSync(`docs/audits/audit-${auditRunId}.md`, markdown) but the script never creates docs/audits/. If that directory is absent (fresh checkout, or run from a different cwd), writeFileSync throws ENOENT after all DB inserts have already committed, so the run half-succeeds (data written, report lost) and exits non-zero. Other scripts in this repo guard this with mkdirSync(dir,{recursive:true}) (see train-effort-v1.mjs lines 258-259).
fix: Call mkdirSync(path.dirname(reportPath), { recursive: true }) before writeFileSync.

title: Zero-copy Float32Array view assumes 4-byte aligned Buffer byteOffset
detail: vec(buf) returns new Float32Array(buf.buffer, buf.byteOffset, buf.byteLength/4). The 3-arg typed-array constructor throws RangeError('start offset of Float32Array should be a multiple of 4') if buf.byteOffset is not a multiple of 4. better-sqlite3 BLOBs are returned as Node Buffers; whenever a Buffer is a view into a shared/pooled ArrayBuffer its byteOffset is arbitrary and frequently unaligned. The sibling scoring scripts that read the same target_vec/ctx_vec blobs deliberately avoid this by copying: score-effort-v1.mjs:84 and train-effort-v1.mjs:107 use buf.buffer.slice(buf.byteOffset, buf.byteOffset+buf.byteLength) which is always alignment-safe. This file (and novelty-sanity.mjs) diverge, so an unaligned blob buffer aborts the whole scoring run. Confidence is low because current better-sqlite3 builds tend to return freshly-allocated (offset 0) buffers, so it may not trigger in practice.
fix: Mirror the safe pattern used by score-effort-v1.mjs: const ab = buf.buffer.slice(buf.byteOffset, buf.byteOffset+buf.byteLength); return new Float32Array(ab); — or copy with Float32Array.from / Buffer copy before viewing.

title: Division-by-zero / crash on empty or single-week result set
detail: x0=Math.min(...xs), x1=Math.max(...xs) (line 35) and xPx divides by (x1 - x0) (line 39). If the query returns exactly one week with count>=50, x1===x0 and every xPx() is NaN, producing a blank/garbage chart. If the query returns zero rows, xs is empty so Math.min/Math.max return Infinity/-Infinity and line 123 rows[rows.length-1].resonance throws TypeError on undefined. The script then fails after the 'plotting 0 weeks' log instead of exiting cleanly.
fix: Guard early: if (rows.length === 0) { console.log('no data'); process.exit(0); } and handle x1===x0 (e.g. fall back to a 1px span or center the single point).

title: copyFileSync of a live WAL database can capture stale/torn data
detail: The script copies data/data.db with copyFileSync while (per the project) the production bot may hold it open in WAL mode. A raw file copy of only the main .db file does not include uncheckpointed pages in data.db-wal, so the snapshot can be missing recently-committed rows or, if a writer is mid-commit, internally inconsistent. The same applies to quality-snapshot-stage1.mjs:19. The header says LOCAL ONLY which mitigates this, but the count summaries printed at the end will then under-report and a downstream merge onto EC2 silently drops those rows.
fix: Before copying, open SRC and run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) (or use the better-sqlite3 db.backup() API / VACUUM INTO 'snapshot.db'), which produces a consistent point-in-time copy that includes WAL contents.

title: Same live-WAL copy risk as quality-snapshot.mjs
detail: unlinkSync(DST) then copyFileSync(SRC, DST) copies the live data.db without checkpointing its -wal sidecar. If the source DB is being written by the running bot, the stage-1 raw/ctx snapshot can omit recently committed messages or be torn. Cross-references the identical pattern in quality-snapshot.mjs:45-46.
fix: Checkpoint or use db.backup()/VACUUM INTO for a consistent snapshot rather than a raw filesystem copy of a WAL-mode database.

title: SQLite datetime strings parsed as local time, producing wrong relative timestamps and day counts
detail: art_job.assigned_at / completed_at are stored as SQLite TEXT via `datetime('now')` (confirmed in src/db/db.ts:353-355 and types.ts:36-39), which yields UTC strings of the form 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no timezone). art.ts feeds these directly into `new Date(job.assigned_at).getTime()` (and the same for completed_at) at lines 425, 635, 712, 732, 865, 1038. Per ECMAScript, a date-time string with a space separator and no offset is parsed in the host's LOCAL timezone by V8/Node, not UTC. So on any host not in UTC, every `<t:...:R>` 'Assigned X ago' value rendered by /art jobs, /art view, /art all, and /art getstatus is off by the server's UTC offset. Worse, in handleFinish (lines 635-637) `daysToComplete = Math.floor((Date.now() - assignedAt)/86400000)` can be off by a day, and for a job assigned minutes ago on a host with a positive UTC offset, `assignedAt` (parsed as local) can be GREATER than Date.now(), making the difference negative and rendering '... Completed in -1 days'. The repo already has the correct fix applied in src/ui/reviewCard.ts:110 and src/features/review/card.ts:129 (`trimmed.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'`), so this column format is known to need normalization before `new Date()`.
fix: Normalize the SQLite datetime string to ISO-UTC before constructing a Date, e.g. a helper `const ms = new Date(job.assigned_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z').getTime();` reused at every call site (mirroring reviewCard.ts:110). Also clamp daysToComplete with `Math.max(0, ...)` to avoid negative day counts from clock/parse skew.

title: Mutating staff subcommands never defer and await a network audit-log post before first ack, risking 10062
detail: Slash commands are dispatched by interactionCreate.ts:265 via `executor(interaction)` with NO auto-defer (wrapCommand only catches errors and posts an error card). handleAssign, handleCancel, and handleReassign never call deferReply(); they perform the DB write and then `await logActionPretty(...)` BEFORE the first interaction acknowledgement (handleCancel: audit_log at ~1136 precedes reply at ~1151; handleReassign: audit_log at ~1242 precedes reply at ~1259; handleAssign: audit_log at ~959 precedes reply at ~972). logActionPretty (src/logging/pretty.ts:464,517,635) calls getLoggingChannel(guild) and `channel.send({...})` — a network POST to Discord. If that post is slow (rate limit, transient latency), the total time from interaction receipt can exceed Discord's ~3s response window, so the subsequent interaction.reply() fails with 10062 (Unknown interaction). The DB mutation (cancel/reassign/create) has already committed, but the staff member sees 'This interaction failed' and wrapCommand then also tries (and fails) to post an error card. By contrast the read-only subcommands (handleJobs, handleAll, handleLeaderboard, handleGetStatus) all correctly deferReply() first.
fix: Call `await interaction.deferReply()` at the top of handleAssign/handleCancel/handleReassign (before the DB work / audit log), and replace the final `interaction.reply(...)` with `interaction.editReply(...)`. Alternatively, reorder so the user is acked first and the audit-log post is fire-and-forget after replying.

title: /backfill spawns a non-existent script — command is permanently broken
detail: execute() spawns `npx tsx scripts/backfill-message-activity.ts <guildId> <weeks> [--dry-run]`, but that file does not exist anywhere in the repo (verified via filesystem + grep; the only references to `backfill-message-activity` are this command, the legacy BACKFILL-NOW.sh, and docs). The real backfill entrypoint is `scripts/backfill/run.ts`, which has a completely different CLI (`--channels=...`, `--skip-reactions`, `--resume-only`) and takes no positional guildId/weeks args. As a result every /backfill invocation immediately fails: tsx exits non-zero with a module-not-found error, the `close` handler reports `❌ Backfill Failed` (or the `error` handler logs a spawn failure), and no data is ever backfilled. The heatmap that /backfill is meant to populate stays empty. Staff-facing command that can never succeed.
fix: Point spawn at the actual script and pass the arguments it expects, e.g. `spawn('npx', ['tsx', 'scripts/backfill/run.ts', ...])` adapted to run.ts's flag-based interface (it currently parses `--channels=` etc., not positional guildId/weeks). Either add a thin `scripts/backfill-message-activity.ts` shim that accepts `<guildId> <weeks>` and calls into the run.ts logic, or rewrite the command to invoke run.ts with the flags it supports. Also update BACKFILL-NOW.sh. Add a smoke test that asserts the spawned script path exists.

title: Backfill cooldown is consumed before validation and before the (failing) spawn, locking the guild out for 30 minutes
detail: checkCooldown('backfill', guildId, COOLDOWNS.BACKFILL_MS) records the cooldown timestamp as a side effect on the *allowed* path (see rateLimiter.ts:77 — it sets `now` whenever it returns allowed:true, even if the caller never proceeds). It is called before the weeks/date validation and before the child process is spawned. Combined with the broken-script bug above, a single attempt fails instantly yet still burns the full 30-minute BACKFILL_MS cooldown for the entire guild, so staff cannot retry for half an hour after every failed run. Even independent of the missing-script bug, if spawn errors or validation rejects the input, the cooldown has already been consumed.
fix: Move checkCooldown after input validation, and ideally only record the cooldown once the child process has actually been spawned successfully (e.g. inside backfillProcess.on('spawn'), or call clearCooldown('backfill', guildId) in the 'error' handler and on validation failure).

title: Resume path bypasses cooldown with no concurrency guard — concurrent resumes double-flag members and double-count stats
detail: runMembersAudit (and the parallel runNsfwAudit) are launched fire-and-forget from buttonRouter.handleAuditButton, which explicitly skips the per-guild cooldown for action === 'resume' (buttonRouter.ts:128). getActiveSession returns the same in_progress session for every clicker, and nothing marks the session as 'running' or takes a lock. If two staff click Resume on the same prompt (or the same user double-clicks before the message updates), two runners execute against the same sessionId concurrently. markUserScanned uses INSERT OR IGNORE so the scanned-set dedups, but both runners load `alreadyScanned` at start, so members not yet recorded get analyzed by BOTH runners: upsertManualFlag/upsertNsfwFlag fire twice, two flag embeds are sent to the channel, and updateProgress overwrites flagged_count from two racing counters (last-writer-wins, can under- or over-count). For NSFW this also doubles paid Google Vision API calls. Same shape in nsfw.ts:144-243.
fix: Add a lightweight in-process lock keyed by `${guildId}:${auditType}` (or sessionId) that rejects a second concurrent runner, and/or transition the session to a distinct 'running' status when a runner picks it up and refuse to resume a session already being processed. Re-applying the cooldown on resume (with clear-on-complete) would also prevent the double-click case.

title: channel cast to TextChannel can be null when the button's channel isn't cached, throwing inside the audit runner
detail: buttonRouter passes `channel as TextChannel` (buttonRouter.ts:187,206) where `channel` is `interaction.channel`, which discord.js types as nullable and can be null if the channel is uncached or inaccessible. members.ts then calls `channel.send(...)` (line 168, 249, 282) and nsfw.ts calls it at 238/318/352. If channel is null, the first `channel.send` throws a TypeError. It is caught by the runner's outer try/catch (and by the fire-and-forget .catch in buttonRouter), so it degrades to a logged failure rather than a crash, but the audit silently produces no output. The unchecked `as TextChannel` hides the nullable case.
fix: In buttonRouter, guard `if (!channel || !channel.isTextBased()) { reply error; return; }` before launching the runner, and narrow to a sendable channel type rather than casting. Alternatively have the runners accept `TextChannel | null` and bail early with a logged warning.

title: /gate reset wipes ALL guilds' data, not just the current guild
detail: In executeReset -> 'wipe_tables', the deletes are unscoped: runDelete("DELETE FROM application"), "DELETE FROM application_response", "DELETE FROM review_action", "DELETE FROM modmail_bridge", "DELETE FROM review_card", "DELETE FROM avatar_scan", "DELETE FROM review_claim" all run with no WHERE guild_id clause. These tables carry a guild_id column (confirmed in db schema / migrations / test fixtures: application.guild_id NOT NULL). The very next step, 'wipe_guild_question' (line 397-411), IS correctly scoped with "DELETE FROM guild_question WHERE guild_id = ?", and the confirmation modal customId is guild-scoped (v1:gate:reset:${guildId}). So the intent is clearly a per-guild reset, but the bulk deletes nuke every guild's applications/responses/actions/modmail bridges/claims that share this SQLite file. Any second guild (e.g. a staging/test guild, or future multi-tenant use) loses all of its gate data when a mod in one guild runs reset. The bot uses guild_id pervasively and supports per-guild config, so this is a genuine multi-guild data-loss bug; even in the current single-prod-guild deployment it is a latent footgun that diverges from the scoped questions wipe.
fix: Scope every delete by guild_id, mirroring the questions wipe. e.g. db.prepare('DELETE FROM application WHERE guild_id = ?').run(guildId); for review_action/modmail_bridge/review_card/avatar_scan/review_claim which key off app_id, delete via subquery: DELETE FROM review_action WHERE app_id IN (SELECT id FROM application WHERE guild_id = ?). Run application delete last (or capture app ids first) so the subqueries still resolve, all inside the existing transaction.

title: Health-check timeout timer is never cleared and not unref'd, keeping a 5s timer + closure alive after every /health
detail: timeoutPromise creates setTimeout(...HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS=5000) but the handle is never stored or cleared. In the normal fast path healthCheckPromise wins Promise.race, yet the 5s timer keeps running to completion on every single /health invocation, holding the reject closure (and the rejected Error it constructs) alive. Unlike armWatchdog in cmdWrap.ts (which calls timer.unref()), this timer is not unref'd, so it can also delay graceful process shutdown by up to 5s. It is not a correctness bug in the happy path (the late rejection is still consumed by Promise.race so no unhandled rejection), but it is an avoidable per-call resource/lifecycle leak in a command anyone can spam.
fix: Capture the handle and clear it in a finally: `let t: NodeJS.Timeout; const timeoutPromise = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => { t = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Health check timeout')), HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS); }); try { await Promise.race([...]); } finally { clearTimeout(t!); }` and/or call t.unref().

title: Timeout fallback calls interaction.reply() although the 5s timeout exceeds Discord's 3s ack window
detail: The happy path uses interaction.reply({embeds:[embed]}) (line 214). On timeout (5000ms) the catch handler also calls interaction.reply({content:'timed out...'}) (line 226). Because HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS (5000) is larger than Discord's ~3000ms initial-response window and the command never defers, by the time the timeout path fires the interaction token is already expired, so the fallback reply will essentially always fail with 10062 (it is .catch()-swallowed, so the user simply sees Discord's generic 'application did not respond'). If the underlying reply happened to succeed just as the timer fired there would also be a 40060 double-acknowledge, again swallowed. Net effect: the timeout branch is effectively dead/ineffective UX rather than a crash.
fix: Either lower the timeout below 3s and/or deferReply up front so a late edit can succeed, or drop the manual timeout race entirely and rely on the wrapCommand error handling. At minimum use replyOrEdit (which already handles deferred/replied/10062/40060) instead of a raw interaction.reply in both branches.

title: review_action meta 'via' mislabels the @user-mention path as 'code'
detail: updateReviewActionMeta is called with via: uidRaw ? "uid" : "code". There are three identifier inputs: app (short code), user (@mention), and uid. When a moderator approves via the `user` mention option, uidRaw is null so via is recorded as "code", even though no short code was used. This corrupts the analytics the comment at lines 329-330 explicitly says this field exists for ('track whether mods prefer short codes or user IDs'). Same pattern in reject.ts.
fix: Derive via from which option was actually provided, e.g. const via = codeRaw ? 'code' : userOption ? 'mention' : 'uid'; and pass that. Apply identically in reject.ts.

title: review_action meta 'via' mislabels the @user-mention path as 'code' (reject)
detail: Both updateReviewActionMeta calls in executeReject use via: uidRaw ? "uid" : "code". The `user` (@mention) lookup path leaves uidRaw null, so a mention-based rejection is logged as via='code'. Inaccurate audit/analytics metadata for how the action was initiated.
fix: Compute via from the actually-provided option: codeRaw ? 'code' : userOption ? 'mention' : 'uid', and use it in both the success and fetch-failure meta updates.

title: Welcome 'general channel not configured' note is never surfaced when a member was resolved but role failed
detail: In the dm_and_welcome step, the welcome branch runs only if (cfg && approvedMember && (cfg.accepted_role_id ? roleApplied : true)). If a role IS configured but role application failed (roleApplied=false), the whole if is skipped AND the else-if (!cfg?.general_channel_id) is also skipped (cfg truthy / general configured paths), so welcomeNote stays null. That part is by design (skip welcome when role failed). However the reply step (lines 340-361) already reports the role failure, so this is consistent. The real minor issue: when cfg exists and approvedMember exists and role applied but general_channel_id is unset, postWelcomeCard is attempted and only surfaces 'general channel not configured' through the thrown-error string match ('not configured') rather than the explicit else-if, making the user-facing message dependent on postWelcomeCard's exact error text. If that text ever changes, the note silently degrades to a raw error string. Low impact, but a brittle coupling worth tightening.
fix: Pre-check cfg.general_channel_id before attempting postWelcomeCard and emit the explicit 'general channel not configured' note, instead of relying on string-matching the thrown error message.

title: welcomebatch send: getConfig fetched after defer but flushSession deletes session before posting, leaving a window where a concurrent enqueue is silently dropped
detail: flushSession (features/welcomeBatch.ts:120-157) snapshots members, clearTimeout + sessions.delete BEFORE awaiting postBatchWelcomeCard. The in-memory session map has no locking. If an /accept enqueue (tryEnqueueWelcome) lands between the snapshot/delete and the network post completing, sessions.get returns undefined so the new member is posted as a SOLO welcome card (tryEnqueueWelcome returns false), splitting what the operator intended as one batch into batch+solo. This is inherent to the unguarded Map design rather than this file specifically, but /welcomebatch send is the trigger. Low severity (cosmetic split, no data loss) and process-local only.
fix: If strict batching matters, guard the session with an 'is flushing' flag so concurrent tryEnqueueWelcome either waits or is still buffered into the in-flight batch, or accept the documented best-effort behavior and note it in the command help.

title: Permission cache is never invalidated on role change (invalidatePermissionCache is dead-wired)
detail: filterCommandsByPermission caches the visible-command list under key `${guildId}:${userId}` with a 5-minute TTL (PERMISSION_CACHE, line 208). The only invalidation path is invalidatePermissionCache (line 325), but a repo-wide search shows it is never called from any production module (only its own file, tests, and graphify artifacts). Consequence: when a member's roles change (promotion to staff/reviewer, or demotion), their /help output stays stale for up to 5 minutes. This is not merely cosmetic: showCommandDetail (index.ts:220-235) reuses filterCommandsByPermission as an authorization gate and replies "You don't have permission to view /<cmd>" for any command not in the cached list. So a just-promoted staffer is falsely told they cannot view staff command help, and a just-demoted user can still read help for commands they lost — until the TTL expires. The code's own comment (lines 206-207) promises this invalidation happens; it does not.
fix: Call invalidatePermissionCache(guildId, userId) from the role-change paths (e.g., roleAutomation / guildMemberUpdate handlers), or key the cache on a hash of the member's role IDs so role changes naturally miss the cache. At minimum, shorten the TTL or expose a bulk clear hook that role-update events invoke.

title: Transient member-fetch failure poisons the permission cache with a public-only list
detail: All help entry points fetch the member with `members.fetch(userId).catch(() => null)` and tolerate null (autocomplete.ts:53, index.ts:90/319/397/461). When the fetch rejects (Discord API hiccup/rate limit — explicitly anticipated by the code comments), member is null and filterCommandsByPermission is called with member=null. hasPermissionLevel(line 213) then returns true only for `public` (and bot owner), so the result is the public-only command list — and that list is cached under `${guildId}:${userId}` for 5 minutes (line 283). Because autocomplete fires on every keystroke and is usually the first help interaction, a single failed fetch there poisons the shared module-level PERMISSION_CACHE, so the subsequent `/help` execute and the showCommandDetail permission gate (index.ts:220) both serve the stale public-only list, falsely hiding staff/reviewer/admin commands and denying their detail view for the whole TTL. Combined with the fact that invalidatePermissionCache is never wired up, nothing clears it early.
fix: Do not cache results computed from a null member (skip PERMISSION_CACHE.set when member is null), or treat a fetch failure as 'unknown' rather than 'public-only' and bypass the cache. Alternatively key the cache on resolved role IDs so a null-member computation can't masquerade as a real permission set.

title: Search-session storage is written every search but never read
detail: storeSearchSession (line 359) is called on every search (index.ts:267) and generateNonce (line 352) mints a nonce embedded into the select-menu custom ID (components.ts:260). However getSearchSession (line 373) is never called anywhere in production code (only in tests/graphify artifacts). The search select-menu handler (index.ts:403-413) ignores the nonce/session entirely and simply acts on interaction.values[0]. The entire SEARCH_SESSIONS LRUCache, the nonce generation, and storeSearchSession are therefore dead weight — allocating crypto randomBytes and cache entries on every search for data that is never consumed.
fix: Either remove SEARCH_SESSIONS/generateNonce/storeSearchSession/getSearchSession (and simplify buildSearchComponents to not need a nonce), or actually use getSearchSession in handleHelpSelectMenu to validate/restore the search context. Pick one; right now it's wasted work and misleading API surface.

title: Help component ownership guard is skipped when message.interaction is undefined
detail: handleHelpButton and handleHelpSelectMenu restrict interaction to the original invoker via `const originalUserId = interaction.message.interaction?.user.id; if (originalUserId && interaction.user.id !== originalUserId) { deny }`. Because the condition is gated on `originalUserId` being truthy, whenever message.interaction is absent (it is deprecated in discord.js v14 in favor of interactionMetadata, and is not populated in some contexts/after restarts), the guard is bypassed and ANY user can drive another user's help session (navigate categories, open the search modal, change views on someone else's ephemeral-less message). Impact is limited because /help is non-sensitive and each command-detail view is independently permission-filtered, but the intended owner-only restriction silently fails open.
fix: Use interaction.message.interactionMetadata?.user.id (with a fallback to the deprecated message.interaction) and treat an unresolved owner as deny-by-default for the navigation guard, or compare against a user id encoded into the custom ID at build time.

title: Permission-filtered command list is cached without keying on member-fetch success/roles, so a transient member fetch failure pins a user to 'public-only' help for up to 5 minutes
detail: filterCommandsByPermission caches the filtered result under key `${guildId}:${userId}` only. The actual permission computation depends on the `member` argument (its roles), which is NOT part of the cache key. In both callers (autocomplete.ts:50-60 and index.ts:88-94 / handleHelpButton index.ts:316-323 / handleHelpSelectMenu index.ts:394-401 / handleHelpModal index.ts:458-465) the GuildMember is fetched with `.catch(() => null)`. If that fetch transiently fails, `member` is null, and for any non-owner hasPermissionLevel() returns true only for 'public' commands. That degraded public-only list is then written to PERMISSION_CACHE (line 283). For the next 5 minutes (TTL) the same staff/reviewer/admin user is served the public-only list from cache even when subsequent fetches succeed, because the cache hit (line 267-273) short-circuits before member is consulted. Net effect: staff intermittently see /help and /help autocomplete with only public commands. Self-heals after TTL. Display-only (does not affect command execution, which is independently gated), hence low severity.
fix: Either (a) skip caching when `member` is null (the unreliable case), e.g. `if (member || isOwner(userId)) PERMISSION_CACHE.set(...)`, or (b) incorporate a role fingerprint into the cache key (e.g. a hash of sorted role IDs) so a different role set / null-member computes a distinct entry. Option (a) is the minimal fix.

title: invalidatePermissionCache is never called from production code, so the documented 'call this when roles change' contract is unmet and stale help lists persist for the full TTL
detail: invalidatePermissionCache() is exported and unit-tested, and the comment at cache.ts:206-207 explicitly states it must be called when a user's roles change to avoid serving a stale command list. A repo-wide search shows it is referenced only by its own definition/comment and the test file — never by any role-change path (no guildMemberUpdate handler, role automation, or config update calls it). Combined with the cache-key issue above, any role change (e.g., a user promoted to reviewer) is not reflected in /help for up to 5 minutes. Impact is limited to help-display accuracy, so low severity, but the function is effectively dead and the invariant it guards is not enforced.
fix: Call invalidatePermissionCache(guildId, userId) from the member/role update path (e.g., guildMemberUpdate when roles change) and from config changes that affect mod_role_ids/reviewer_role_id, or document that staleness up to CACHE_TTL_MS is accepted and remove the misleading 'call this' comment.

title: Help button/select 'only original user' guard relies on deprecated message.interaction, which is often undefined, silently disabling the check
detail: Both handleHelpButton (line 291) and handleHelpSelectMenu (line 378) gate interaction to the original user via `const originalUserId = interaction.message.interaction?.user.id;` then `if (originalUserId && interaction.user.id !== originalUserId)`. `Message#interaction` is deprecated in discord.js v14 (replaced by interactionMetadata) and is null/undefined for many messages (e.g., after restart or when Discord omits it). When originalUserId is undefined the whole guard is skipped, so any user can drive another user's help embed. This is NOT a privilege escalation because every downstream view re-derives the member and re-filters commands using the clicking user's own id (index.ts:312-313, 390-391, and filterCommandsByPermission), so a hijacker only ever sees commands they are themselves permitted to see; worst case is mild UX griefing (navigating someone else's ephemeral-less help message). Hence low severity, medium confidence on the trigger condition.
fix: Use interaction.message.interactionMetadata?.user?.id (with fallback to the deprecated field) for the owner check, and consider making the help reply ephemeral so cross-user interaction is impossible. At minimum, decide explicitly whether undefined originalUserId should allow or deny.

title: searchCommands scoring compares the full multi-word query against single command names, so every multi-term search collapses to the lowest 'description' score
detail: After AND-matching individual terms, the scoring block sets `queryLower = query.toLowerCase()` (the entire raw query, line 156) and compares it with `lowerName === queryLower`, `lowerName.startsWith(queryLower)`, `lowerName.includes(queryLower)`, alias includes, etc. For any multi-word query (e.g., 'role config'), no single command name/alias contains the full multi-word string, so all branches fail and every result is scored 50 / matchedOn='description' (lines 181-184). The subsequent sort (line 190-193) then degenerates to pure alphabetical order, defeating relevance ranking for multi-term searches. Single-word searches are unaffected. Impact is degraded result ordering only, not wrong results, so low severity.
fix: Score against individual terms rather than the whole query — e.g., compute the best per-term match (max over terms of name-exact/startsWith/includes) instead of using the full `query` string, or score using the first term and use the rest only for filtering.

title: handleHelpButton switch has no case for the 'search' navigation type and no button ever emits a search nonce id, leaving both the parse branch and a switch path dead
detail: parseHelpCustomId can return { type: 'search', nonce } for ids matching /^help:search:([a-f0-9]+)$/ (metadata.ts:257-264), but buildHelpCustomId({ type:'search' }) is never called anywhere in src (only the type union and the builder case exist). Search results are navigated via the select menu id `help:select:search:${nonce}` (components.ts:260), which is routed to handleHelpSelectMenu, not through a button. Consequently: (1) no button ever produces `help:search:<nonce>`, and (2) even if one did, handleHelpButton's switch (lines 326-343) has cases only for overview/category/command/search_modal, so 'search' would hit `default` and reply 'Unknown navigation'. This is dead/unreachable code rather than a live bug; flagged for cleanup and to document the gap should a future change start emitting search-nonce buttons.
fix: Either remove the unused 'search' member from HelpNavigation + its builder/parser branches, or add a `case 'search':` that loads the session via getSearchSession(nav.nonce) and re-renders results, if button-based search navigation is intended.

title: showSearchResults relies on '"update" in interaction' to branch, which is true for ALL ModalSubmitInteraction at runtime; it happens to be harmless only because the branch calls editReply, not update
detail: showSearchResults uses `if ("update" in interaction)` to distinguish component interactions, then casts to ModalSubmitInteraction and calls editReply. At runtime discord.js defines `update() {}` on ModalSubmitInteraction.prototype (node_modules/discord.js/src/structures/ModalSubmitInteraction.js:268, applied via InteractionResponses.applyToClass), so `"update" in interaction` is true for EVERY modal, not only message-sourced ones. The code is correct today purely by accident: the branch body calls editReply (valid after the deferUpdate() done in handleHelpModal:451), not update(). This is a fragile, misleading guard: anyone refactoring the branch to call interaction.update() (the natural reading of the condition) would crash on plain modals, and the unit test masks this because its mock omits an `update` property (tests/commands/help/index.test.ts:567-584), exercising a different branch than production. No current user-facing bug, hence low severity / medium confidence.
fix: Branch on a precise predicate instead of property presence: for the modal path call interaction.editReply directly (it is always deferred via deferUpdate), and for component vs chat-input use interaction.isMessageComponent()/instanceof checks rather than `"update" in interaction`.

title: verified_users row is inserted BEFORE the role grant; grant failure leaves a verified record with no role and the 'already verified' check then lies
detail: The flow inserts into verified_users first (lines 196-198), then attempts member.roles.add (lines 206-217) inside a try/catch that ONLY logs on failure (logger.error at 216) and continues. If the role add fails (missing Manage Roles permission, role above the bot in hierarchy, transient API error, member fetch failure), the user is permanently recorded as verified in the DB but never receives the Thin Line role. The log embed is still sent with 'Role Granted: Failed', but the user is told 'Thank you for your service. You have been given the Thin Line role.' (line 219) regardless. Worse, if they re-run /verify, the existence check at lines 69-81 finds the row and replies 'You're already verified ... You have the Thin Line role.' so they can never recover the role through the command. The write is non-idempotent w.r.t. the actual desired state (DB row + role).
fix: Grant the role first (and treat a failed grant as a hard failure that aborts before the INSERT), or wrap both in a compensating flow: if roles.add throws, do not insert (or delete the just-inserted row) and tell the user verification could not be completed. At minimum, make the success DM and embed conditional on roleGranted, and make the 'already verified' path re-attempt the role grant if the member lacks the role.

title: INSERT catch block treats ALL errors as 'duplicate verification' and silently aborts
detail: The try/catch around the INSERT (lines 195-203) assumes any thrown error means a UNIQUE-constraint duplicate and replies 'You're already verified!' then returns. But the same catch fires for unrelated failures: missing verified_users table (migration 064 not run), disk full / SQLITE_BUSY, corruption, etc. In those cases the user is falsely told they are already verified, no role is granted, and no log is written — a silent failure that masks the real DB error from operators (only logger.warn 'duplicate verification attempt' is emitted, with the actual err object buried). Genuine duplicates are also already prevented earlier by the existence check at line 61, so reaching this catch via a true duplicate requires the rare double-run race, making the misclassification of other errors the more likely real-world trigger.
fix: Inspect the error: only treat it as a duplicate when err.code === 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE' (or the message contains 'UNIQUE constraint failed'); otherwise log at error level and tell the user verification failed and to try again later. Re-throw or surface unexpected errors instead of swallowing them as 'already verified'.

title: Finalize button interaction is awaited but never acknowledged → user sees 'This interaction failed'
detail: The Finalize button press is captured via `await uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent(...)` (line 179) but the resolved component interaction is discarded — it is never acknowledged with update()/deferUpdate()/reply(). Discord requires every component interaction to be acknowledged within 3 seconds; otherwise the client shows a red 'This interaction failed' on the button. The verification still completes server-side (the message is edited at line 191 and the record is inserted), but the user who clicked Finalize is shown a failure state, which is confusing for an honor-system verification flow and will generate support noise. Contrast with line 154 where the select-menu interaction IS correctly acknowledged via categoryInteraction.update().
fix: Capture the interaction and acknowledge it, e.g. `const finalizeInteraction = await uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent({...}); await finalizeInteraction.deferUpdate();` (or .update({components: []})) before continuing.

title: Hardcoded cross-guild LOG_CHANNEL_ID silently disables the verification audit log in any other guild
detail: LOG_CHANNEL_ID is a hardcoded snowflake (line 26). The command is guild-scoped (setDMPermission(false)) and queries are keyed by guildId, but the audit log embed is always sent to this one fixed channel. guild.channels.fetch(LOG_CHANNEL_ID) (line 225) for a guild that does not contain that channel returns null (or throws, caught at 255), so the entire accountability log — the stated WHY of the feature ('Answers are logged for accountability') — is silently skipped while verification still succeeds and grants the role. The uploaded ID documents are then neither retained nor logged anywhere. Also note the documents themselves (potential government IDs/badges) are re-posted as embeds to a staff channel; that is by design but worth flagging as PII handling.
fix: Resolve the log channel from per-guild config (e.g. guild_config) instead of a hardcoded constant, and if the configured channel cannot be resolved, log a warning that is visible to operators rather than silently dropping the audit record.

title: Env SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS silently overrides an explicit per-guild DB value of exactly 7
detail: getFlaggerConfig uses silentDays === 7 as the sentinel for 'DB had no value' (lines 166-169). But 7 is also a valid, explicitly-settable per-guild value: setSilentFirstMsgDays accepts the range 7..365 (line 236) and 7 is the minimum allowed. If a guild deliberately sets silent_first_msg_days = 7 in guild_config and the SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS env var is set to a different number (e.g. 30), the DB read sets silentDays = 7 (line 140-142), then line 166 sees silentDays === 7 and overwrites it with the env value (30). The guild's explicit choice is silently discarded, changing flagging behavior. The code comment itself flags this fragility ('this logic assumes 7 is the default').
fix: Track whether the DB actually supplied a value using a real sentinel instead of the magic number. e.g. let dbDays: number | null = null; set it from row.silent_first_msg_days when non-null; apply the env fallback only when dbDays === null; finally silentDays = dbDays ?? envDays ?? 7.

title: db.transaction monkeypatch drops the .deferred/.immediate/.exclusive variants of the returned transaction function
detail: better-sqlite3's transaction(fn) returns a callable that also carries .deferred, .immediate, .exclusive (and .default) sub-functions for choosing the BEGIN mode. The wrapper at lines 97-111 returns a brand-new closure ('wrapped') that only proxies the default call path; the variant properties are not copied over. Any caller doing db.transaction(fn).immediate(...) would get 'undefined is not a function'. No current caller in src uses these variants (verified by grep), so this is latent rather than live, but it is a silent capability regression that future code could hit unexpectedly.
fix: After building 'wrapped', re-attach the variants, e.g. (wrapped as any).deferred = originalTransaction wrapped equivalents, or more simply copy them: for (const k of ['deferred','immediate','exclusive','default']) (wrapped as any)[k] = (originalReturn as any)[k]; — or wrap each variant with the same timing logic.

title: /stats history export produces a download link to a non-existent /exports/ route (always 404)
detail: When export:true is passed, the handler writes the CSV to data/exports/<file>.csv and then surfaces a link `${process.env.PUBLIC_URL || "https://pawtropolis.tech"}/exports/<filename>` to the moderator, labeled "Download CSV ... Link expires in 24 hours". I grepped the bot's web bootstrap (src/startup/web.ts, src/web/dashboardApi.ts) and the entire SvelteKit route tree (web/src/routes). There is no route, static handler, or @fastify/static mount that serves `/exports/...`. The only export endpoint is web/src/routes/api/export/+server.ts, which generates its CSV inline from action_log and never reads data/exports. So every link rendered by this feature resolves to a 404 — the export is effectively unusable; the file is written to disk but can never be downloaded.
fix: Either (a) attach the generated CSV directly to the editReply via AttachmentBuilder (as /stats export in export.ts already does) instead of writing to disk and linking, or (b) add a real authenticated `/exports/:filename` route that serves files from data/exports with path-traversal protection. Option (a) is simpler and removes the disk dependency entirely.

title: Exported CSVs accumulate forever in data/exports despite "expires in 24 hours" claim
detail: Each export writes a uniquely-named file (stats-history-<modId>-<ts>-<rand>.csv, up to MAX_EXPORT_ROWS=50000 rows) into data/exports via writeFileSync, but nothing ever deletes them. I searched the whole repo (schedulers, startup tasks, scripts) for any cleanup of data/exports or any honoring of the advertised 24h expiry — there is none. The embed text "Link expires in 24 hours" is therefore false, and the directory grows unboundedly on every invocation. On the 2GB-RAM / constrained-disk host described in src/db/db.ts, repeated large exports can fill the volume. Combined with finding above, these files are also never even served, so they are pure dead weight.
fix: Stop persisting to disk and attach the buffer to the reply (preferred). If on-disk staging is required, add a scheduler that prunes data/exports files older than 24h (matching the promise), or write to an OS temp dir and unlink after streaming.

title: Username fallback search checks 25 arbitrary applicants, not applicants matching the query
detail: When the query is not a snowflake and no guild member matches, the fallback runs `SELECT DISTINCT a.user_id FROM application WHERE guild_id = ? LIMIT 25` — there is no ORDER BY and no filter tied to trimmedQuery. It then fetches those 25 arbitrary user_ids from Discord and substring-matches their username/tag against the query. For any guild with more than 25 distinct applicants (the normal case), a legitimate user who applied and left is very likely NOT among the 25 rows SQLite happens to return, so the command reports `No user found matching "<q>". Try searching by user ID instead.` even though the user's applications exist in the DB. The inline comment frames the LIMIT 25 as DoS protection, masking that it also silently caps correctness. Impact: moderators get false negatives when searching departed users by name; the feature appears broken for its stated purpose ("handles users who applied and then left").
fix: Persist a username/tag at application time (e.g., a denormalized column or user_cache) and filter the SQL with a LIKE on that column so the 25 candidates are actually relevant, or raise/remove the cap and rely solely on the existing 50ms-per-call rate limiting. At minimum, when candidateUserIds.length === 25 and no match is found, tell the user the search was truncated rather than implying no records exist.

title: SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS env var silently overrides a guild's explicit DB value of 7
detail: getFlaggerConfig initializes silentDays=7, then reads the DB row. If the DB has a non-null silent_first_msg_days it is assigned to silentDays (lines 140-142). The env fallback at line 166 only fires when `silentDays === 7`. The problem: 7 is a VALID, user-settable value (setSilentFirstMsgDays accepts days>=7, line 236). So a guild that deliberately ran `/config set flags.silent_days 7` stores 7 in the DB, but on read the code cannot distinguish "DB said 7" from "DB had no row / null", and therefore overwrites the guild's explicit 7 with the env default (e.g. SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS=60). This violates the documented resolution priority (DB > ENV, lines 102-106) for exactly the value 7. Impact: a guild that intentionally set the most-aggressive 7-day threshold gets a different (env) threshold applied to first-message flagging, changing who gets flagged. The in-code comment even acknowledges the brittleness ('GOTCHA: This logic assumes 7 is the default').
fix: Track whether the DB actually supplied a value instead of overloading the sentinel 7. e.g. `let dbProvidedDays = false;` set true inside the `row.silent_first_msg_days !== null` branch, then gate the env fallback on `!dbProvidedDays` instead of `silentDays === 7`.

title: DB row inserted before role grant; if role grant fails the user is permanently locked out and falsely told they have the role
detail: The INSERT into verified_users (line 196-198) commits BEFORE the role is added (lines 206-217). If `member.roles.add(VERIFIED_ROLE_ID)` throws (missing Manage Roles perm, role above bot in hierarchy, transient API error), the error is caught and only logged (line 215-216); roleGranted stays false but the DB row already exists. On any subsequent `/verify`, the existing-row check (line 69) short-circuits and tells the user 'You have the Thin Line role' (line 78) — which is false — and never retries the role grant. Result: a user whose role-add failed can never obtain the Thin Line role through this command. The log embed even records 'Role Granted: Failed' (line 233), confirming the path is expected to occur.
fix: Either (a) grant the role first and only INSERT after a confirmed grant, or (b) in the existing-row branch, re-check member.roles.cache.has(VERIFIED_ROLE_ID) and re-attempt the grant if the role is missing rather than asserting the user already has it.

title: Any gatekeeper can flush/close a batch session owned by a different gatekeeper via the send branch
detail: The toggle 'send and close' branch is entered solely when isMemberBuffered(guild.id, target.id) is true (line 118), with no check that the current user opened the session. addMember (the add branch) explicitly guards against cross-opener interference and returns 'denied_other_opener' (welcomeBatch.ts line 204-205), but flushSession has no such owner check. So if gatekeeper A opens a batch and queues user X, gatekeeper B right-clicking the buffered user X will flush and close A's in-progress session prematurely. This is an asymmetric authorization inconsistency: B is blocked from adding to A's session but allowed to send/close it. Impact is limited because all actors are trusted gatekeepers, but it can cause A's batch to be sent before A finished queueing.
fix: In the isMemberBuffered branch, fetch the session opener (getSessionStatus(guild.id).openedBy) and if it differs from interaction.user.id (and the user is not a bypass/owner), reply that another gatekeeper owns the session instead of flushing it.

title: Finalize button interaction is never acknowledged → user sees "This interaction failed"
detail: The select-menu step correctly acknowledges its component interaction via categoryInteraction.update(...) (line 154). The Finalize step, however, only awaits the button via uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent({...}) (lines 179-183) and discards the resulting ButtonInteraction without ever calling .update(), .reply(), or .deferUpdate(). discord.js collectors/awaitMessageComponent do NOT auto-acknowledge. Discord requires a component interaction to be acknowledged within 3 seconds; otherwise the clicking user is shown "This interaction failed". So every successful verification finalization shows the user an error toast even though the backend proceeds to insert the record, grant the role, and DM them. This is confusing and looks broken to end users in the exact honor-system flow the feature is built around.
fix: Capture the interaction and acknowledge it, e.g. `const finalizeInteraction = await uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent({...}); await finalizeInteraction.deferUpdate();` (or .update({ components: [] })), then proceed. Mirror the pattern already used for categoryInteraction.update() on line 154.

title: User-uploaded identity documents (badges/IDs) are posted to a hardcoded channel and retained indefinitely
detail: The flow invites users to upload verification documents such as badges and IDs (lines 141-145). Every uploaded image URL is then re-posted into a channel identified by a hardcoded snowflake LOG_CHANNEL_ID = "1430015254053654599" (line 26) as embed images (lines 240-253). Although the prompt asks users to redact PII, this is an honor-system flow and many users will upload un-redacted government-issued IDs / first-responder credentials. The consequences: (1) sensitive PII is durably stored in a Discord channel with whatever broad staff access that channel has, beyond the stated "internal records" need and with no retention/deletion; (2) the channel ID is hardcoded rather than configurable, so if the channel is deleted/changed the documents silently fail to log (caught only by a warn) or, worse, a reused ID could route PII to the wrong channel. The attachment.url values are also CDN links that remain accessible.
fix: Make the log channel configurable per-guild (e.g. via guild_config) instead of a hardcoded ID, restrict it to a least-privilege staff channel, and avoid persisting raw ID images — store only a boolean "documents provided" or a short-lived reference, and document a deletion policy. At minimum, do not echo the uploaded image URLs into a long-lived channel.

title: Env fallback overrides a guild's explicitly-configured silent_first_msg_days when the configured value equals the default (7)
detail: getFlaggerConfig uses `silentDays === 7` as a sentinel meaning "DB had no value" (lines 166-169). But 7 is also a fully valid value a guild can persist: setSilentFirstMsgDays accepts the range 7-365 (line 236), so a guild can explicitly set 7. When such a guild exists AND process.env.SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS is set to a different number (e.g. 30), the DB-provided 7 is silently clobbered by the env value, ignoring the guild's explicit configuration. The comment on lines 162-163 even acknowledges the fragility. Trigger is narrow (guild explicitly set the boundary value 7 while a differing env default is present), hence low severity, but the resolution logic is genuinely incorrect.
fix: Track whether the DB actually supplied a value with a separate boolean (e.g. `let dbHadDays = false;` set inside the `row.silent_first_msg_days !== null` branch) and only apply the env fallback when `!dbHadDays`, instead of overloading the magic number 7.

title: avatar_scan.reason column default differs between fresh-create and ALTER paths
detail: When ensureAvatarScanSchema creates the table fresh, `reason TEXT` is declared with no default (line 51). When the column is instead added to a legacy table via ALTER, it is added as `reason TEXT DEFAULT 'none'` (line 121). The same column therefore has different default semantics depending on whether the DB was created fresh or migrated: fresh DBs default reason to NULL, migrated DBs default to the string 'none'. Code that branches on reason === 'none' vs reason == null (e.g. avatarScan upsert logic and scan.ts which inserts reason='none' explicitly) can behave inconsistently across environments. Low impact because most writers set reason explicitly, but it is a latent data-integrity inconsistency.
fix: Make the two paths agree — either give the CREATE TABLE column `DEFAULT 'none'` (line 51) or drop the default on the ALTER (line 121) — and normalize existing NULLs if 'none' is the intended canonical value.

title: avatar_scan.final_pct declared NOT NULL via ALTER but nullable in the canonical CREATE/ALTER in ensure.ts
detail: db.ts adds final_pct as `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` at module load (line 248), while ensure.ts both creates it (line 48) and ALTERs it (line 105) as `INTEGER DEFAULT 0` (nullable). Because the avatar_scan table is normally created later by ensureAvatarScanSchema() during ClientReady (startup/schema.ts:51) and db.ts runs first at import time, the db.ts ALTER usually no-ops with "no_table" and the nullable definition wins. But on any DB where avatar_scan already exists at import time, final_pct becomes NOT NULL, diverging from the canonical schema. This nullability divergence across environments can surprise writers that rely on inserting NULL or omitting the column. Same-column-different-constraint is a schema-consistency hazard even though current writers default it to 0.
