fix: Standardize the final_pct definition across db.ts and ensure.ts (pick one: nullable DEFAULT 0 to match ensure.ts, or NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 everywhere) so the resulting schema is identical regardless of creation order. Ideally remove the duplicate add in db.ts and let ensure.ts own avatar_scan.

title: Game-night and movie-night attendance overwrite each other (UNIQUE constraint missing event_type)
detail: finalizeGameAttendance writes to movie_attendance with `INSERT OR REPLACE ... VALUES (..., 'game', ...)` keyed implicitly on the table's UNIQUE constraint. That constraint is `UNIQUE(guild_id, user_id, event_date)` (migrations/025_role_automation.ts:111) and migration 040 (which added the event_type column) only ALTERs in the column + a NON-unique index `idx_movie_attendance_event_type`; it never rebuilds the unique key to include event_type. event_date is a date-only string `YYYY-MM-DD` (src/commands/event/game.ts:92, src/commands/event/movie.ts:88). Movie night finalize uses the same table with the same date (src/features/movieNight.ts:292-295). Therefore, if a user attends both a movie night and a game night on the same calendar day, whichever event is finalized second silently REPLACES the other event's row, destroying the first event's attendance/qualification record and corrupting tier counts (getUserQualifiedGameCount / getUserTotalEventCount). The same applies to creditHistoricalGameAttendance (lines 744-757) and bumpGameAttendance (lines 816-829) whose `ON CONFLICT(guild_id, user_id, event_date)` cannot even reference event_type because it is not a unique key — at runtime this ON CONFLICT clause resolves against the (guild_id,user_id,event_date) unique index and will collide with a movie record of the same day.
fix: Add event_type to the uniqueness key: create a migration that rebuilds movie_attendance with `UNIQUE(guild_id, user_id, event_date, event_type)` (SQLite requires create-new-table + copy + drop + rename), or add a separate `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON movie_attendance(guild_id,user_id,event_date,event_type)` after dropping the old unique index, then update all INSERT OR REPLACE / ON CONFLICT targets accordingly.

title: PM2 self-stop kills the process mid-restore, so file replacement/verify/restart never run
detail: restoreCandidate with pm2Coord=true runs `await execAsync('pm2 stop ' + processName)` (line 506) BEFORE replacing the DB file (line 544) and before restarting PM2 (line 620). The live restore button (src/features/dbRecoveryButtons.ts:193-199) invokes this path with pm2Coord:true and the bot itself is the PM2-managed process (env.PM2_PROCESS_NAME). When PM2 stops that very process, the running Node event loop is terminated, so the awaited execAsync never resolves and steps 4–6 (copyFile of the candidate over the live DB, post-restore verification, `pm2 start`) never execute. Result: the database is NOT restored, PM2 may leave the app stopped, and the Discord reply promising success is never sent. The pre-restore backup is created (step 2) but the actual restore silently no-ops.
fix: Do not stop the running bot from within itself. Either (a) perform the copy + integrity verify FIRST while running, then schedule a detached `pm2 restart` (spawned with detached:true / unref) as the final step, or (b) move restore into an out-of-process CLI/worker (src/ops/dbRecoverCli.ts) that PM2 does not manage, or (c) use better-sqlite3's online backup API to replace data without stopping the process.

title: listCandidates maps foreign_key_violations from the row_count column
detail: When building a BackupCandidate from persisted metadata, `foreign_key_violations: existingMeta?.row_count` reads the wrong column (row_count) — a copy-paste error. The db_backups table (migrations/012:52-62) has no foreign-key-violation column at all, and validateCandidate persists only row_count (the summed row total). Consequently any UI/embed that shows cached FK violations for a not-yet-revalidated candidate will display the total row count as the FK-violation count, which is misleading (e.g., a healthy backup appears to have thousands of FK violations).
fix: Set `foreign_key_violations: undefined` here (it is not persisted), or add a dedicated `foreign_key_violations` column to db_backups and persist/read it. Do not alias it to row_count.

title: Banner sync error logs the full guild banner CDN URL (low-value info leak / log noise)
detail: Not a real secret leak — guild banner URLs are public CDN links. Noted only for completeness: the module logs banner URLs at info level on every sync. No PII or credential exposure. No action strictly required.
fix: Optional: drop guildBannerURL from the info log to reduce noise. Not a security defect.

title: 7-day reopen window miscomputed due to UTC-vs-local Date parsing of closed_at
detail: closeTicket() (src/features/modmail/tickets.ts:165) writes closed_at via SQLite datetime('now'), which produces a space-separated UTC string with NO timezone marker, e.g. "2026-05-31 12:00:00". At threadReopen.ts:73 this is parsed with `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. Per ECMAScript, a date-time string that uses a space separator and omits a timezone offset is treated as LOCAL time by V8/Node, not UTC. So the computed `closedAt` epoch is shifted by the host's UTC offset (e.g. +7h on a UTC-7 server, making the ticket look ~7h newer; -offset on UTC+ servers, making it look older). The `now - closedAt > sevenDays` boundary at line 77 is therefore wrong by the server's UTC offset, so tickets near the 7-day edge are routed down the wrong branch: some get a brand-new thread when they should reopen the old one, and others reopen an old (possibly already-archived/locked) thread when they should start fresh. The unit tests in tests/features/modmail/threadReopen.test.ts pass only because they feed closed_at via Date.toISOString() (with a 'Z'), which IS parsed as UTC — masking the production format mismatch. The same bug exists in src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304 (dashboardReopenThread) and the modstats calc in context/06 docs, so behavior is inconsistent across entry points.
fix: Parse the stored value as UTC explicitly. Either store an epoch (strftime('%s','now')) and read it as a number, or normalize before parsing: replace the space with 'T' and append 'Z' (e.g. `new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z')`), or route through the existing normalizeTimestamp helper used in web/src/lib/server/queries/modmail.ts. Apply the same fix in dashboardBridge.ts:304 and update the tests to use the SQLite datetime format ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') so they actually exercise the production path.

title: reopenTicket can violate the partial-unique open-ticket index, surfacing as a generic failure
detail: reopenTicket() (tickets.ts:174-180) runs `UPDATE modmail_ticket SET status='open' WHERE id=?`. The schema (src/db/db.ts:193-199) enforces `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id,user_id,status) WHERE status='open'` — at most one open ticket per (guild,user). A realistic sequence: close ticket A for a user, later open a fresh ticket B for the same user (now the user's single allowed open row), then a mod runs /modmail reopen on ticket A (or clicks reopen for the most-recent-closed). The UPDATE flips A back to status='open' while B is still open, violating the partial unique index and throwing SQLITE_CONSTRAINT inside the db.transaction at threadReopen.ts:89. The whole reopen is rolled back and the user gets the opaque message "Failed to reopen modmail thread. Check logs." with no indication that a newer ticket already exists. The DB stays consistent (transaction rolls back) so this is a UX/robustness defect rather than corruption.
fix: Before reopening, check for an existing open ticket for the same (guild_id,user_id) via getOpenTicketByUser and, if present, return a clear message (e.g. "This user already has an open modmail: <#threadId>") instead of attempting the constraint-violating UPDATE. Alternatively, atomically close any other open ticket for that user as part of the reopen transaction.

title: Open flow guards only on open_modmail but createTicket can still hit the modmail_ticket open-unique index
detail: The race guard checks/locks the open_modmail table (threadOpen.ts:231-255), but createTicket() inserts into modmail_ticket, which has its own partial unique index idx_modmail_open_unique on (guild_id,user_id,status) WHERE status='open' (db.ts:193-199). These two tables can legitimately diverge: e.g. a prior close that cleaned up open_modmail (cleanupOpenModmail / the DELETE FROM open_modmail) but where closeTicket failed to commit, or a manual/guard-row deletion. In that state open_modmail reports "no open ticket" so the guard passes, but the lingering open row in modmail_ticket makes the createTicket INSERT throw SQLITE_CONSTRAINT. The outer catch (lines 444-448) matches SQLITE_CONSTRAINT and treats it as a race, but the subsequent lookup at line 452 finds no open_modmail row, so it falls through to the generic "Failed to create modmail thread" path and the pending-row cleanup — confusing the operator even though no duplicate was actually created.
fix: Make the two sources of truth agree: either gate creation on getOpenTicketByUser (modmail_ticket) in addition to the open_modmail guard, or, in the SQLITE_CONSTRAINT branch, also look up the existing OPEN modmail_ticket (not just open_modmail) and surface its thread link so the message is accurate.

title: 7-day reopen window mis-computed due to local-time parsing of UTC SQLite timestamp
detail: `ticket.closed_at` is stored by closeTicket() (src/features/modmail/tickets.ts:165) as SQLite `datetime('now')`, i.e. a UTC string of the form "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" with no timezone marker (confirmed by schema src/db/db.ts:186-187: `closed_at TEXT`). Line 73 does `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. V8 parses the space-separated, marker-less format as LOCAL time, not UTC. Verified empirically: on a UTC-5 host, `new Date('2026-05-31 12:00:00').toISOString()` === '2026-05-31T17:00:00Z' — a 5-hour error equal to the host's UTC offset. Effect: `now - closedAt` is off by the host offset, so the `> sevenDays` boundary at line 77 is wrong by that offset. On a host behind UTC the reopen window is effectively lengthened; on a host ahead of UTC it is shortened, so a ticket closed ~6d 16h ago (with a +9h offset) can be wrongly treated as >7 days and routed to create a brand-new thread (line 79) instead of reopening. The bot is not guaranteed to run in UTC, so this changes user-visible behavior at the boundary.
fix: Parse as UTC. Either append 'Z'/replace space with 'T'+'Z' (`new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ','T')+'Z')`), or better, store/compare epoch seconds consistently (e.g. compare via SQLite `strftime('%s',closed_at)` or use the project's nowUtc/time helpers). Apply the same parsing fix anywhere closed_at/created_at TEXT columns are turned into Date().

title: closeModmailThread archives the thread, then immediately tries to delete the same thread (redundant/likely-failing second op)
detail: In closeModmailThread the thread is fetched and explicitly archived+locked at lines 266-268 (`setLocked(true)` then `setArchived(true)`), and `threadForCleanup` is set to that thread. Later (lines 363-394), if `modmail_delete_on_close` is not false (default true), it calls `threadForCleanup.delete(...)`. Archiving first is wasted work when the configured behavior is delete, and on an already-archived thread the subsequent edit/delete round-trip is more failure-prone; if delete then fails the thread is left archived/locked but the bot is NOT removed (the catch at 388 only logs). This is inconsistent with closeModmailForApplication (the other close path), which does NOT pre-archive and instead routes through archiveOrDeleteThread() with proper permission pre-checks and bot-removal fallback. Net impact is minor (extra API calls, occasional thread left visible) rather than data loss, because DB state is already committed at 232-249.
fix: Mirror the auto-close path: skip the unconditional setArchived/setLocked at 266-268 when delete-on-close is enabled, or refactor closeModmailThread to also use archiveOrDeleteThread() so archive is only used as a fallback and the bot is removed if delete fails.

title: Reopen can violate the partial-unique open-ticket index if the user already has another open ticket
detail: When called with `userId`, reopen selects the most recent CLOSED ticket (lines 44-57) and only checks that THAT ticket is not already open (line 68). It then calls reopenTicket() inside the transaction (line 90), which sets status='open'. The schema enforces `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id,user_id,status) WHERE status='open'` (src/db/db.ts:195-199). If the same user simultaneously has a different open ticket (possible if a prior close only updated the guard table, or via manual DB edits / races), the UPDATE to 'open' throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT and the whole reopen fails with the generic "Failed to reopen" message (caught at 150). Low confidence because the normal open-path guard usually prevents a user from having both an open and a reopenable closed ticket simultaneously.
fix: Before reopenTicket(), check for an existing open ticket for (guild_id,user_id) and either reuse/return it or close it first; alternatively catch the constraint error specifically and return a clear message pointing at the existing open thread.

title: ensureGateEntry calls .has() on fetchPins().items which is a plain Array, throwing TypeError after a successful pin
detail: In discord.js 14.26.4 (the pinned version, ^14.26.4), MessageManager.fetchPins() returns `{ hasMore: boolean, items: readonly MessagePin[] }` where `items` is a plain readonly Array (typings/index.d.ts lines 6581-6590). The pin-verification block casts `items` to `{ has: (id) => boolean }` and calls `pinnedItems.has(message.id)`. Arrays have `includes`, not `has`, so `pinnedItems.has` is undefined and the call throws `TypeError: pinnedItems.has is not a function`. This runs INSIDE the try at line 596 AFTER message.pin() has already succeeded; the catch at 615 logs and then re-throws (line 623). ensureGateEntry is awaited inside withStep('ensure_entry', ...) in src/commands/gate/gateMain.ts:214, and withStep propagates (cmdWrap.ts:392, 'caught by wrapCommand upstream'). Net effect: every /gate setup (and /update re-ensure at update.ts:427) that successfully pins the panel still surfaces an error card to the staff user, even though the panel was created and pinned correctly. Note the SAME file's findExistingGateEntry (lines 160-167) correctly treats items as an array of {message}, proving the intended shape.
fix: Replace the Collection-style `.has()` access with array semantics consistent with the rest of the file: `const pinnedItems = (pinnedResponse as { items?: ReadonlyArray<{ message?: Message }> }).items; const pinnedMatch = Array.isArray(pinnedItems) ? pinnedItems.some((it) => it?.message?.id === message.id) : false;`. Then the success path returns result without throwing.

title: ensureGateEntryStartup iterates pinned MessagePin objects as if they were Message objects, so pinned gate panels are never detected
detail: fetchPins().items is `readonly MessagePin[]` where MessagePin = { message, pinnedAt, pinnedTimestamp } (typings 6586-6590). The startup code does `const pinnedCollection = (pinned as { items?: { values: () => Iterable<Message> } }).items;` then `for (const m of pinnedCollection.values()) candidates.set(m.id, m);`. Array.prototype.values() yields the elements, which are MessagePin objects, NOT Message objects. So `m.id` is undefined (every pinned entry is keyed under the same `undefined` slot in the candidates Map) and `m` has no `.components`/`.embeds`. The later guard `if (!Array.isArray(m.components) || !Array.isArray(m.embeds)) continue;` (line 263) is therefore always true for these entries, so the pinned branch contributes nothing. Impact: the startup foreign-bot-panel cleanup and current-bot pinned-panel reuse never see pinned messages; after a bot-identity swap an old foreign pinned panel can be missed, and a current pinned panel may be re-posted instead of edited. The recent-50 fetch at line 256 partially masks this (the panel is usually also in recent history), so it limps along rather than fully failing.
fix: Iterate items as a plain array of MessagePin and use the inner message: `const items = (pinned as { items?: ReadonlyArray<{ message?: Message }> }).items; if (Array.isArray(items)) { for (const it of items) { const m = it?.message; if (m) candidates.set(m.id, m); } }` — matching findExistingGateEntry in the same file.

title: DM verification sessions are looked up by userId only, ignoring guildId, so a user in two bot guilds gets cross-guild misrouting
detail: Sessions are stored keyed by `${guildId}:${userId}` (sessionKey, line 83-85; activeSessions.set at 326) but hasActiveSession(userId) (87-92) and getSessionForUser(userId) (94-99) scan only by session.userId and return the FIRST match. messageCreate.ts:154-156 and interactionCreate.ts routing call these with only the author/user id. The bot is explicitly multi-guild (startup/ready.ts and several schedulers loop over client.guilds.cache). Consequences for a user who is in two guilds where the bot lives: (a) startDmVerification's duplicate guard at line 191 keys by guild+user, so it WILL create a second session for guild B while guild A's session exists, but getSessionForUser then returns whichever was inserted first — a DM answer intended for guild B can be persisted against guild A's appId via upsertAnswer (handleDmAnswer line 380), and the Submit button resolves to the wrong guild's application; (b) only one of the two verifications is reachable via DM at a time. This is data-integrity-relevant (answers written to the wrong application) though it requires the dual-guild precondition.
fix: Key all session operations by guild+user. Either thread guildId through the message/button routing (parse it from the active session's stored thread/guild, or include it in the button customId which already carries a nonce) and look up via activeSessions.get(sessionKey(guildId,userId)), or at minimum disallow more than one active session per user globally and tie the DM answer to the single session deterministically. The nonce on the buttons already scopes button actions, but text-answer routing (handleDmAnswer) has no guild scoping at all.

title: Thread-based verification session sends follow-up questions to message.channel, ignoring the session's targetChannelId
detail: A session may run inside a per-user verify thread (targetChannelId set, lines 64, 324). handleDmAnswer routes purely off message.channel (line 410 `message.channel.send(...)`). messageCreate.ts only invokes handleDmAnswer for a thread message when getVerifyThreadByThreadId matches AND author matches (lines 132-140), and separately for DM messages (152-157). If a user with an active THREAD session instead types in their DM with the bot (e.g. they had a prior DM context, or the bot DMed them elsewhere), getSessionForUser still returns the thread session and the next question/summary is sent to the DM channel, splitting the flow across two channels. Conversely there is no assertion that message.channel.id === session.targetChannelId. Lower severity because the documented happy path keeps the user in one place, but the missing channel check means answers can be accepted from, and questions delivered to, a channel other than the one the session belongs to.
fix: In handleDmAnswer, if session.targetChannelId is set, verify message.channel.id === session.targetChannelId before accepting the answer (ignore or gently redirect otherwise), and send follow-up questions to the resolved target channel rather than blindly to message.channel.

title: Non-null assertion on a possibly-undefined Guild passed to logActionPretty (guild!) drops the audit-log entry when the guild is uncached
detail: guild is obtained via interaction.client.guilds.cache.get(session.guildId) (line 534), typed Guild | undefined, and the `if (guild)` block (535-538) explicitly handles the undefined case for member fetch. But at line 565 logActionPretty(guild!, ...) uses a non-null assertion. logActionPretty immediately dereferences guild.id synchronously (src/logging/pretty.ts:488) with no undefined guard. If the guild is not in cache at submit time (sharding eviction, large-guild lazy cache), guild is undefined and logActionPretty rejects with TypeError. It is an async function so the throw becomes a rejected promise caught by the `.catch()` at line 571 — so no crash, but the gate_submit audit-log row is silently never written and only a warn is logged. The `!` hides a genuinely possible undefined.
fix: Guard before logging: `if (guild) { await logActionPretty(guild, {...}).catch(...); }` (you already fetched/checked guild above), or change logActionPretty to accept Guild | undefined and no-op when absent. Do not use `!` here.

title: Zero-duration or 0% threshold qualifies everyone (requiredMinutes 0, 0 >= 0 true), including users with no attendance
detail: eventDurationMinutes = floor((end-start)/60000). requiredMinutes = ceil(eventDurationMinutes * pct/100). qualified = userMinutes >= requiredMinutes. If an event is ended almost immediately (end ~ start, duration 0) or qualificationPercentage is 0, requiredMinutes becomes 0 and the check 0 >= 0 marks EVERY tracked user as qualified — including users with userMinutes 0. The caller in gameNight.ts:270-287 writes qualified=1 to the attendance row and grants based on it, so a mis-ended or zero-duration game night would hand out qualification to everyone present (or even to zero-minute sessions). Also note attendancePercentage caps nowhere: a user with more recorded minutes than the (rounded-down) event duration can show >100%. Low severity because normal events have positive duration and threshold defaults to 50, but the boundary is unguarded.
fix: Treat non-positive eventDurationMinutes as non-qualifying (return qualified=false / require an explicit minimum), and require userMinutes > 0 to qualify. Optionally clamp requiredMinutes to at least 1 when thresholdPercentage > 0, and clamp attendancePercentage to 100.

title: Check-then-act on activeSessions allows duplicate DM verification sessions / duplicate first-question DMs on rapid double-click
detail: startDmVerification checks activeSessions.has(existingKey) at line 191 and only inserts the session at line 326, after multiple awaits (getOrCreateDraft DB writes, getDraft, and the DM/thread send). Discord can deliver two Verify button interactions for the same user before the first inserts its session. Both pass the has()-check, both create/reuse the (idempotent) draft, both send a first-question DM/thread message, and the second set() overwrites the first session (new nonce), orphaning the first message's Cancel button under the old nonce (which then reports 'old session'). Impact is limited (duplicate DM, mild confusion) because getOrCreateDraft is idempotent and the nonce guard rejects the stale button, but it is a genuine unguarded check-then-act on shared mutable state.
fix: Reserve the session slot synchronously before the awaits: insert a placeholder session (or a per-key 'in-progress' marker) immediately after the has()-check and before any await, then populate it; or wrap startDmVerification in a per-(guild,user) async mutex.

title: Reopen within 7 days of a DELETED thread commits open-state then throws, leaving an orphaned 'open' ticket pointing at a dead thread
detail: On close, the default config modmail_delete_on_close (treated as true unless explicitly false in threadClose.ts:365 and :546) DELETES the Discord thread. reopenModmailThread first commits a transaction that flips the ticket to status='open' and re-inserts the open_modmail guard row (lines 89-109), then calls addOpenThread(ticket.thread_id) restoring the in-memory routing set (lines 113-116), and ONLY THEN does `interaction.client.channels.fetch(ticket.thread_id)` (line 120). For a thread that was deleted on close, that fetch rejects with Unknown Channel (10003), which is caught by the outer try/catch (line 150) and returns {success:false}. But the DB transaction and addOpenThread have already taken effect. Result: the ticket is now marked 'open' with a thread_id that no longer exists, the open_modmail guard row blocks the user from ever getting a NEW modmail (openPublicModmailThreadFor short-circuits on the existing guard row), and OPEN_MODMAIL_THREADS/handleInboundDmForModmail will route the applicant's DMs to a dead thread (silently failing). Because delete-on-close is the default, virtually every recently-closed ticket has a deleted thread, so the common `/modmail reopen user:@x` path (closed_at within 7 days -> reopen branch, lines 72-85) reliably lands in this broken state. The staff member is told 'Failed to reopen' while the system is left inconsistent.
fix: Fetch and unarchive/unlock the thread BEFORE mutating the DB and in-memory set, and treat a missing/deleted thread explicitly: if the thread can't be fetched (null or fetch throws), do NOT reopen in place — instead fall through to creating a fresh thread via openPublicModmailThreadFor (as the >7-day branch already does). Alternatively, wrap the unarchive in its own try/catch and roll back (reopenTicket->close, delete the open_modmail row, removeOpenThread) if the thread is gone. Either way, never leave status='open' with a thread_id that fails to resolve.

title: closeModmailThread / closeModmailForApplication are check-then-act with no atomic guard: concurrent close (double-click, or manual close racing auto-close-on-decision) double-flushes transcripts and double-DMs the user
detail: closeModmailThread guards only with a plain read: getTicketById then `if (ticket.status === 'closed') return` (lines 211-228). Two near-simultaneous invocations (e.g. a fast double-click of the Close button — handleModmailCloseButton at handlers.ts:144-159 calls deferUpdate then closeModmailThread, and Discord delivers two distinct interactions; OR a moderator clicking Close while an approve/reject decision concurrently runs closeModmailForApplication, which is fired unawaited via .catch() from web/routes/review.ts:223-608 and review/handlers/actionRunners.ts) both read status='open', both pass the guard, and both proceed. flushTranscript is NOT idempotent: the first call posts the transcript and deletes the in-memory buffer (transcript.ts:262); the second call finds an empty buffer, reconstructs the same conversation from modmail_message in the DB (transcript.ts:129-160), and posts a SECOND transcript message to the log channel. The user also receives two 'Modmail Closed' DMs, the dashboard gets two thread_closed notifications, and two modmail_close action-log rows are written. closeModmailForApplication has the same plain-read guard (getOpenTicketByUser at lines 456-460) and shares no lock with closeModmailThread, so the two functions can race each other as well.
fix: Make the status flip the atomic gate. Perform the close inside a transaction that conditionally updates only when still open and checks the affected row count, e.g. `UPDATE modmail_ticket SET status='closed', closed_at=datetime('now') WHERE id=? AND status='open'`; if changes()===0, another path already closed it — return early and skip transcript flush, DM, archive, logging, and dashboard notify. Apply the same guarded UPDATE in both closeModmailThread and closeModmailForApplication so they mutually exclude.

title: 7-day reopen window uses new Date() on a space-separated UTC SQLite timestamp, which Node parses as LOCAL time — window is shifted by the host's UTC offset
detail: closed_at is written by closeTicket via `datetime('now')` (tickets.ts:165) and the column default is also `datetime('now')` (db.ts:186), producing strings like '2026-05-31 12:00:00' (UTC, space separator, no 'T'/'Z'). Per ECMAScript, only the ISO simplified format (with 'T') is spec-parsed; a space-separated date-time is implementation-defined and V8/Node parse it as LOCAL time. So `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()` yields an instant offset from the true UTC instant by the host timezone offset, while `Date.now()` (line 74) is true UTC. The comparison `now - closedAt > sevenDays` is therefore skewed by up to the offset (e.g. several hours), so the 7-day boundary is wrong near the edge: tickets get the reopen-in-place branch vs the new-thread branch incorrectly. Harmless on a UTC host; wrong elsewhere. The identical pattern exists at src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304.
fix: Normalize the stored timestamp to a true epoch before comparing, e.g. parse as UTC: `new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z').getTime()`, or store/compare epoch seconds consistently (the open_modmail table already uses INTEGER strftime('%s','now')). Fix dashboardBridge.ts:304 the same way.

title: Private-thread mod-add loop relies on role.members (cache-only) and is currently dead code for modmail
detail: ensureModsCanSpeakInThread's private-thread branch (lines 165-232) iterates `role.members` (line 194) to add every mod to the thread. role.members reflects only the cached GuildMember collection; without the GuildMembers intent / full member fetch, large guilds will have incomplete role.members, so some moderators would never be added to a private thread and couldn't see it. In practice this branch is unreachable from modmail today: the only caller is threadOpen.ts:319, and threadOpen always creates PUBLIC threads (forum.threads.create / textChannel.threads.create default to public), so the function returns early at the isPublic check (lines 140-163). So this is a latent bug / dead path rather than an active one, but it will silently break if a private-thread modmail path is ever added.
fix: If private modmail threads are ever introduced, fetch role members explicitly (await role.guild.members.fetch() or role.members after a member fetch) rather than trusting the cache, and rely on parent-channel SendMessagesInThreads overwrites (already set at lines 113-131) instead of per-member adds where possible. Otherwise consider removing the unreachable branch to avoid future foot-guns.

title: Close-button success confirmation is posted to the thread that closeModmailThread just deleted, so staff get no confirmation under the default delete-on-close
detail: handleModmailCloseButton defers the update (line 150) and, on success, posts the confirmation via `interaction.channel.send(...)` (lines 162-167). But closeModmailThread, when modmail_delete_on_close is unset/true (the default, threadClose.ts:365), deletes the very thread the button lives in (threadClose.ts:370) before returning success. interaction.channel is that deleted thread, so the send throws and is swallowed by the catch at line 168. Net effect: after a successful close with the default config, the acting moderator receives no visible confirmation at all (the deferUpdate produced no ephemeral message either). Functional close still works; this is a UX/observability gap, not data loss.
fix: When result.success, send an ephemeral interaction.followUp({flags: Ephemeral, content: result.message}) instead of (or in addition to) posting into interaction.channel, since the channel may have been deleted as part of the close. Or skip thread deletion until after confirmation is delivered.

title: reopenModmailThread can throw on partial unique index when user already has a newer open ticket
detail: reopenModmailThread (userId path) selects the most recent ticket WHERE status='closed' (lines 46-56), then reopenTicket(ticket.id) runs `UPDATE modmail_ticket SET status='open' ...` (tickets.ts:174-179) with no guard against an existing open ticket for the same (guild_id, user_id). The runtime schema defines a partial unique index `idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id, user_id, status) WHERE status='open'` (src/db/db.ts:193-199). If the user already has an open ticket (e.g. a fresh thread was created after the prior one closed, or via the >7-day branch at threadReopen.ts:77-85 which opens a new ticket), flipping the old closed ticket back to 'open' violates the index and throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE inside the transaction (lines 89-109). The catch returns a generic 'Failed to reopen modmail thread' with no explanation. Integrity is preserved by the constraint, but the operation fails confusingly and the DM/unarchive side effects never run.
fix: Before reopening, check for an existing open ticket for (guildId, userId) and either refuse with a clear message ('User already has an open modmail thread: <#...>') or close/merge it first. Alternatively wrap reopenTicket in a guard that detects the constraint and surfaces a specific message.

title: closed_at parsed as local time but stored as UTC, skewing the 7-day reopen window
detail: closeTicket writes `closed_at = datetime('now')` (tickets.ts:164-166), which SQLite stores as a space-separated UTC string like '2026-05-31 12:34:56' (TEXT column, src/db/db.ts:186-187). reopenModmailThread computes `const closedAt = new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()` (line 73). Per the ES spec, the date+time space-separated form (no 'T', no 'Z') is parsed as LOCAL time by V8, not UTC (verified: new Date('2026-05-31 12:34:56') yields a local-time instant, off by the host UTC offset). So closedAt is shifted by the server's UTC offset (e.g. several hours), making the `now - closedAt > sevenDays` boundary (lines 75-77) decide reopen-vs-new-thread incorrectly near the 7-day edge. Low impact (hours of skew on a 7-day window) but a real correctness defect.
fix: Parse explicitly as UTC: `new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z').getTime()`, or store/compare epoch seconds consistently. Best: use a shared dt helper that knows the SQLite storage format.

title: Modmail close transcript buffer leaks in memory when no log channel is configured
detail: closeModmailThread relies entirely on flushTranscript to clear the per-ticket in-memory transcript buffer. flushTranscript only deletes transcriptBuffers entries on its success paths (transcript.ts:203 and 262). When `modmail_log_channel_id` is not configured it returns early at transcript.ts:119-122 WITHOUT deleting the buffer, and the exception path (transcript.ts:265-283) also never deletes it. closeModmailThread never calls the exported clearTranscriptBuffer as a safety net (grep shows it is only re-exported, never invoked in the close flow). Result: on every modmail close in a guild with no log channel set, the ticket's transcript lines remain in the module-level transcriptBuffers Map forever, growing unbounded with message volume. Same gap applies to closeModmailForApplication (lines 505-511).
fix: After flushTranscript returns (regardless of outcome), call clearTranscriptBuffer(ticketId) in both closeModmailThread and closeModmailForApplication; or have flushTranscript delete the buffer in a finally block / on the no-log-channel early return.

title: Modmail close button has no permission check and routes without a gate
detail: closeModmailThread performs no authorization check — it only looks up the ticket and closes it (lines 211-228). The slash command path enforces canRunAllCommands || hasManageGuild || isReviewer (commands.ts:65-75), but the Close button path does not: interactionCreate.ts:500-512 routes v1:modmail:close:* straight to handleModmailCloseButton, which immediately deferUpdates and calls closeModmailThread (handlers.ts:144-159) with no permission check. The Close button is only attached to the bot's first message inside the modmail thread (threadOpen.ts:382-387), a staff-only space, so practical exposure is low; but the close path is unauthenticated by design and would be abusable if that button/customId ever reaches a non-staff context.
fix: Add the same permission gate used by executeModmailCommand to handleModmailCloseButton (or inside closeModmailThread) before performing the close, and verify the resolved ticket's guild_id matches interaction.guildId.

title: /modmail close by thread ID does not verify the ticket belongs to the invoking guild
detail: When a thread ID is supplied (slash option `thread`, commands.ts:82-83) closeModmailThread calls getTicketByThread(threadId) (tickets.ts:85-98), which selects purely by thread_id with no guild_id filter. A reviewer in guild A who learns a modmail thread ID from guild B (where the same bot operates) could close guild B's ticket; downstream code then uses interaction.guildId for cleanup/config, producing cross-guild state mismatches (open_modmail row in guild B left as-is while DB ticket is closed). The per-guild permission check in commands.ts only validates the caller in guild A, not that the target ticket is in guild A.
fix: After resolving the ticket, assert `ticket.guild_id === interaction.guildId` and refuse otherwise. Apply the same guard in reopenModmailThread's threadId branch (threadReopen.ts:58-62).

title: Manual close archives+locks the thread and then immediately deletes it (redundant API calls, asymmetric behavior)
detail: closeModmailThread first fetches the thread and unconditionally calls setLocked(true) then setArchived(true) (lines 260-268), stashing it as threadForCleanup. Later, when modmail_delete_on_close is not false (the default), it calls threadForCleanup.delete() (lines 368-371), so the archive+lock work is wasted and two extra rate-limited API calls are made on every close. Separately, this manual-close DM (lines 280-292) does NOT attach the conversation transcript, whereas closeModmailForApplication does capture and attach it (lines 500-595) — inconsistent user experience for two close paths.
fix: Skip the eager setLocked/setArchived when the effective config will delete the thread (read modmail_delete_on_close once up front and branch). Optionally unify the two close paths so the manual close also offers the transcript DM.

title: Dead defensive check: closeModmailForApplication tests status!=='open' on a query that already filters status='open'
detail: getOpenTicketByUser only returns rows WHERE status='open' (tickets.ts:59-77), so `if (!ticket || ticket.status !== 'open')` at lines 457-460 can only ever be true via the `!ticket` branch; the status comparison is unreachable. Harmless, but it implies a guard that does not actually exist (it will not catch a 'closed' ticket because such a ticket is never returned here).
fix: Drop the redundant status comparison, or fetch via a status-agnostic lookup (getTicketById/getTicketByThread) if the intent is genuinely to re-check status.

title: Already-resolved/terminal/invalid guard replies overwrite the review card embed after deferUpdate
detail: All of the run*Action functions are reached after the interaction has already been acknowledged with interaction.deferUpdate() (every modal handler in modals.ts calls deferUpdate before invoking the runner, and the wrong_password/stale_modmail button paths in buttons.ts:96-141 also deferUpdate before calling runRejectAction). After deferUpdate, discord.js sets interaction.deferred = true (verified in node_modules/discord.js InteractionResponses.deferUpdate, and the deferUpdate doc explicitly says it defers an update to 'the message to which the component was attached'). lib/cmdWrap.replyOrEdit then takes the `interaction.deferred` branch and calls interaction.editReply(), which edits the SOURCE review-card message. So when two moderators race (e.g. one approves, the other clicks reject/kick/approve a moment later), the loser's guard branch (`replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: 'Already approved.' })` / 'This application is already resolved.' / 'Already resolved (...)' / 'Application not ready' etc.) replaces the entire review card's embed + buttons with a bare plain-text line. The card is only repaired later if some other path happens to call ensureReviewMessage; on these early-return guard branches it is not refreshed, so the card stays clobbered. Note the modal-opener guards in helpers.ts correctly pass flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral and run before showModal (interaction not yet acked) so they reply ephemerally and are fine — the defect is specifically the post-deferUpdate runners which omit the ephemeral flag.
fix: On the early guard branches inside the run*Action functions (and the duplicate-resolution checks in runVoteOutAction), do not use editReply on a component-deferred interaction. Either pass flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral and use interaction.followUp(...) for the notice (followUp is valid after deferUpdate and posts an ephemeral message instead of editing the card), or refresh the card via ensureReviewMessage and send the notice as an ephemeral followUp. Concretely, replace replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: ... }) with interaction.followUp({ content: ..., flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }).catch(...) in these guard paths.

title: permanent=false reject UPDATE unconditionally clears a prior permanent rejection flag/timestamp is avoided, but permanently_rejected is overwritten to 0 on every non-permanent reject
detail: rejectTx always runs `permanently_rejected = ?` with `permanent ? 1 : 0`. The terminal-state guards above only short-circuit when the current status is exactly 'rejected'/'approved'/'kicked'. A row can legitimately be permanently_rejected=1 while its status is, e.g., 'needs_info' or 'submitted' if a new application/flag path set the permanent flag without flipping status to 'rejected' (the permanent flag is a per-(guild,user) blocklist concept queried in claimHandlers.ts:84-88 across ANY of the user's rows). When a moderator then performs a normal (non-permanent) reject on such a row, this UPDATE forces permanently_rejected back to 0, silently un-banning a user who was previously permanently rejected. Even within a single row, doing a normal reject after the flag was set elsewhere downgrades it. The permanent_reject_at CASE correctly preserves the timestamp, but permanently_rejected itself is clobbered to 0.
fix: Do not lower the flag on a non-permanent reject. Use `permanently_rejected = CASE WHEN ? = 1 THEN 1 ELSE permanently_rejected END` (mirroring the permanent_reject_at CASE), so a normal reject never clears an existing permanent ban; only an explicit perm-reject sets it to 1.

title: runVoteOutAction uses interaction.followUp for duplicate/recorded notices but relies on an upstream deferUpdate that may not have happened on the slash path
detail: runVoteOutAction is typed ReviewActionInteraction (ButtonInteraction | ChatInputCommandInteraction | ModalSubmitInteraction) and calls interaction.followUp(...) directly (lines 843, 899) instead of replyOrEdit. followUp throws InteractionNotReplied if the interaction was neither deferred nor replied (verified in discord.js InteractionResponses.followUp: `if (!this.deferred && !this.replied) throw`). The vote-out modal handler does deferUpdate first, so the modal path is safe; but the function's type signature admits a ChatInputCommandInteraction caller, and if any current/future slash entry point invokes runVoteOutAction without first deferring, these followUp calls throw, are caught only by the outer try/catch in the modal handler (not present on a raw call), and the moderator gets no feedback. The terminal/missing-reason guards above (lines 822, 830) use replyOrEdit and are robust; the two raw followUp calls are the inconsistency.
fix: Use replyOrEdit (which handles fresh/deferred/replied uniformly) with flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral for the 'already voted' and 'Vote recorded' notices, or assert/ensure the interaction is deferred at function entry. This makes the runner safe regardless of caller ack state.

title: Legacy ping regex /^v1:ping:(.+)$/ also matches v1:ping:delete:* customIds (latent routing collision)
detail: handlePingInUnverified's legacy matcher /^v1:ping:(.+)$/ matches the delete-ping customId v1:ping:delete:<id> as well (payload becomes 'delete:<id>'). userMatch=/user([0-9]+)/ then fails, producing the misleading 'Invalid ping button data.' reply. This is currently masked because interactionCreate.ts:514 routes `v1:ping:delete:` first and returns before reaching the ping route at line 529. The bug is not live today, but the over-broad regex is a footgun: any reordering of the dispatcher, or a direct call to handlePingInUnverified, would mis-handle delete buttons. Defense-in-depth: the handler should not accept delete IDs.
fix: Tighten the legacy pattern to require a user segment and exclude the delete subroute, e.g. /^v1:ping:(?!delete:)(.+:user\d+)$/ or simply parse for user and bail if payload starts with 'delete:'. Better, rely solely on the centralized BTN_PING_UNVERIFIED_RE and drop the hand-rolled regexes.

title: Approval role-grant-failure abort path does not refresh the review card, leaving stale action buttons on an already-approved application
detail: When accepted_role_id is set but the role grant fails, the function logs, posts a channel error, calls updateReviewActionMeta, notifies the dashboard, and returns — but never calls ensureReviewMessage. The DB transaction (approveTx) has already committed status='approved'. The review card therefore still shows the pending approve/reject/kick buttons. A moderator clicking another action sees confusing behavior (the subsequent txs correctly return 'already'/'terminal' so no double-action occurs, but the card is misleading and the success/role-note summary the normal path would post is skipped). Impact is limited to UX/observability, not data integrity, because all downstream txs re-read status under transaction.
fix: Before returning in the role-failure block, call `await ensureReviewMessage(interaction.client, app.id).catch(...)` so the card reflects the approved-but-role-failed state (terminal card without action buttons), consistent with every other terminal path in this file.

title: Permanently-rejected check runs AFTER claimTx, leaving an orphaned claim on early return
detail: In handleClaimToggle, claimTx(app.id, ...) (line 43) atomically creates the review_claim row + audit row and commits. Only AFTER that does the code run the permRejectCheck query (lines 84-88: SELECT permanently_rejected ... WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND permanently_rejected=1). If that matches, the function replies 'permanently rejected ... cannot reapply' and returns at line 101 WITHOUT releasing the claim it just acquired (no unclaimTx/clearClaim). Result: the application is now claimed by a moderator who was told the action failed, blocking other Gatekeepers from claiming/acting until an admin force-clears it. Note the dashboard equivalent (src/web/routes/review.ts:49-50) performs the SAME perm-reject check and is documented as intended behavior (docs/reference/dashboard-api-security.md:42), so this is real defense-in-depth code, not dead code. Trigger requires app.user_id to have BOTH a non-terminal app row (so claimTx succeeds) and a separate row with permanently_rejected=1; getOrCreateDraft (src/features/gate/drafts.ts:155-162) normally blocks perm-rejected users from new drafts, which lowers (but does not eliminate) the probability — admin/unblock paths or direct flag-setting can produce the coexisting rows. The failure mode is fail-unsafe: state is corrupted instead of the action being rejected cleanly.
fix: Move the permanently_rejected check BEFORE claimTx so a perm-rejected applicant never gets claimed. Alternatively, if the check must stay post-claim, call clearClaim(app.id) (or unclaimTx) before returning at line 101 so the orphaned claim is released.

title: Garbled user-facing message for INVALID_STATUS claim errors (esp. panic mode)
detail: For err.code === 'INVALID_STATUS' the handler builds the message via err.message.split(' ')[2] to extract the status word. claimTx throws INVALID_STATUS in two cases: (1) terminal status, message 'Application already <status>' -> split[2] = '<status>' (works); (2) panic mode (src/features/reviewActions.ts:60-62), message 'Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended.' -> split(' ')[2] = 'is'. So when a guild is in panic mode and a moderator clicks Claim, they see 'Cannot claim: application is already **is**.' instead of the panic-mode notice. This is misleading exactly during an emergency lockdown. The technique (parsing a human-readable Error.message by word index) is also brittle to any future wording change.
fix: Carry structured data on ClaimError (e.g., a `status` field or a distinct PANIC code) and branch on that instead of string-splitting the message. At minimum, special-case the panic-mode message (or add a PANIC ClaimError code) so the reply reads 'Panic mode is active; review operations are suspended.'

title: BigInt() called on comma-separated permission NAMES, not numeric bitfields — diff/dangerous-change code throws on real data
detail: Every consumer in this file treats RoleSnapshot.permissions and PermissionOverwriteSnapshot.allow/deny as numeric bitfield strings: `new PermissionsBitField(BigInt(oldRole.permissions))` (256-257), `BigInt(oldOw.allow/deny)` (346-349), `BigInt(bitfield)` in bitfieldToPermissionNames (382), and `BigInt(role.permissions)` in getDangerousChanges (414). But the ONLY producers of those fields are roleToSnapshot/channelToSnapshot in src/features/serverAudit/types.ts (lines 234, 252-253), which store comma-separated permission NAMES: `permissions: role.permissions.join(',')` and `allow/deny: ow.allow.join(',')`. At runtime a snapshot holds e.g. `"Administrator,ManageRoles"` or `"ViewChannel"`. `BigInt("ViewChannel")` throws `SyntaxError: Cannot convert ViewChannel to a BigInt`. Trigger paths: (a) computeSnapshotDiff itself calls getDangerousChanges(diff) at line 247, so it throws whenever diff.rolesAdded is non-empty (any role added since last audit has ≥1 perm) or whenever computeRoleChange runs for a role whose permissions string changed; (b) computeOverwriteModification throws whenever a channel overwrite's allow/deny string changes. Impact: In src/commands/audit/diff.ts the catch at line 141 surfaces `❌ Failed to compute diff: Cannot convert ... to a BigInt` to the user — `/audit diff` is broken for any server with real permission changes. In src/features/serverAuditDocs.ts the whole block is wrapped in a silent try/catch (line 174), so DIFF.md is never written and result.dangerousChangeCount stays 0 — dangerous permission escalations (Admin/ManageRoles/Ban added to a role) are silently never detected or alerted, a security-monitoring failure. The unit test masks this because tests/features/securityDiff.test.ts only ever uses `permissions: "0"` / `""` (BigInt("0")=0n, BigInt("")=0n do not throw) and never diffs two roles that actually differ in a named permission.
fix: Make producers and consumers agree on one format. Simplest: since snapshots already store comma-separated names, replace the BigInt/PermissionsBitField parsing with set-diffing of the name lists, e.g. `const oldSet = new Set(oldRole.permissions ? oldRole.permissions.split(',') : []);` then compute added = newSet items not in oldSet and removed = oldSet items not in newSet. Do the same for allow/deny in computeOverwriteModification and overwritesAdded/removed, and make bitfieldToPermissionNames just `bitfield ? bitfield.split(',') : []`. Alternatively change roleToSnapshot/channelToSnapshot to store the real numeric bitfield (role.permissions.bitfield.toString()) — but that requires re-fetching bitfields in analyze.ts (RoleData.permissions is already names-only), so the split-based fix is safer. Add a test where two roles differ by a named permission to prevent regression.

title: ManageRoles Scope Warning reports role.position as the count of manageable roles
detail: The issue text reads `Role can assign/remove ${role.position} roles below it.` but role.position is the hierarchy position index, not the number of roles beneath this one. The code computes `rolesAbove` (line 369) but never computes a roles-below count, then substitutes the position integer as if it were that count. Example: a staff role at position 50 with only 3 roles beneath it will tell moderators it can assign/remove 50 roles. This is misinformation inside a security advisory generated by `/audit security` (CONFLICTS.md) and shown to leadership, undermining trust in the audit and potentially causing wrong remediation decisions. Detection of the issue itself is fine; only the reported number is wrong.
fix: Compute the actual count, e.g. `const rolesBelow = roles.filter((r) => r.position < role.position && r.name !== '@everyone').length;` and interpolate `${rolesBelow}` instead of `${role.position}` in the issue string.

title: `modmail_delete_on_close` opt-out is silently ignored — threads always deleted on close
detail: Both close paths compute the delete decision as `cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== false` (line 365 in `closeModmailThread`, line 546 in `closeModmailForApplication` feeding `archiveOrDeleteThread`). The `GuildConfig` type declares `modmail_delete_on_close?: boolean | null`, but that is a type-level lie. The column is created as `INTEGER DEFAULT 1` (src/lib/config.ts:375, ensureModRolesColumns), the config command stores the boolean via upsert which converts `false`->integer `0` / `true`->`1` (src/lib/config.ts:687; src/commands/config/setFeatures.ts:300-304), and `getConfig` does `SELECT *` and returns the raw row with no boolean coercion (src/lib/config.ts:707-724). So at runtime `cfg.modmail_delete_on_close` is the NUMBER `0` or `1`, never a boolean. `0 !== false` evaluates to `true` (strict inequality: number 0 is not boolean false), so `preferDelete`/`deleteOnClose` is `true` even when an admin explicitly set 'Delete on Close = off' (stored as 0). Impact: every modmail close DELETES the Discord thread regardless of the setting, irreversibly destroying the in-channel thread/history against explicit admin opt-out. The opt-out path (archive+lock, keep thread) is unreachable.
fix: Compare the integer truthiness instead of strict boolean inequality. Either coerce in getConfig (e.g. `modmail_delete_on_close: config.modmail_delete_on_close == null ? null : !!config.modmail_delete_on_close`) or change the consumers to `const preferDelete = cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== 0 && cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== false;` (default true only when null/undefined). Cleanest: normalize all INTEGER-boolean config columns to real booleans on read in getConfig.

title: 7-day reopen window parses UTC SQLite timestamp as local time
detail: `const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime() : 0;` then `if (now - closedAt > sevenDays)`. `closed_at` is written by `closeTicket` as `datetime('now')` (src/features/modmail/tickets.ts:165) and the column is TEXT (src/db/db.ts:187), producing a UTC string like `"2025-05-31 14:00:00"` with no timezone marker. Per V8/Node semantics, `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS")` (space-separated, no 'Z') is interpreted in the host's LOCAL timezone, not UTC. Comparing that against `Date.now()` (true UTC epoch) shifts `closedAt` by the host's UTC offset (up to ±14h), so the 7-day boundary is wrong by that offset whenever the bot host is not on UTC — a ticket can be treated as 'too old' (forcing a brand-new thread) or 'still reopenable' incorrectly near the boundary. The codebase already knows the correct fix: src/ui/reviewCard.ts:108-111 and src/features/review/card.ts:129 normalize with `trimmed.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'` before parsing; this call site omits it. (Same defect exists in the sibling src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304.)
fix: Normalize before parsing, mirroring reviewCard.ts: `const raw = ticket.closed_at; const iso = raw && raw.includes(' ') && !raw.includes('T') ? raw.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z' : raw; const closedAt = raw ? Date.parse(iso) : 0;` Or store closed_at as a Unix epoch integer (strftime('%s','now')) consistently and compare numerically.

title: Private-thread mod add iterates only cached role members (role.members)
detail: In `ensureModsCanSpeakInThread`, the private-thread branch adds mods via `const members = role.members; for (const [memberId] of members) { await thread.members.add(memberId); }`. `Role.members` is derived from the guild member cache and contains only members currently cached; without a prior `guild.members.fetch()` it can be empty or partial (common right after a restart before GUILD_MEMBERS chunking completes). Result: some moderators silently never get added to a private modmail thread and cannot see/reply. Note: the active modmail flow creates PUBLIC threads (openPublicModmailThreadFor uses CreatePublicThreads and the public branch returns early at line 162), so this branch is effectively dead for the current flow — hence low severity/confidence — but it is a latent bug if a private thread is ever passed.
fix: Before iterating, fetch members: `const role = await guild.roles.fetch(roleId); const members = await guild.members.fetch().then(() => role.members);` or fetch members with the role explicitly. Alternatively rely on a parent permission overwrite for the role (already set on the parent) rather than per-member adds.

title: Post-thread-creation failure returns 'Failed to create' even though the thread exists and is registered
detail: Thread creation (lines 289-303), permission setup, the `registerModmailThreadTx` UPDATE/UPSERT (lines 323-330), and `addOpenThread` (333) all run BEFORE later steps like `thread.send(...)` (line 408) and the applicant DM. If any later awaited step throws, control jumps to the catch (440). The cleanup there only deletes rows with `thread_id = 'pending'` (line 478), so the already-registered real row and ticket survive (correct), but the function still returns `{ success:false, message: 'Failed to create modmail thread...' }`. The moderator is told it failed while a fully functional, routable modmail thread actually exists, leading to confusion and possible duplicate-open attempts (which will then correctly report 'already exists'). Impact is UX/operational, not data corruption.
fix: Track a flag once the thread is created+registered; in the catch, if the thread already exists/registered, return success (or a 'thread created but follow-up step failed' message with the thread link) instead of a generic failure.

title: Ticket open button has no dedup/cooldown — double-click creates duplicate channels and burns numbers
detail: handleOpenButton defers ephemerally then calls TicketService.create() with no per-user/per-type guard. TicketService.create() (src/features/tickets/service.ts:214-352) never checks for an existing open ticket of the same type for the opener — it unconditionally allocateNextNumber(), creates a Discord channel, posts a greeting with role pings, and inserts a ticket row. The interactionCreate router (src/events/interactionCreate.ts:582-595) routes tk: buttons directly to handleTicketButton with no checkCooldown wrapper (unlike error-card buttons which do gate on a cooldown). Discord button double-clicks are extremely common, and because the first interaction is deferred (not yet replied) the second click is still a valid, separately-dispatched interaction. Two near-simultaneous clicks each create a full ticket channel, each consume a ticket number, and each fire pingRoleIds notifications. Impact: orphan/duplicate ticket channels, wasted ticket numbers, duplicate staff pings, and user confusion about which channel is real.
fix: Add a guard before creation: either (a) a short per-(userId, typeKey) cooldown via checkCooldown around handleOpenButton, and/or (b) in TicketService.create(), SELECT for an existing open ticket WHERE opener_user_id = ? AND type_key = ? AND status = 'open' and short-circuit (reply with a link to the existing channel) instead of opening another. A UNIQUE partial index on (opener_user_id, type_key) WHERE status='open' would make it race-proof.

title: INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on whole-second joined_at_s silently drops a session on rapid same-second rejoin
detail: insertVoiceJoin inserts (guild_id, user_id, channel_id, joined_at_s) with INSERT OR IGNORE, and joined_at_s = floor(Date.now()/1000) (1-second resolution). The table's UNIQUE constraint is exactly (guild_id, user_id, channel_id, joined_at_s) (migrations/052_voice_session.ts:27). Scenario: a user with an open row for channel A at second T leaves (Case 2 closes that row, setting left_at_s=T) and rejoins channel A within the same second (Case 1). The new INSERT collides with the just-closed row's identical 4-tuple and is silently IGNORED, so no open session exists. The user's voice time in A is then untracked until a later second boundary. The same collision can happen on a quick A→B→A move sequence within one second. Voice minutes feed newsletter/pulse stats (web/src/lib/server/queries/pulse.ts:334-344), so this under-counts voice activity. Low frequency but real and silent.
fix: Drop INSERT OR IGNORE in favor of a plain INSERT (the UNIQUE was meant only to dedupe true duplicates), or add a finer-grained discriminator to the uniqueness (e.g., include a monotonic counter or use millisecond precision for joined_at), or close+insert atomically while ensuring the new row cannot collide with the row just closed.

title: close() writes the permanent archive BEFORE applying the closed state, so the archive records the ticket as still open
detail: In close(), writeArchive(ticket) is awaited at line 465 using the in-memory ticket object fetched by findById (status='open', closedAt=null, closeReason=null). Only afterward (line 466) does getSetClosedStmt() flip status to 'closed' and set closed_at/close_reason. writeArchive serializes that stale ticket object into the JSON payload (service.ts:560-568 `payload.ticket = ticket`). The archive file — the long-term auditable record the module exists to produce — therefore says status:'open', closedAt:null, closeReason:null for a ticket that is being closed. The 'closed' and 'archived' events are captured, but the embedded ticket snapshot is wrong.
fix: Run getSetClosedStmt() first, then re-read the row (or mutate the local object's status/closedAt/closeReason/closedByUserId) and pass the closed snapshot to writeArchive, so the archived ticket reflects its terminal state.

title: create() creates the Discord channel before the DB insert; an insert failure orphans an untracked channel
detail: The Discord channel is created at line 241 (guild.channels.create), and only after that does getInsertTicketStmt().run(...) insert the tracking row (line 252). create() is not wrapped in any compensating try/catch. If the DB insert throws (e.g., ticket table missing per the lazy-prepare warning at lines 39-44, a constraint violation, or a transient SQLite error), the function rejects but the Discord channel already exists with no corresponding ticket row. It will never be found by findByChannelId, never closed by the lifecycle, and the allocated number is consumed. The handler (handlers.ts:247) just reports the error to the user, leaving a permanent orphan channel under the Tickets category.
fix: Insert the DB row first (using a placeholder channel_id is awkward), or wrap the post-create steps in try/catch and delete the freshly-created channel (channel.delete()) if the DB insert fails, so a failed open leaves no orphan.

title: Reopen 7-day window uses local-time parsing of a UTC SQLite timestamp (timezone-dependent boundary error)
detail: closeTicket() in tickets.ts writes closed_at with SQLite datetime('now'), which produces a UTC wall-clock string WITHOUT a timezone marker, e.g. '2026-05-31 12:00:00' (space-separated, no 'Z'). threadReopen.ts line 73 then does `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. V8/Node parses a non-ISO, space-separated date string as LOCAL time, not UTC. So the parsed instant is shifted by the host's UTC offset. The result feeds the 7-day comparison `now - closedAt > sevenDays` (line 77), which decides whether to reopen the existing thread vs. create a brand-new one (line 79). On a host behind UTC the effective window is lengthened; ahead of UTC it is shortened — by up to the full UTC offset (e.g. ~5-8h for US zones). Tickets right at the boundary will take the wrong branch: either spuriously spawning a new thread (and new ticket row) for a ticket that should reopen, or reopening a thread Discord may have already auto-archived. The unit tests mask this because threadReopen.test.ts constructs closed_at via Date.toISOString() (with 'Z', parsed as UTC), which never matches the real datetime('now') format the DB actually stores. dashboardBridge.ts:304 repeats the same `new Date(ticket.closed_at)` pattern on the same column, so the inconsistency is systemic.
fix: Parse closed_at as UTC explicitly. Either store epoch seconds (strftime('%s','now')) like open_modmail.created_at and compare numerically, or normalize on read, e.g. `const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? Date.parse(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z') : 0;`. Align closeTicket() and the reopen/dashboard readers on one canonical format, and update tests to use the actual DB format.

title: Intended-ephemeral claim feedback becomes a public edit of the review card (flags dropped after deferUpdate)
detail: handleClaimToggle is always entered AFTER the parent handleReviewButton called interaction.deferUpdate() (src/features/review/handlers/buttons.ts:177-181). deferUpdate() sets interaction.deferred = true (discord.js InteractionResponses.deferUpdate -> this.deferred = true), and for a component interaction the response '@original' is the message the button is attached to: the public review card. Every feedback call here uses replyOrEdit(interaction, { content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }). But replyOrEdit (src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:503-506) takes the deferred branch and explicitly strips flags (`const { flags, ...editPayload } = withFlags; interaction.editReply(editPayload)`), which PATCHes '@original'. Net effect: messages meant to be private to the clicking moderator -- 'This application is already claimed by another moderator.', 'Cannot claim: application is already X.', 'An unexpected error occurred.', and especially 'This user has been permanently rejected from <server> and cannot reapply.' (lines 91-93) -- are written publicly onto the shared review card, overwriting its content line and exposing internal moderation state to everyone who can see the channel. The success path (lines 146-150) similarly edits the card content rather than sending the intended per-mod confirmation.
fix: After an upstream deferUpdate(), do not use replyOrEdit for per-moderator feedback. Use interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) directly (followUp preserves flags and posts a separate ephemeral message), or have replyOrEdit honor ephemeral by routing to followUp when the interaction was deferred via deferUpdate rather than calling editReply. At minimum, stop stripping flags for genuinely ephemeral content.

title: Unclaim feedback/errors also leak onto the public review card (same deferUpdate + stripped-flags path)
detail: handleUnclaimAction is invoked from handleUnclaimModal (src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts:242-270), which calls interaction.deferUpdate() before delegating. As with claim, interaction.deferred is true, so every replyOrEdit({ ..., flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) here (NOT_CLAIMED / NOT_OWNER / APP_NOT_FOUND error strings, the unexpected-error string, and the 'Application `CODE` unclaimed successfully.' confirmation at 243-248) is turned into a public editReply on the review card with the ephemeral flag discarded (src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:505). Owner-mismatch and not-claimed messages intended for one mod are shown to the whole channel and clobber the card's content line.
fix: Same as the claim finding: send these as interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) instead of relying on replyOrEdit (which drops flags on the deferred/editReply branch).

title: Modal error replies overwrite the public review card content instead of being ephemeral
detail: Each modal handler calls interaction.deferUpdate() (e.g. lines 49-53, 87-91, 126-130, 165-169, 203-207, 242-246) before doing work, so interaction.deferred is true. On the error paths these handlers call replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: 'Failed to process ... (trace: <id>).' }) with no flags, which takes the editReply branch in src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:503-506 and PATCHes the card's '@original' message -- replacing the review card's content line with the failure/trace text visible to the whole channel. The unclaim-cancelled branch (modals.ts:258-265) additionally passes flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral, which is then stripped by replyOrEdit, so 'Unclaim cancelled. You must type UNCLAIM...' is shown publicly on the card too. Result: a transient handler error visibly corrupts the shared card content for all moderators.
fix: On these post-deferUpdate error paths, use interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) so the failure notice is a separate ephemeral message and the card content is left intact.

title: renderWelcomeTemplate applicant.tag dereferences member.user without a guard, can throw and abort the welcome
detail: In postWelcomeMessage's custom-template branch, applicant.tag is computed as `member.user?.tag ?? member.user.username`. The optional chain on the first operand concedes that member.user may be null/undefined, but the fallback dereferences member.user.username unguarded. If member.user is ever nullish (partial/uncached GuildMember), this throws a TypeError and the welcome post fails. This is inconsistent with the defensive pattern used a few lines up in the same file (buildDefaultWelcomeMessage line 147 uses `member.user?.tag ?? member.user?.username ?? member.id`). Likelihood is low for a freshly fetched approved member, but it is a genuine latent crash path.
fix: Mirror the safe cascade: `tag: member.user?.tag ?? member.user?.username ?? member.id`.

title: removeRole skips audit logging on member-not-found / role-not-found, creating audit-trail gaps
detail: assignRole logs a 'skipped' role_assignments row for every early-return (member not found at 235-237, role not found at 252-254). removeRole's equivalent early returns (member not found at 335-343, role not found at 347-357) return a failure result but do NOT call logRoleAssignment. Code that audits role activity by reading role_assignments will therefore see asymmetric history: failed adds are recorded but failed removes are silently missing. Not a crash, but it undermines the 'full audit trail' the module advertises and can hide why an expected role removal never happened.
fix: Add logRoleAssignment(guild.id, userId, roleId, 'Unknown', 'skipped', reason, triggeredBy, { error: errorMsg }) to both removeRole early-return branches, matching assignRole.

title: vote_out voter ordering is nondeterministic on same-second votes (ORDER BY created_at with 1s resolution, no tiebreak)
detail: getVoteOutVotersStmt orders by created_at ASC, but vote_out.created_at is a TEXT column populated via datetime('now') (migrations/061_vote_out.ts:23 and insertVoteOutStmt at queries.ts:124), which has only 1-second resolution. Two mods voting within the same second get identical created_at values, and SQLite does not guarantee a stable order for ties, so the rendered public attribution ('X and Y voted <@user> out.' built from getVoteOutVoters/getVoteOutEntries in actionRunners.ts:1011-1020) and the button-label ordering can vary between renders. Cosmetic, but it makes the consensus-rejection message and audit display order unstable.
fix: Add a deterministic tiebreak using the autoincrement id, e.g. `ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC`, in both getVoteOutVotersStmt queries (or store an integer epoch instead of a TEXT datetime).

title: Garbled claim error during panic mode (fragile message string parsing)
detail: On a failed claim, INVALID_STATUS is rendered as `Cannot claim: application is already **${err.message.split(" ")[2]}**.` This assumes the ClaimError message is always the terminal-state form "Application already <status>" (split()[2] == status). But claimTx() throws the SAME INVALID_STATUS code for panic mode with message "Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended." (reviewActions.ts:62). split(" ")[2] of that string is "is", so during panic mode a moderator clicking Claim sees the nonsensical message "Cannot claim: application is already **is**." It also needlessly calls ensureReviewMessage() to "refresh card after blocked claim" even though nothing changed. The claim is still correctly blocked, so this is cosmetic/diagnostic, but it actively misleads the operator during an emergency (panic) when clear messaging matters most.
fix: Do not parse the human message. Either (a) carry the status as a structured field on ClaimError (e.g. add a `status?` property set when throwing terminal-state errors) and render that, or (b) add a distinct error code for panic (e.g. "PANIC_MODE") and branch on it explicitly so panic shows "Review operations are suspended (panic mode)."

title: claimTx writes integer Unix seconds into ISO/TEXT claimed_at, breaking the review-card claim timestamp parser
detail: claimTx inserts claimed_at = nowUtc() (an INTEGER, Unix seconds — see src/lib/time.ts:34). The review_claim.claimed_at column is TEXT (src/db/db.ts:132) and the shared type declares it `string // ISO timestamp string` (src/features/review/types.ts:66). SQLite TEXT affinity coerces the integer to the string "1735689600". The review card's embed builder parses it with a naive branch: `typeof claim.claimed_at === "number" ? claim.claimed_at : Math.floor(new Date(claim.claimed_at).getTime()/1000)` (src/features/review/card.ts:339-342). Because the stored value is a numeric STRING, the else branch runs `new Date("1735689600")` which is an Invalid Date, so getTime() is NaN and the rendered Discord relative timestamp `<t:NaN:R>` is broken on the live "Claim Status" line. (src/ui/reviewCard.ts:96 has a robust parseClaimedAt that handles numeric strings; card.ts does not, so the two renderers disagree.) Root cause is the type/representation mismatch introduced at this write site.
fix: Standardize the representation. Simplest: store ISO text here (e.g. tsToIso(nowUtc()) or datetime('now')) so it matches the declared type and both parsers; OR change card.ts:339-342 to use the tolerant parseClaimedAt() (or Number()-first heuristic) like ui/reviewCard.ts. Pick one canonical format and apply it at every read/write of claimed_at.

title: Unclaim via modal: 'ephemeral' confirmation is not ephemeral and overwrites the review card
detail: handleUnclaimAction is reached two ways: directly from the unclaim button (deferUpdate'd) and from the unclaim confirmation MODAL (handlers/modals.ts:242-270 calls deferUpdate() then handleUnclaimAction). After unclaim succeeds, line 243 calls replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: `Application \`code\` unclaimed successfully.`, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }). When the interaction is deferred (both paths defer), replyOrEdit takes the editReply branch (src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:503-506) which DESTRUCTURES AND DISCARDS `flags` and edits the deferred source message. So (a) the Ephemeral flag is silently ignored, and (b) editReply targets the review card message the unclaim button lives on, overwriting the freshly re-rendered card (ensureReviewMessage was just called at line 233) with the plain text "Application … unclaimed successfully.", dropping the embed/buttons. handleClaimToggle relies on this same editReply-edits-card behavior ON PURPOSE (line 145-150), which is why this asymmetric misuse for unclaim is easy to miss.
fix: For confirmations that must be ephemeral after a deferUpdate, use interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) instead of replyOrEdit, or have replyOrEdit fall through to followUp when the caller passes Ephemeral on a deferred(update) interaction. Do not editReply the card unless that is the intent.

title: Possible TypeError reading member.user.username when member.user is nullish
detail: In postWelcomeMessage's custom-template branch: `tag: member.user?.tag ?? member.user.username`. The left operand uses optional chaining (member.user?.tag), acknowledging member.user could be nullish, but the `??` fallback dereferences member.user.username WITHOUT optional chaining. If member.user is ever null/undefined (uncached/partial GuildMember), the fallback throws TypeError and the whole approval-time welcome post fails. Contrast line 147 which correctly guards every hop: `member.user?.tag ?? member.user?.username ?? member.id`.
fix: Mirror line 147: use `member.user?.tag ?? member.user?.username ?? member.id` (also pass a safe display fallback).

title: getClaim returns an object typed as ReviewClaimRow but missing the app_id field
detail: This getClaim SELECTs only `reviewer_id, claimed_at` yet casts the result to ReviewClaimRow, whose type declares a non-optional `app_id: string` (types.ts:63-67). At runtime app_id is undefined while the type says it is present — an unsound cast. The sibling implementation in reviewActions.ts:209 correctly selects app_id, reviewer_id, claimed_at, so the two getClaim functions diverge. Current consumers (claimGuard, card.ts) only read reviewer_id/claimed_at, so no crash today, but any future code that trusts the type and reads claim.app_id from this path will get undefined silently.
fix: Add app_id to the SELECT here (SELECT app_id, reviewer_id, claimed_at ...) to match the declared type and the reviewActions.ts implementation, or narrow the return type to Pick<ReviewClaimRow,'reviewer_id'|'claimed_at'>.

title: Idempotent re-claim still posts a duplicate public 'claimed' message and dashboard event
detail: claimTx treats a re-claim by the SAME moderator as an idempotent no-op: it returns early without inserting a review_action and without error (reviewActions.ts:95-98). handleClaimToggle cannot distinguish this from a first-time claim, so on a double-submit it still logs 'application claimed successfully', re-runs logActionPretty(action:'claim'), fires notifyDashboard('review:claimed'), and posts another public '<@user> has claimed this application.' card edit. The button cooldown (buttons.ts:84 isRateLimited) suppresses most rapid double-clicks, so the window is small, but a click outside the cooldown window (or a retried interaction) yields duplicate public chatter / dashboard noise.
fix: Have claimTx signal whether a new claim was actually created (e.g. return boolean or throw a benign ALREADY_OWNED sentinel) and have handleClaimToggle skip the public message / dashboard notify when the claim already belonged to the same moderator.

title: beforeSend only scrubs event.message, not exception values — Discord tokens/secrets in thrown errors reach Sentry unredacted
detail: The beforeSend hook applies the Discord-token regex and env scrubbing ONLY to event.message and event.contexts.runtime.env. However, captureException() (the primary path, called from index.ts uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers and captureException() throughout the codebase) puts the error text in event.exception.values[].value and stack frames, NOT event.message. So if a Discord bot token, DSN, or other secret ever appears in a thrown Error's message or stack (e.g. a discord.js error echoing an Authorization header, or an error string built from config), it is sent to Sentry verbatim with no redaction. The token regex never runs against the field that actually carries exception text. This defeats the stated purpose ('tokens in error messages would be a security nightmare').
