fix: In beforeSend, also iterate event.exception?.values and run the same token regex on each value.value (and optionally on stack frames / breadcrumb messages / event.request data). Factor the redaction into a helper and apply it to message, exception values, and breadcrumbs uniformly. Consider also setting sendDefaultPii:false and using Sentry's built-in data scrubbing.

title: Sentry onFatalError calls process.exit(1) immediately, bypassing the app's deliberate delayed-exit-to-flush and buffered-write flush
detail: onUncaughtExceptionIntegration.onFatalError logs then calls process.exit(1) synchronously. But src/index.ts:54-63 installs its own uncaughtException handler that intentionally does setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_EXIT_DELAY_MS) specifically to 'Give Sentry time to flush'. Sentry's integration also listens on uncaughtException; its onFatalError firing an immediate process.exit(1) preempts that delay, so (a) the Sentry capture may not finish flushing over the network, and (b) buffered writes that are only drained in the SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful path (messageActivityLogger.flushOnShutdown, messageArchive.flushArchiveBuffersOnShutdown, voice session close, DB close) are skipped entirely on an uncaught exception, risking lost activity/archive data. The comment 'let app handle gracefully / Allow existing handlers to run' directly contradicts the immediate exit.
fix: Do not call process.exit(1) inside onFatalError. Either let the app's own uncaughtException handler own the exit (after its flush delay), or in onFatalError await Sentry.close(timeout) and trigger the same buffer-flush sequence before exiting. At minimum, replace the immediate exit with a short setTimeout matching UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_EXIT_DELAY_MS so the delayed-flush intent is preserved.

title: Module-level db.prepare() on sync_marker is unguarded; the 'first startup before migration' case the comment claims to handle actually throws at import time, not in the try/catch
detail: touchStmt and getStmt are compiled with db.prepare() at module load (lines 25-37). better-sqlite3 validates table existence at prepare() time, so on a brand-new DB where this module is imported before migration 026 has created sync_marker, db.prepare('UPDATE sync_marker ...') throws 'no such table: sync_marker' during module evaluation. db.ts deliberately does NOT create sync_marker (lines 287-288: 'created by migration 026 ... Do not add schema creation here'). The try/catch in touchSyncMarker/getSyncMarker only wraps .run()/.get(), so the comment 'Silently ignore if table doesn't exist yet (first startup before migration)' is misleading: that exact scenario fails at prepare(), outside the guard, and would crash whatever first imports this module (e.g. src/lib/config.ts, src/features/logger.ts). In production this is masked because migrations run as a separate pre-step, but the safety the comment promises is not actually provided.
fix: Lazily prepare the statements inside the functions (e.g. memoize on first call) so preparation happens under the try/catch, or wrap the module-level prepare calls in try/catch returning a null-statement fallback. Alternatively guarantee migration 026 runs before any import of this module and remove the misleading comment.

title: Initial-check setTimeout is neither captured, cleared on stop, nor unref'd
detail: startDiskSpaceScheduler schedules the first disk check with `setTimeout(async () => {...}, 15000)` but does not store the returned handle. Only the periodic `setInterval` handle is saved to `_activeInterval` and unref'd. Consequences: (1) `stopDiskSpaceScheduler()` cannot cancel this pending timer, so if the bot starts and is asked to shut down within 15s, `checkDiskSpace` still fires after stop was called (touching `client.guilds.cache`, sending an embed) during teardown; (2) unlike the `setInterval`, this timeout is not `.unref()`'d, so for up to 15s it can keep the Node event loop alive and delay a clean process exit. Compare with badgeRefreshScheduler.ts which captures and unref's its startupTimer.
fix: Capture the timeout handle (e.g. a module-level `_startupTimeout`), call `.unref?.()` on it, and clear it in `stopDiskSpaceScheduler()` alongside `_activeInterval`.

title: Disk usage computed from bfree (incl. root-reserved blocks) and no guard for statfs returning zeros
detail: getDiskStats computes freeBytes from `stats.bfree` (total free blocks) rather than `stats.bavail` (blocks available to a non-privileged process). On typical ext4 volumes ~5% is reserved for root, so usedPercent is under-reported relative to what the bot process can actually use, delaying the 80%/90% alerts the feature exists to deliver. Separately, if statfs ever returns blocks=0, `usedPercent = Math.round((usedBytes/0)*100)` is NaN; `NaN >= CRITICAL_THRESHOLD_PERCENT` and `NaN >= WARNING_THRESHOLD_PERCENT` are both false, so the check silently records success and never alerts even on a genuinely full disk.
fix: Use `stats.bavail` for the free/available figure that drives the alert threshold (keep bfree only if you specifically want raw free). Add a guard: if `totalBytes <= 0` or `!Number.isFinite(usedPercent)`, log a warning and skip rather than treating it as healthy.

title: Panic mode skips role removal after the DB row was already deleted, orphaning the multiplier role
detail: cleanupExpiredMultipliers calls removeExpiredMultipliers() which both SELECTs and DELETEs the expired rows from active_byte_multipliers (see byteMultiplierStore.ts removeExpiredMultipliers). processExpiredMultiplier then early-returns when isPanicMode(guild) is true, before removing the Discord role. Because the tracking row is already gone, the user keeps the XP-multiplier role indefinitely; nothing will ever retry the removal once panic mode clears. The in-code NOTE acknowledges manual cleanup is required, but this is a real economy/integrity gap (the XP boost outlives its paid window) rather than a no-op.
fix: Check panic mode (or skip such guilds) before deleting from the DB, or re-insert/return the entry when role removal is skipped so a later run retries it. Simplest: filter expired entries by panic state and only delete the ones you will actually process.

title: getActionMeta(action) result is dereferenced before the try/catch; an unmapped action throws after the audit row is already written
detail: After the action_log INSERT (guarded by try/catch) and the getLoggingChannel await, getActionMeta(action) is called and `actionMeta.emoji`/`.title`/`.color` are dereferenced at lines 538-539 — outside any try/catch (only the later channel.send is wrapped). The exhaustive Record<ActionType,ActionMeta> makes meta[action] safe for typed callers, but any caller that passes an action via `as any` / a stale string read from the DB would get `undefined` and throw a TypeError out of logActionPretty. Since the DB write already succeeded, the failure is a post-commit crash that the caller must handle; not all callers wrap logActionPretty in try/catch.
fix: Guard the lookup: `const actionMeta = getActionMeta(action); if (!actionMeta) { logActionJSON(...); return; }`, or move embed construction into the existing send try/catch so a bad action still degrades to JSON logging instead of throwing.

title: Failed Discord thread creation leaves an orphan open ticket that permanently blocks future modmail for the user
detail: The race-protection transaction (lines 227-263) atomically commits BOTH a new modmail_ticket row (createTicket, line 241, status defaults to 'open' per db.ts:185) AND a 'pending' open_modmail guard row. If the subsequent Discord thread creation (forum.threads.create line 289 or textChannel.threads.create line 298) throws — e.g. transient 500, rate limit, or perms revoked between the precheck and the call — control jumps to the catch (line 440). The cleanup there (lines 476-479) deletes ONLY the 'pending' open_modmail row; it never deletes the orphan modmail_ticket row. That row remains with status='open', thread_id=NULL. There is a partial unique index idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id,user_id,status) WHERE status='open' (db.ts:195-198). On the user's NEXT open attempt, the open_modmail fast-path is clear (pending was deleted), so execution re-enters the transaction and createTicket runs INSERT INTO modmail_ticket with default status='open' -> violates the partial unique index -> throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT. The catch then misclassifies this as isRaceCondition (line 448 matches 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT'), finds no open_modmail row, and returns the generic 'Failed to create modmail thread' error. Net effect: once thread creation fails, that applicant can never have a modmail thread opened again until someone manually deletes the orphan ticket row from the DB. The stated invariant in the code comment ('if INSERT into open_modmail fails we don't leave orphan tickets') only covers the open_modmail collision, not a post-transaction Discord failure.
fix: In the catch block's cleanup, also remove the just-created ticket when the thread was never created. Either (a) wrap the ticket delete with the pending-row delete in one transaction keyed on ticketId: DELETE FROM modmail_ticket WHERE id = ? AND thread_id IS NULL AND status='open', or (b) defer createTicket until after the Discord thread exists (only the 'pending' open_modmail row needs to be inserted in the locking transaction). Also avoid classifying a modmail_ticket unique-index violation as a 'race' that links to a non-existent open_modmail row.

title: closed_at parsed with new Date() treats SQLite's space-separated UTC timestamp as local time, skewing the 7-day reopen window
detail: closeTicket (tickets.ts:165) writes closed_at via datetime('now'), which yields a string like '2026-05-31 12:00:00' — UTC with a SPACE separator and NO 'Z'/offset. At line 73, closedAt = new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime(). Per ECMAScript, a non-ISO, space-separated datetime string is parsed in the host LOCAL time zone, not UTC (only the 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ' ISO form is guaranteed UTC). So the computed epoch is shifted by the server's UTC offset (up to ~14h). The threshold 'now - closedAt > 7 days' (line 77) therefore decides reopen-vs-new-thread using a time that is off by the offset: on a server west of UTC it makes the window effectively longer (reopens threads that are actually older than 7 days), east of UTC effectively shorter. The team already KNOWS this exact pitfall: web/src/lib/server/queries/shared.ts normalizeTimestamp() comments 'SQLite datetime(now) returns YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC, no Z suffix). new Date() parses space-separated formats as local time — normalize to ISO8601 UTC' and the dashboard modmail query uses it. This reopen path (and the identical dashboardBridge.ts:304) bypass that normalization. Tests miss it because the fixtures feed closed_at via Date.toISOString() (threadReopen.test.ts:191/255/286), i.e. proper ISO with 'Z', which never reproduces the space-separated production format.
fix: Normalize before parsing, mirroring shared.ts: const iso = ticket.closed_at.includes('T') ? ticket.closed_at : ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'; const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(iso).getTime() : 0; (or store closed_at as a unix epoch via strftime('%s','now') consistently). Apply the same fix to src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304.

title: reopenTicket can violate the open-ticket partial unique index if another open ticket already exists for the user
detail: The reopen transaction calls reopenTicket(ticket.id) (sets status='open', tickets.ts:177). There is a partial unique index idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id,user_id,status) WHERE status='open' (db.ts:195-198). If, between this ticket's close and the reopen, a different open modmail_ticket was created for the same (guild_id,user_id) (e.g. a brand-new thread was opened, then a stale closed ticket is reopened via /reopen by user lookup which selects the most recent CLOSED row, lines 46-56), flipping the old row to 'open' produces two status='open' rows for the same user and trips the unique index, aborting the transaction. The user-facing result is the generic 'Failed to reopen modmail thread' (line 153). Lower likelihood because the open_modmail guard usually prevents a second concurrently-open ticket, but the reopen-by-userId path does not verify the user has no other currently-open ticket before flipping status.
fix: Before reopenTicket, assert there is no other open ticket for (guild_id,user_id) (SELECT ... WHERE status='open' AND id != ticket.id) and refuse with a clear message, or catch the constraint error specifically and report 'user already has an open modmail thread'.

title: clearStaleAcknowledgments deletes ALL acks when validKeys is empty (json_each NOT IN empty set)
detail: clearStaleAcknowledgments runs `DELETE ... WHERE guild_id = ? AND issue_key NOT IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`. When `validKeys` is empty, `keysJson` is '[]', so `json_each('[]')` yields zero rows and `issue_key NOT IN (<empty>)` is TRUE for every row -> every acknowledgment for the guild is deleted. The sole caller (src/features/serverAuditDocs.ts:76-77) builds `validKeys = new Set(issues.map(i => i.issueKey))` from analyzeSecurityIssues(). If a transient/partial Discord fetch (fetchRoles/fetchChannels) yields incomplete data so analyze produces zero issues, every previously-acknowledged issue is permanently wiped, and on the next clean audit those issues reappear as un-acknowledged 'new' warnings, spamming staff. (For a genuinely clean server with no issues this delete is harmless because there is nothing left to ack, so impact is limited to the partial-fetch / analyzer-regression case.)
fix: Guard the empty case: `if (validKeys.size === 0) return 0;` before running the delete, and/or only run the cleanup when the audit fetch is known to be complete (e.g., roles/channels arrays non-empty). Alternatively skip the prune when issues.length === 0 in serverAuditDocs.ts.

title: getAcknowledgedIssues returns the shared mutable cached Map reference
detail: On a cache hit (line 140-143) and on a miss the same `result` Map is both stored in ackCache and returned to the caller. Any caller that mutates the returned Map (set/delete/clear) would silently corrupt the cached entry for up to CACHE_TTL_MS (5 min), affecting subsequent /audit security runs for that guild. Current callers (serverAudit/docs.ts partitionIssues, audit/acknowledge*.ts) only read via .get(), so this is latent rather than live, but it is a footgun for future callers and for listAcknowledgedIssues semantics.
fix: Return a defensive copy (e.g., `return new Map(cached)`), or document/freeze the contract that the returned Map is read-only.

title: getServiceToggles uses `row.service in toggles`, which also matches Object.prototype keys
detail: The loop does `if (row.service in toggles) { toggles[row.service as AIDetectionService] = ... }`. The `in` operator walks the prototype chain, so a stored service value of 'constructor', 'toString', 'hasOwnProperty', '__proto__', etc. would pass the guard and assign onto toggles, polluting the returned record (and via getEnabledServices, the enabled-services list). The ai_detection_toggles table (migration 037) has no CHECK constraint on `service`; the only sanctioned writer is setServiceEnabled typed to AIDetectionService, so this requires a corrupt/hand-edited row to trigger -- hence low severity, but it is a real input-validation gap.
fix: Use an own-property / allowlist check: `if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(toggles, row.service))` or `if (ALL_SERVICES.includes(row.service as AIDetectionService))`.

title: isServiceEnabled treats any DB error as 'enabled', risking unintended paid-API spend
detail: isServiceEnabled wraps the query in `try { ... } catch { return true; }`. The comment intends this only for the pre-migration 'table missing' case, but the bare catch also swallows transient errors (e.g., 'database is locked', a column rename/typo, a prepared-statement handle error after reconnection). In those cases a service an admin explicitly DISABLED is reported as ENABLED, so the AI-detection pipeline will call that external API (Hive/RapidAI/Sightengine/Optic) and incur cost the admin tried to avoid. Fail-open on a cost/safety toggle is the wrong default for anything but the known 'no such table' error.
fix: Narrow the catch: inspect the error and only default to true for a missing-table error (e.g., message includes 'no such table'); for other errors log and default to disabled (fail-closed) or rethrow.

title: generateReportData can throw on missing table while sibling readers return safe defaults
detail: getFindingsByRun/getFindingsBySeverity/listAuditRuns each wrap their query in try/catch and return [] on error (e.g., audit_findings table absent pre-migration). generateReportData calls getStatusCountsStmt.all(), getApiTotalsStmt.get(), getDocIssuesStmt.all(), getPermMismatchesStmt.all() WITHOUT try/catch, so the same missing-table/locked-db condition that the other functions tolerate will throw out of generateReportData. Also getApiTotalsStmt.get() is cast `as {total_calls;total_cost}` and dereferenced at lines 293-294 without a null guard; .get() returns undefined for an empty/absent result, which would throw on property access. Impact is limited because no src/ runtime path calls generateReportData (only scripts/tests), but it is an inconsistent contract that can crash an admin/script caller.
fix: Wrap the four statement calls in try/catch returning the same zeroed ReportData defaults the rest of the module uses, and null-guard the apiTotals result (`apiTotals?.total_calls ?? 0`).

title: Unsound cast of raw row to AuditSession (audit_type/status unions not enforced by schema)
detail: getActiveSession casts the better-sqlite3 row directly to `AuditSession`, whose audit_type is 'members'|'nsfw' and status is 'in_progress'|'completed'|'cancelled'. The audit_sessions table (migration 033) declares audit_type and status as plain TEXT with no CHECK constraint, so the compile-time union is not guaranteed at runtime. Any out-of-band write produces a value TypeScript believes is impossible, and downstream switch/exhaustiveness logic on audit_type could mis-handle it. Practically the only writer (createSession) is typed, so impact is low.
fix: Either add CHECK(audit_type IN ('members','nsfw')) / CHECK(status IN (...)) to the table, or validate the row's audit_type/status against the allowed sets before returning instead of a blind `as` cast.

title: Movie tier count includes game-night attendance (cross-event-type contamination)
detail: getUserQualifiedMovieCount() counts every qualified row in movie_attendance for the user with NO event_type filter (WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND qualified=1). Game nights (src/features/events/gameNight.ts) persist into the SAME movie_attendance table with event_type='game' (finalizeGameAttendance, lines 247-253). This count is the basis for movie tier-role promotion in updateMovieTierRole (movieNight.ts:391). Result: a user who qualifies only for game nights is granted Movie-Night tier roles (and the reverse: getUserTotalEventCount in gameNight.ts:344 is also unfiltered). The economy/role-reward is inflated and wrong. Note gameNight.ts:331 getUserQualifiedGameCount correctly filters event_type='game', proving the movie side simply forgot the filter.
fix: Add AND event_type = 'movie' to getUserQualifiedMovieCount (and decide intended semantics for getUserTotalEventCount). e.g. SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND event_type='movie' AND qualified=1.

title: Movie and game attendance collide on UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,event_date); same-day REPLACE drops a row
detail: movie_attendance has UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,event_date) (migrations/025_role_automation.ts:111) and event_type was added later with DEFAULT 'movie' (migration 040). finalizeMovieAttendance writes via INSERT OR REPLACE without specifying event_type (so it defaults to 'movie'), while finalizeGameAttendance (gameNight.ts:247) writes the same key with event_type='game'. The UNIQUE key does NOT include event_type, so if the same user attends both a movie night and a game night on the same calendar date, the second finalize REPLACEs (deletes+reinserts) the first event's row entirely. One event's attendance/qualification is silently lost. The manual-adjust helpers (creditHistoricalAttendance ON CONFLICT, bumpAttendance) have the same key collision.
fix: Include event_type in the uniqueness model: change the constraint to UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,event_date,event_type) (new migration) and update all ON CONFLICT targets to match; or incorporate event_type into a synthetic key. Until then movie and game nights cannot safely share a date.

title: Crash recovery loads game-night sessions into the movie session map
detail: recoverPersistedSessions() reads active_movie_events and active_movie_sessions with NO event_type filter, even though those tables are shared with game nights (gameNight.ts persists rows with event_type='game'). gameNight.recoverPersistedGameSessions (gameNight.ts:444,467) correctly filters WHERE event_type='game', but the movie recovery does not. After a restart, game-night active events/sessions are loaded into movieSessions/activeEvents and will be treated as movie attendance (e.g. surfaced by /movie resume, finalized as movie rows). Both recovery paths run at startup, so the game rows get pulled into both maps.
fix: Filter the movie recovery queries to event_type='movie' (or IS NULL for legacy rows): add WHERE event_type='movie' to both SELECTs in recoverPersistedSessions, mirroring gameNight.ts.

title: finalizeMovieAttendance clears ALL guilds' in-memory sessions
detail: After persisting the ending guild's rows, finalizeMovieAttendance calls movieSessions.clear() which wipes sessions for EVERY guild, not just guild.id. The code comment acknowledges this and assumes a single active guild. If two guilds run movie nights concurrently, ending one event discards the other guild's in-progress in-memory tracking (it would be partially recoverable from the periodic DB persist, but any minutes since the last 5-min checkpoint for the still-active guild are lost, and its in-memory state is gone until next persist/reconcile).
fix: Delete only this guild's keys: for (const key of [...movieSessions.keys()]) if (key.startsWith(guild.id+":")) movieSessions.delete(key); — matching the per-guild deletion gameNight.ts:305-309 already uses.

title: event_type='movie' missing on movie writes makes legacy/movie rows indistinguishable from intent
detail: All movie writes (finalizeMovieAttendance INSERT OR REPLACE, creditHistoricalAttendance, bumpAttendance) omit the event_type column and rely on the table DEFAULT 'movie'. This works for fresh inserts, but combined with the unfiltered movie reads it means there is no explicit tagging of movie rows; any future change to the default, or an UPDATE path, can silently mislabel rows. Game-night code always specifies event_type explicitly. Inconsistent handling is the root enabler of the cross-type bugs above.
fix: Explicitly write event_type='movie' in all movie INSERT/REPLACE statements so intent is encoded in the row, not just the column default.

title: notify_cooldown_seconds / notify_max_per_hour of 0 silently coerced to defaults
detail: getNotifyConfig uses `row.notify_cooldown_seconds || 5` and `row.notify_max_per_hour || 10`. A legitimately configured value of 0 (admin wanting no cooldown, or a hard 0/hour disable) is falsy and replaced by the default. notifyLimiter.canNotify (src/lib/notifyLimiter.ts:75-76) repeats the same `|| 5` / `|| 10`, so a 0 can never take effect. Impact is limited (0 cooldown vs 5s; 0/hour can't disable pings), but the configured intent is not honored.
fix: Use nullish coalescing for the numeric defaults: `row.notify_cooldown_seconds ?? 5` and `row.notify_max_per_hour ?? 10`, here and in notifyLimiter, so an explicit 0 is preserved.

title: getWsPing treats a genuine 0ms ping as unavailable (-1)
detail: getWsPing returns -1 when `!_cachedClient.ws.ping`. discord.js reports -1 before the first heartbeat (the intended 'unknown' case), but a 0 value is also falsy and would be reported as -1. More relevantly, the WS-ping alert check (runCheck, line 394) guards with `summary.wsPingMs > 0`, so the -1 sentinel is handled there; the only impact is the dashboard summary showing -1 instead of 0 in the unlikely 0ms case. Minor display correctness issue.
fix: Distinguish unknown from zero: `const p = _cachedClient?.ws.ping; return (typeof p === 'number' && p >= 0) ? p : -1;`

title: Scheduler-health assertions are guarded by `if (schedulersField)`, so the test passes vacuously if the field disappears
detail: The test 'shows scheduler status when schedulers are tracked' mocks getSchedulerHealth() to return a 2-entry Map, then locates the embed field named 'Schedulers' and only runs its expect() calls inside `if (schedulersField) { ... }`. If a regression in src/commands/health.ts caused the Schedulers field to stop being emitted (e.g., the `if (schedulerHealthMap.size > 0)` block were removed or the field renamed), `schedulersField` would be undefined, the if-block would be skipped, and the test would still report PASS with zero assertions executed. The test therefore does not actually protect the behavior it is named for. (It happens to run the assertions today only because the current implementation does emit the field.)
fix: Assert the field exists before inspecting it: `expect(schedulersField).toBeDefined();` then drop the `if` guard and assert `schedulersField.value` contains 'modMetrics' and 'opsHealth' unconditionally. Optionally also assert the WARN/failure formatting for the opsHealth entry (consecutiveFailures: 2).

title: Gatekeeper-denial tests only assert the guard was *called*, never that the command aborted — an inverted/removed authz check would not be caught
detail: The 'denies access when user lacks gatekeeper role' test sets requireGatekeeper -> false and then asserts only `expect(requireGatekeeper).toHaveBeenCalled()`. It never asserts that the privileged work was skipped (e.g., that findAppByShortCode / approveTx were NOT invoked, or that no approval reply was produced). Because the denial message is produced inside requireGatekeeper itself (which is mocked away), the test has no observable post-condition for the abort. Consequence: if src/commands/gate/accept.ts regressed to `if (requireGatekeeper(...)) return;` (inverted) or dropped the early `return`, an unprivileged user could drive the approval flow and the suite would stay green. The identical weak pattern appears in the sibling gate-command tests, all on security-critical authz paths: gate/reject.test.ts (127-144), gate/kick.test.ts (137-146), gate/unclaim.test.ts (130-139), and gateMain.test.ts (202-209, requireStaff).
fix: After the guarded execute() call, also assert the command short-circuited: e.g. `expect(findAppByShortCode).not.toHaveBeenCalled();` and `expect(approveTx).not.toHaveBeenCalled();` (and the analogous tx/lookup mocks for reject/kick/unclaim/gate). This makes an inverted or removed guard fail the test.

title: Subcommand-routing tests assert only the outer `route_subcommand` step, which fires for every subcommand — the assertion is tautological
detail: execute() in src/commands/gate/gateMain.ts wraps the entire switch in `withStep(ctx, 'route_subcommand', ...)`, so ctx.step is called with 'route_subcommand' for EVERY subcommand and group. The test 'routes to welcome preview subcommand' (and the comment claims it verifies welcome-preview routing) asserts `expect(ctx.step).toHaveBeenCalledWith('route_subcommand')`, which would pass for setup, reset, status, set-questions, or any other branch — it does not verify that the preview path specifically ran. It provides no protection against the preview branch being mis-wired. (Contrast with the status/config tests at 211-225, which assert branch-specific steps like 'query_stats'/'load_config' and are meaningful.)
fix: Assert a step or side-effect unique to executeWelcomePreview, e.g. spy on renderWelcomeTemplate and `expect(renderWelcomeTemplate).toHaveBeenCalled()`, or assert a preview-specific withStep phase ('render_preview').

title: shared re-export contract test omits four exports that gate commands actually import (tryEnqueueWelcome, hasRoleOrAbove, ROLE_IDS, shouldBypass)
detail: This file's stated purpose (header) is to 'Verify all expected exports are available and correctly re-exported.' It checks ~24 names but misses tryEnqueueWelcome (consumed by src/commands/gate/accept.ts) and hasRoleOrAbove / ROLE_IDS / shouldBypass (consumed by src/commands/gate/unclaim.ts), all of which are re-exported from src/commands/gate/shared.ts (lines 13-16, 44). If any of those re-exports were dropped from shared.ts, this 'exports' contract suite would stay green while accept.ts/unclaim.ts break at runtime, defeating the file's purpose. Impact is limited because the per-command tests mock shared.js wholesale and would also miss it, but the dedicated contract test is exactly where this should be caught.
fix: Add `expect(shared.tryEnqueueWelcome).toBeTypeOf('function')`, `expect(shared.hasRoleOrAbove).toBeTypeOf('function')`, `expect(shared.shouldBypass).toBeTypeOf('function')`, and `expect(shared.ROLE_IDS).toBeDefined()` to the exports suite.

title: Cross-ref: accept.ts mislabels analytics `via` as "code" for the user-mention path; no test covers the mention path's meta, so the bug is invisible
detail: In the cross-referenced callee src/commands/gate/accept.ts line 336, updateReviewActionMeta is called with `via: uidRaw ? 'uid' : 'code'`. accept supports three identifiers (app code, user mention, uid). When an app is resolved via the `user` mention option, uidRaw is null, so `via` is recorded as 'code' even though no short code was used — an analytics mislabel of how the approval was initiated. src/commands/gate/reject.ts (lines 213, 221) has the identical `uidRaw ? 'uid' : 'code'` mislabel for its mention path. The accept.test.ts 'accepts by user mention' test (281-316) asserts only that findPendingAppByUserId/approveTx were called and never inspects the updateReviewActionMeta `via` argument, so this defect is fully uncovered. Reported as a cross-reference because the bug lives in callee files outside this bucket; impact is limited to analytics fidelity, not control flow.
fix: In accept.ts/reject.ts, derive `via` from which option was actually supplied: `via: codeRaw ? 'code' : userOption ? 'mention' : 'uid'`. Then add an assertion in the mention test verifying `updateReviewActionMeta` received `expect.objectContaining({ via: 'mention' })`.

title: claimedAtToDate/claimedAtToEpoch mis-parse the actual stored claimed_at format (epoch-seconds string) -> Invalid Date / NaN
detail: These helpers do `new Date(claimed_at)` and `new Date(claimed_at).getTime()/1000`, and their JSDoc/param type declare claimed_at as an "ISO timestamp string". But the value is never ISO: review_claim.claimed_at is a TEXT column (src/db/db.ts:132) and claimTx (src/features/reviewActions.ts:114) inserts nowUtc(), which returns epoch SECONDS as a number (src/lib/time.ts:34 `Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)`). SQLite stores that as a numeric string like "1748600000". `new Date("1748600000")` yields Invalid Date, so claimedAtToDate returns Invalid Date and claimedAtToEpoch returns NaN. The real card consumer sidesteps them with a custom parser (src/ui/reviewCard.ts parseClaimedAt, which explicitly notes the DB "may contain numeric strings from nowUtc()"). A grep shows claimedAtToEpoch/claimedAtToDate are defined but never called anywhere in src/tests/web, so today this is dead code -- but it is a latent trap: any future caller trusting the JSDoc ("ISO timestamp string") will silently get NaN/Invalid Date for every claim.
fix: Make the helpers tolerant of epoch-seconds numeric strings (and epoch ms), e.g. detect an all-digit string and treat it as seconds: `const n = Number(claimed_at); const ms = Number.isFinite(n) ? (n < 1e12 ? n*1000 : n) : Date.parse(claimed_at); return new Date(ms);`. Alternatively delete the unused helpers and standardize on parseClaimedAt. Also correct the ReviewClaimRow.claimed_at type/comment which claims ISO but is actually an epoch-seconds string.

title: Panic-mode claim error mis-parses ClaimError message, showing "application is already **is**"
detail: For an INVALID_STATUS ClaimError the handler builds the user message via `err.message.split(" ")[2]`. This assumes the message is exactly `Application already <status>` (reviewActions.ts:82), where token[2] is the status -> correct for terminal states. But claimTx ALSO throws INVALID_STATUS for panic mode with message "Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended." (reviewActions.ts:62). split(" ")[2] of that is "is", so a moderator clicking Claim while panic mode is active sees: "Cannot claim: application is already **is**." -- nonsensical and hides the real (panic) reason. It also needlessly calls ensureReviewMessage to "refresh" for a non-status condition.
fix: Stop string-slicing err.message. Either add a dedicated error code for panic mode (e.g. PANIC_MODE) or pass the status in a structured field on ClaimError and branch on it. At minimum, special-case the panic message text before the generic INVALID_STATUS branch.

title: Claim 'success' posts a public follow-up on every claim instead of editing the card (misleading comment + channel noise)
detail: The parent handleReviewButton always calls deferUpdate() before handleClaimToggle (src/features/review/handlers/buttons.ts:177-188). After deferUpdate() on a ButtonInteraction, interaction.replied === true (deferred stays false). replyOrEdit (src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:507-509) therefore takes the `replied` branch and calls followUp(). The payload here passes no flags, so withFlags defaults flags to 0 (public) (cmdWrap.ts:500). Net effect: every successful claim posts a NEW public message "<@mod> has claimed this application." into the review channel. The inline comment says "Update the review card message content to show who claimed it", but followUp does not edit the card at all -- the card is already separately refreshed two lines earlier via ensureReviewMessage(), so this public follow-up is duplicate noise rather than a card edit. By contrast the unclaim success path correctly uses MessageFlags.Ephemeral (claimHandlers.ts:243-245).
fix: If a confirmation is wanted, make it ephemeral (add flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral) like the unclaim path; the public claim state is already conveyed by the refreshed card. If a public note is genuinely desired, edit the card / post intentionally and fix the misleading comment.

title: Inconsistent optional chaining on member.user can throw TypeError in welcome rendering
detail: In postWelcomeMessage the applicant tag is computed as `member.user?.tag ?? member.user.username`. The first operand guards member.user with optional chaining, but the fallback `member.user.username` does not. If member.user is ever null/undefined, `member.user?.tag` is undefined and the `??` then evaluates `member.user.username`, throwing "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'username')". That exception would propagate out of the custom-template branch and abort posting the welcome (the surrounding try/catch is only around channel.send, not this expression). On a GuildMember user is effectively always populated, so this is latent, but the code is internally inconsistent (one operand guards, the other doesn't).
fix: Use a fully-guarded cascade, e.g. `member.user?.tag ?? member.user?.username ?? member.displayName ?? member.id`, mirroring the safe fallback already used in buildDefaultWelcomeMessage (welcome.ts:147).

title: Cleanup setInterval is never unref'd or cleared — keeps the event loop alive (hangs tests/shutdown)
detail: At module load, rateLimiter.ts calls `setInterval(cleanupOldCooldowns, CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS)` (10 min) and never calls `.unref()` on the returned timer, nor stores it for clearing, nor guards on a test env. By contrast, cmdWrap.ts (armWatchdog, line ~192) correctly does `timer.unref()`. A live, ref'd interval keeps the Node process alive. This is exercised by my bucket: tests/commands/listopen.test.ts imports src/commands/listopen.js, which imports rateLimiter (`checkCooldown`, `clearCooldown`, `COOLDOWNS`). The module's own comment even admits this: 'This interval is never cleared, so this module can't be cleanly unloaded ... If tests start hanging, this is why.' Impact: vitest workers may not exit cleanly (forces teardown timeout / --forceExit reliance), and in production it blocks graceful shutdown.
fix: Capture the handle and unref it, mirroring cmdWrap.ts: `const t = setInterval(cleanupOldCooldowns, CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS); if (typeof t.unref === 'function') t.unref();`. Optionally export a `stopCleanup()` that clears it for deterministic test teardown.

title: handleHelpButton switch has no `case "search"` — search navigation falls through to 'Unknown navigation'
detail: parseHelpCustomId can return `{ type: "search", query, nonce }` for any customId matching `^help:search:([a-f0-9]+)$` (metadata.ts lines 257-264). In handleHelpButton the switch handles overview/category/command/search_modal and a default branch, but there is NO `case "search"`. If a button with id `help:search:<hex>` were ever clicked, the user would get 'Unknown navigation. Please use /help to start over.' Currently this is latent: components.ts only emits `help:search:modal` for buttons and uses the nonce form for the SELECT menu (`help:select:search:<nonce>`), so no button produces the bare `help:search:<nonce>` id today. It is a real unreachable/forgotten branch that will silently break if a future component starts emitting that id. Compounding it, the bucket's own test (tests/commands/help/index.test.ts) never exercises the `search` nav type in handleHelpButton, so the gap is invisible to the suite.
fix: Either add an explicit `case "search": ... break;` (e.g., reload the cached session via getSearchSession(nav.nonce) and re-render) or, if bare search buttons are intentionally unsupported, drop the `search` arm from the HelpNavigation parse path for buttons and document it. Add a button-handler test covering a `help:search:<nonce>` id.

title: 7-day reopen window parses SQLite UTC timestamp as local time
detail: closed_at is written by closeTicket() in tickets.ts via SQLite datetime('now'), which yields a space-separated UTC string like "2026-05-31 12:34:56" with no timezone marker (confirmed: db.ts line 187 `closed_at TEXT`, and closeTicket uses `datetime('now')`). At threadReopen.ts:73 this is parsed with `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. Node/V8 parses non-ISO, space-separated datetime strings as LOCAL time, not UTC. The comparison `now - closedAt > sevenDays` (lines 74-77) is therefore skewed by the host's UTC offset. On a server several hours behind UTC, a freshly-closed ticket can compute a NEGATIVE elapsed time (closedAt appears in the future) and on a server ahead of UTC the window is shortened. Impact: the boundary between 'reopen in place' and 'create a brand-new thread' (lines 78-85) is off by the offset, so tickets near the 7-day edge are mis-routed. Not exploitable, but a genuine boundary/timezone bug.
fix: Parse as UTC explicitly. Either store/read epoch seconds, or normalize: `const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z').getTime() : 0;`. Best: make SQLite emit ISO-Z (e.g. strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')) or unixepoch() and parse consistently.

title: reopenTicket can violate partial unique index when user has a newer open ticket
detail: db.ts defines `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id, user_id, status) WHERE status='open'` (db.ts:195-198), enforcing at most one open ticket per (guild,user). reopenModmailThread's user-based lookup (threadReopen.ts:44-57) explicitly selects the most recent ticket WHERE status='closed'. If, after that ticket was closed, a NEW modmail was opened for the same user (a normal sequence), that new ticket is already status='open'. reopenTicket() then runs `UPDATE ... SET status='open'` on the old closed ticket inside the db.transaction at threadReopen.ts:89-109, which collides with the partial unique index and throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT. The transaction rolls back and the catch at threadReopen.ts:150-154 returns a generic 'Failed to reopen modmail thread. Check logs.' Impact: staff get an opaque failure (and a logged error/Sentry capture) instead of a clear 'user already has an open modmail' message; the real cause is hidden. The guard-table UPSERT in the same transaction would also have pointed the open_modmail row at the wrong (old) thread had the UPDATE succeeded.
fix: Before reopening by userId, check for an existing open ticket (getOpenTicketByUser) and short-circuit with a clear message linking the existing thread; otherwise catch SQLITE_CONSTRAINT specifically in reopenModmailThread and surface 'This user already has an open modmail thread.'

title: User DM transcript (on auto-close) uses only in-memory buffer; empty after a restart while log channel gets full transcript
detail: closeModmailForApplication captures the user-facing transcript at lines 500-503 strictly from the in-memory buffer (getTranscriptBuffer(ticketId)); if the buffer is empty it sets userTranscriptText=null and attaches no file to the applicant DM (lines 588-595). However flushTranscript (transcript.ts:126-160) falls back to reconstructing the transcript from the modmail_message table when the in-memory buffer is empty (e.g. after a bot restart mid-conversation). Result: after a restart, the log channel receives the complete DB-reconstructed transcript but the applicant's closure DM silently omits the conversation copy it promises ('A copy of your conversation is attached below.'). Inconsistent and surprising for an audit/compliance feature, though not corrupting data.
fix: Reconstruct the user transcript from modmail_message (same query flushTranscript uses) when the in-memory buffer is empty, instead of attaching nothing; or fetch the buffer/DB lines once and reuse for both the DM and the flush.

title: Close button posts public message into a channel that may have just been deleted
detail: On a successful close, handleModmailCloseButton sends result.message to interaction.channel (lines 162-167). For the in-thread Close button, interaction.channel IS the modmail thread, but closeModmailThread deletes that thread when modmail_delete_on_close is not false (the default true) — see threadClose.ts:363-371 which calls threadForCleanup.delete(). So the subsequent send targets a deleted channel and always throws (swallowed by the try/catch at 168-170). Effectively dead in the delete-on-close path: the success/log-URL message the code intends to surface publicly is never posted. Functionally harmless because deferUpdate already acked the interaction, but the intended user feedback is silently lost.
fix: Only post the public close message when the thread was archived (not deleted), or post it to the parent channel; gate on the archive action returned from closeModmailThread, or skip the channel.send when interaction.channel is the closed thread.

title: Unreachable null branch in lensUrl ternary
detail: avatarUrl is set from user.displayAvatarURL({ size: 128 }) (line 364), which always returns a non-empty CDN URL string, never null/empty. The ternary at lines 369-371 (`avatarUrl ? ... : null`) therefore always takes the truthy branch; the `: null` and the later `if (lensUrl)` guard (line 389) are effectively dead. No runtime impact, but misleading defensive code.
fix: Drop the ternary and unconditionally build lensUrl from the encoded avatarUrl, or remove the dead null branch/guard.

title: Default mockAll return value is unreachable; per-action count assertions are vacuous
detail: The default mock is `mockAll.mockImplementation((query) => { if (typeof query === "string") return []; return [{action:"approve",cnt:80},{action:"reject",cnt:15},{action:"kick",cnt:5}]; })`. The intent is that the per-action counts query returns the approve/reject/kick array. But in the source (src/commands/stats/history.ts lines 111-118) the counts query is built as `db.prepare(SQL).all(moderator.id, guildId, fromTimestamp)` — the SQL string is the argument to db.prepare(), and the FIRST argument passed to `.all()` is always `moderator.id` (the string "mod-user-123"). The test's withSql mock passes the SQL string as `_sql` and ignores it, invoking `fn()` which calls `.all(moderator.id, ...)`. Therefore the `query` parameter the mock inspects is ALWAYS the actor-id string, so `typeof query === "string"` is ALWAYS true and the mock ALWAYS returns []. The `[{approve:80}...]` branch is dead code. Consequence: in every test using the default beforeEach (e.g. 'embed contains approvals and rejections' L347, 'embed contains reject rate' L361), `counts` is always {} and computed Approvals/Rejections/Reject-Rate values are 0/0.0. Those tests only assert the field NAMES exist (toContainEqual with name only, never value), so they pass regardless and would NOT catch a regression that mis-computes approval/rejection counts or reject rate. This is a false sense of coverage on the command's core numeric output.
fix: Make the mock branch on the SQL text rather than the bound parameters, e.g. set per-call implementations via the prepared SQL: have `mockPrepare.mockImplementation((sql) => ({ get: mockGet, all: (...args) => routeBySql(sql, args) }))` and key the returned rows off `sql` (counts vs response_ms vs daily). Then add value assertions like `expect(fields.find(f=>f.name==="Approvals").value).toBe("80")` so the count math is actually exercised.

title: 'CSV contains correct header row' test asserts nothing about the header
detail: The test is named 'CSV contains correct header row' and includes the comment 'AttachmentBuilder stores the data - need to access it', but the only assertion is `expect(attachment).toBeDefined()`. It never decodes the AttachmentBuilder buffer nor checks the header string. The handler (src/commands/stats/export.ts L116) emits a specific header 'Moderator ID,Total Decisions,Approvals,...'; if that header were reordered, renamed, or dropped, this test would still pass. It provides no protection for the behavior its name claims.
fix: Read the attachment payload (e.g. `(attachment.attachment as Buffer).toString('utf-8')`) and assert it `.startsWith('Moderator ID,Total Decisions,Approvals,Rejections,Modmail,Perm Reject,Kicks,Avg Response Time (seconds),Avg Response Time (formatted)')`, plus assert a sample data row is present. Or delete the test if redundant.

title: Filename-format assertion can never fail because AttachmentBuilder.name is unset under the partial mock
detail: The test asserts `attachment.name` matches /^stats-full-export-30d-\d+\.csv$/. The shared-module mock imports the REAL AttachmentBuilder from discord.js (L25), and the source passes `{ name: ... }` to its constructor, so for the real class `attachment.name` is the getter returning the configured name — this currently works. However the sibling assertions elsewhere read `call.files[0].name` the same way, so it is load-bearing that the real AttachmentBuilder is used. If a future refactor swaps to a stubbed AttachmentBuilder (as several other stats tests stub builders), `attachment.name` would be undefined and `expect(undefined).toMatch(...)` would throw rather than fail cleanly. Lower confidence because it passes today; flagging the fragility because the test relies on importActual for a value it then regex-matches without a guard.
fix: Guard the access, e.g. `expect(typeof attachment.name).toBe('string')` before the `.toMatch`, or assert against the constructor input via a spy on AttachmentBuilder so the test is independent of which build of the class is in scope.

title: Unused afterEach import
detail: `afterEach` is imported from vitest (L8) but never used anywhere in the file (unlike reset.test.ts which uses it for timer teardown). Harmless at runtime but indicates leftover scaffolding; under a strict noUnusedLocals/eslint config this would fail the lint/build gate.
fix: Remove `afterEach` from the import list.

title: getAvgClaimToDecision / getAvgSubmitToFirstClaim SQL is never actually exercised by any test
detail: shared.test.ts only asserts these two functions are `typeof === 'function'` (lines 145-157) and explicitly documents (lines 142-144) that they are 'tested indirectly through the command handler tests that mock the shared module'. But stats/user.test.ts ALSO mocks them (user.test.ts lines 39-41 replace them with vi.fn()). The net result is that the real bodies of getAvgClaimToDecision/getAvgSubmitToFirstClaim in src/commands/stats/shared.ts (lines 60-132) — including their multi-CTE action_log JOIN SQL and the `c.claim_time < d.decision_time` / `c.claim_time > s.submit_time` guards — are executed by zero tests. A regression in that SQL (e.g. flipping the inequality, dropping a bind param, the INNER JOIN losing rows) would pass the entire suite green. This is a real coverage blind spot on the moderator-performance metric, not a wrong assertion.
fix: Add a focused test that imports shared.ts WITHOUT mocking db (use an in-memory better-sqlite3 with a small action_log fixture, like tests/config.test.ts does) and asserts the computed averages for known claim/decision/submit timestamps, including the boundary where claim_time == decision_time (should be excluded).

title: Permission test does not assert the `requirements` hierarchy clause, so an authz regression can slip through
detail: The handler src/commands/stats/user.ts (lines 47-51) gates on requireMinRole with options that include `requirements: [{ type: 'hierarchy', minRoleId: ROLE_IDS.GATEKEEPER }]`. The test 'calls requireMinRole with GATEKEEPER role' (lines 118-133) asserts only objectContaining({ command, description }). Because objectContaining ignores extra/missing sibling keys it does not assert the second positional arg (minRoleId === 'role-gatekeeper') beyond the loose match, nor the requirements array. If someone changed the min role or dropped the hierarchy requirement, this test would still pass. Several timing/field tests (e.g. lines 306-319, 321-334) also assert field values that come straight from the mocked formatDuration return, so they validate the mock rather than real formatting.
fix: Tighten the assertion to check the exact second arg (ROLE_IDS.GATEKEEPER) and include requirements in the expected object; for the formatDuration field tests, drive them through the real formatDuration (it is pure) instead of a hard-coded mockReturnValue so the embed-formatting path is actually verified.

title: CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS on a fixed-path file DB is not crash-safe across an aborted run
detail: beforeEach (lines 32-61) opens a file DB at a fixed path tests/test-config.db and runs `CREATE TABLE guild_config (...)` with no IF NOT EXISTS / DROP. afterEach (lines 65-70) closes and unlinks it. Within a normal run this is fine and the suite is green. But if a previous run was killed (CI cancel, crash) after creating the file but before afterEach unlinked it, the next run's first beforeEach will throw 'table guild_config already exists' and every test in the file fails until the stray .db is manually removed. The neighboring stores it nominally backstops (flagger/logging) use guild_config too, so a poisoned file is plausible. Low impact because it self-heals once cleaned, and no parallel file collides on this exact path.
fix: Use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` plus an explicit `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS guild_config` at the top of beforeEach, or switch to an in-memory DB (':memory:') / a unique temp path per run via os.tmpdir()+randomUUID so a leftover file can never break the next run.

title: env.test.ts schema has drifted from src/lib/env.ts and asserts the OPPOSITE of real behavior (false confidence)
detail: This test defines its OWN local `envSchema` (lines 30-38) and never imports the real schema from src/lib/env.ts. Two concrete drifts make the test misleading: (1) NODE_ENV. The local enum is z.enum(["development", "production"]) (line 34). The REAL schema (src/lib/env.ts line 118) is z.enum(["development", "production", "test"]). The test's comments and intent explicitly assert that "test" is REJECTED — line 28 ("no 'staging', 'test', etc."), line 94 ("NODE_ENV must be exactly 'development' or 'production'"), line 96 ("Other values like 'staging', 'test', 'local' are rejected"). The real schema ACCEPTS "test". So the only NODE_ENV-negative test uses "staging" (line 101), which happens to fail in both, hiding the drift. (2) RESET_PASSWORD. The real schema requires RESET_PASSWORD (src/lib/env.ts line 136, .min(1)). The local schema omits it entirely, so the 'complete environment' (line 41) and 'apply default values' (line 61) cases pass here but would FAIL against the real schema. Net impact: a real regression to env validation (e.g., someone removing the RESET_PASSWORD requirement, or restricting NODE_ENV to drop 'test' and breaking the test run-mode at src/lib/env.ts line 32 `process.env.NODE_ENV === "test"`) would not be caught by this suite. The test gives false confidence that env validation is verified.
fix: Import and test the actual schema/env module instead of a hand-maintained copy (e.g., export the zod schema from src/lib/env.ts and import it here, or drive process.env + dynamic import of env.ts). At minimum, sync the local enum to include "test", add RESET_PASSWORD to the local object/required-field tests, and fix the now-incorrect comments at lines 28/94/96.

title: Hive tests re-implement parsing logic inline and never call detectHive — zero real coverage
detail: The file's stated purpose is to 'Verify response parsing and error handling' of src/features/aiDetection/hive.ts, but detectHive is never imported or invoked. Every 'parsing' test (lines 40-196) copies the nesting/loop logic into the test body and asserts on that local copy (e.g., lines 58-75, 92-106, 148-160). Config/timeout tests (lines 199-223) assert string/number literals constructed in the test. Because the real detectHive (which performs the fetch, the !response.ok throw at hive.ts:39-42, the output guard at hive.ts:60-64, and the class scan at hive.ts:68-76) is never executed, any regression in the real parser (wrong key path, dropped typeof guard, inverted ok check) passes this suite. This is a test that looks like coverage but provides none for the module it names.
fix: Mock global.fetch (the file already saves originalFetch at line 27 but never uses it) and call detectHive(url), asserting the returned number/null for the documented response shapes and error codes. Remove or convert the inline-logic 'tests' into real calls.

title: Optic tests re-implement parsing inline and never call detectOptic — zero real coverage
detail: Same pattern as the Hive test. The file claims to verify src/features/aiDetection/optic.ts response parsing/error handling, but detectOptic is never imported or called. The 'parsing' tests (lines 33-101) just read `response?.report?.ai?.confidence` from local literals; the API-config tests (lines 105-123) assert locally-built strings; the 'non-numeric confidence' test (lines 91-101) only checks `typeof x === 'number'` on a local object, not optic.ts's actual guard at optic.ts:57-60. The real function's behavior (Bearer header, `object` body key at optic.ts:32-34, !response.ok throw, null on non-numeric) is never exercised, so regressions in optic.ts would not fail this suite.
fix: Mock fetch and invoke detectOptic(url); assert the numeric/null return and that the request used the `object` body key and Bearer auth. Replace inline-logic assertions with real calls.

title: Most activityTracker tests assert local literals/SQL strings, not the module under test
detail: Only the first describe block (lines 59-86) actually calls trackJoin. Everything after line 88 — the UPSERT SQL block (92-102), silent-days math (114-166), config checks (171-197), first-message existence (201-224), embed format (229-258), edge cases (263-295), and schema-column lists (299-330) — constructs strings/objects/arithmetic inside the test and asserts on those, never touching activityTracker.ts. For example the 'uses UPSERT for join tracking' test (92-102) asserts a SQL string defined in the test, while the real trackJoin SQL lives at activityTracker.ts:40-48 and additionally sets `left_at = NULL` on conflict (not present in the test's copy). The silent-days flag logic is re-derived (143-165) instead of calling evaluateAndFlag. These pass unconditionally and cannot detect a real change in the module (e.g., flipping `< config.silentDays` at activityTracker.ts:213, or changing the UPSERT). Note trackFirstMessage/trackLeave/evaluateAndFlag have no real test here at all.
fix: Drive behavior through the exported functions: assert trackJoin's prepared SQL via the db mock (it can capture the SQL passed to prepare) including the `left_at = NULL` clause, and add tests that call trackFirstMessage to exercise the threshold/flag path. Delete or rewrite the literal-only describe blocks.

title: ensure.test.ts mocks db.pragma() but the code path uses .all() — tests pass for the wrong reason
detail: Two tests set up `mockFns.pragma.mockReturnValue([])` to simulate 'no columns exist': 'adds logging_channel_id column to existing guild_config' (248) and 'adds panic_mode columns when table exists' (286). But the real code reaches those branches via hasColumn() (ensure.ts:506-517), which reads columns through `db.prepare('PRAGMA table_info(...)').all()` — i.e. the `.all()` mock, not `db.pragma()`. The `.all` mock is set to [] in beforeEach (line 81) regardless, so the branch is taken and the assertion (logger.info / exec called) passes — but it passes by accident, not because the pragma stub did anything. If hasColumn were changed to use db.pragma (or the column-detection logic changed), these tests would not meaningfully validate the intended branch. They assert only that some info log / exec happened, which is too weak to catch a real regression (e.g., adding the column to the wrong table).
fix: Remove the misleading pragma stubs and instead assert on the SQL/args passed to db.exec (e.g., that an ALTER TABLE guild_config ADD COLUMN logging_channel_id / panic_mode was issued). Drive column-presence through the `.all()` mock that hasColumn actually consumes.

title: ensure.test.ts assertions are too weak to detect real defects (toHaveBeenCalled with no argument/SQL checks)
detail: Across the suite the success assertions are just `expect(mockFns.run).toHaveBeenCalled()` / `expect(logger.info).toHaveBeenCalled()` with no check on WHAT SQL ran or with which table/column/args. Because every ensure* function issues at least one run/exec and one info log, these assertions are satisfied even if the function targeted the wrong table, added the wrong column, or built malformed SQL. E.g. 'skips column addition when columns already exist' (149-161) still just asserts run was called (for the index) and cannot distinguish 'correctly skipped ALTERs' from 'incorrectly ran them'. The 'skips when all columns exist' cases (314-327, 349-359) only assert logger.info, so a regression that wrongly re-adds columns would still pass. These provide near-zero protection for schema-mutation code where a wrong table/column name is a realistic bug.
fix: Assert on the actual SQL text/arguments captured by the prepare/exec mocks (e.g., expect a specific ALTER/CREATE statement, and in the 'columns already exist' cases assert that NO ALTER ... ADD COLUMN was issued). The db mock already records calls; tighten the expectations.

title: legacyGuard test duplicates the guard regex by hand and over-claims coverage (guard only wraps prepare, not exec)
detail: The test asserts against a hand-copied LEGACY_RE (line 20). It currently matches the source exactly (src/db/db.ts:48), so there is no drift today, but the file itself acknowledges it must be manually kept in sync (lines 18-19) — a regression hazard, not a present bug. More substantively, the suite gives the impression that legacy 'ALTER TABLE ... RENAME' SQL is blocked, but the real guard only wraps db.prepare (db.ts:50-62); db.exec is NOT guarded. src/db/ensure.ts:84 issues `db.exec('ALTER TABLE avatar_scan RENAME COLUMN app_id TO application_id')`, which bypasses the guard entirely. So a reader trusting this test could wrongly assume RENAME is rejected everywhere. The regex test passing does not reflect runtime protection on the exec path that ensure.ts actually uses.
fix: Export the regex (or the wrapped-prepare factory) from src/db/db.ts and import it here instead of copying, so drift is impossible. Add a note/test clarifying the guard covers prepare only, or extend the guard to db.exec if RENAME should truly be blocked at runtime.

title: Failure message reports un-stripped matches (includes allowed code-block mentions), confusing diagnostics
detail: The assertion correctly uses `realMatches` (mentions after fenced code blocks are stripped, lines 91-92), but the error message interpolates `matches` (line 89/95), which is computed against the FULL text including code blocks. If a file legitimately contains mention syntax inside a ``` fenced block AND also has a real violation outside it, the failure message will list the code-block mentions too, sending the developer to lines that are actually allowed. If a file's only mentions are inside code fences, realMatches is empty so the test passes (correct) — but `matches` would be non-empty, which is harmless only because the message isn't shown on pass. This is a diagnostics defect, not a guard-correctness defect.
fix: Interpolate `realMatches.join(", ")` (not `matches`) into the failure message so the reported mentions are exactly the ones that caused the failure.

title: Synchronous DB throw escapes Promise.allSettled, defeating the partial-results design
detail: executeAnalyticsCommand builds the Promise.allSettled input by EAGERLY calling the query functions: `Promise.resolve(getActionCountsByMod(...))`, `Promise.resolve(getTopReasons(...))`, etc. The real query functions in src/features/analytics/queries.ts are synchronous (better-sqlite3) and re-throw on any DB error (queries.ts:144, 258, 357, 457, 527). Because the call happens during array-literal construction, a synchronous throw propagates out BEFORE Promise.allSettled is ever invoked, so it is NOT captured as a 'rejected' settlement. It is instead caught by the outer try/catch at command.ts:336, which logs an error and replies '❌ Analytics query failed' — the exact opposite of the intended behavior, which is to show partial results (warn + show whatever succeeded). One failing query thus blanks the entire command instead of degrading gracefully. The test tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts:271-283 ('handles query failures gracefully') hides this because it uses mockGetActionCountsByMod.mockRejectedValue(...) which returns an already-rejected Promise (async) rather than throwing synchronously like the real code path; so the test exercises a code path that production never takes.
fix: Wrap each call so a synchronous throw becomes a rejected promise that allSettled can capture, e.g. use `Promise.resolve().then(() => getActionCountsByMod(...))` for each entry, or wrap the bodies in async helper functions. Then allSettled will correctly mark individual failures as rejected and the partial-results/warn path will run.

title: Monthly leaderboard/stats compare ISO-8601 string against SQLite datetime('now') format, undercounting month-boundary completions
detail: getMonthlyLeaderboard and getArtistStats compute the month start with `new Date(); setDate(1); setHours(0,0,0,0); .toISOString()`, producing a string like '2026-05-01T00:00:00.000Z' (with 'T' separator, milliseconds, and 'Z'). They then compare `completed_at >= startIso`. But completed_at is written by `datetime('now')` (store.ts:297) which produces SQLite's canonical format '2026-05-01 00:00:00' (SPACE separator, no ms, no 'Z'). The two formats are compared lexically. At character index 10 the stored value has ' ' (0x20) while the bound has 'T' (0x54); since ' ' < 'T', any job whose completed_at date-part equals the boundary day (the 1st of the month at/after midnight) compares as LESS THAN startIso and is wrongly excluded from the monthly count. Additionally, toISOString() converts LOCAL midnight to a UTC instant while completed_at is stored in UTC, so the boundary is further skewed by the server's UTC offset. Net effect: a recurring, silent undercount of jobs completed around the start of each month in artist leaderboards and stats. store.test.ts mocks db.get/all and only asserts pass-through values, so it never exercises this comparison and cannot catch the bug.
fix: Make the bound match the stored format and timezone. Either compute the boundary with SQLite (e.g. `completed_at >= datetime('now','start of month')`) or format the JS Date as a UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' string (space separator, no ms/Z) using UTC getters. Whichever is chosen, the comparison string and the stored column must use the same format and the same (UTC) timezone.

title: findAppByCodeOrMessage messageId path does not verify the resolved application belongs to the requesting guild
detail: In findAppByCodeOrMessage, the Priority-1 messageId branch looks up review_card by message_id and then fetches `SELECT * FROM application WHERE id = ?` with NO check that app.guild_id === the passed guildId. The short-code branch (Priority 2) is guild-scoped via findAppByShortCode, and the full-app-id branch (lines 159-163) explicitly checks `fullIdApp.guild_id === guildId` — so the messageId branch is the inconsistent one. The test file even documents this expectation (tests/features/appLookup.test.ts:363-373, 'application table lookup -> verifies guild_id matches'), yet the messageId branch omits it. Impact is currently latent: a grep shows no production caller invokes findAppByCodeOrMessage (only findAppByShortCode is used externally), so the gap is dormant. But if a future caller passes an attacker-influenced messageId, it could resolve an application from another guild, leaking cross-tenant data.
fix: After fetching the application by id in the messageId branch, verify `app.guild_id === guildId` before returning (mirroring the full-app-id branch); return null otherwise. The function's return type is also implicitly `any`/unknown here — annotate it and the messageId branch to ApplicationRow | null for type safety.

title: findAppByCodeOrMessage has an inferred union/any return type that hides shape mismatches
detail: findAppByCodeOrMessage has no declared return type. The messageId branch returns the raw result of `db.prepare('SELECT * ...').get(...)` (typed `unknown`/implicitly any), the short-code branch returns ApplicationRow, and the full-id branch returns AppRow. Callers therefore get a widened/inconsistent type and any field-shape assumptions are unchecked by the compiler. Combined with the missing guild check above, this makes it easy to introduce a real bug at a call site without a type error.
fix: Declare an explicit return type (ApplicationRow | null) and cast each branch's row to ApplicationRow | undefined consistently, normalizing the messageId branch like the others.

title: Test asserts a 'Unknown' fallback branch that the real SQL makes unreachable (masks intent / weak coverage)
detail: The test 'handles null normalized_reason' feeds mockAll a row { normalized_reason: null } and asserts result[0].reason === 'Unknown', exercising the `r.normalized_reason || 'Unknown'` fallback at approvalRate.ts:246. However, the production SQL (approvalRate.ts:219-235) filters nulls via `AND ra.reason IS NOT NULL`, `AND TRIM(ra.reason) != ''`, and `HAVING normalized_reason IS NOT NULL AND normalized_reason != ''`, so a null normalized_reason can never be returned by the query. The branch is effectively dead in production and the test only passes because the DB is mocked. This is not a runtime bug, but the test gives false confidence that the null-handling path matters; note also the sibling getTopReasons maps null to '' (queries.ts:337) while this maps to 'Unknown', an inconsistency that could surprise a future refactor that relaxes the SQL filters.
fix: Either remove the unreachable fallback (and test) or, if defensive handling is desired, align it with getTopReasons and document that the SQL already excludes nulls. Prefer an integration test against a real in-memory SQLite DB so the SQL filters are actually exercised.

title: closed_at parsed as local time instead of UTC, skewing the 7-day reopen window
detail: closeTicket() (tickets.ts:165) writes closed_at via SQLite datetime('now'), which yields a UTC string of the form 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' with NO timezone designator (the schema column is closed_at TEXT, db.ts:187). Line 73 does `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. V8/Node parses a space-separated, zone-less datetime string as LOCAL time, not UTC. So `closedAt` is offset from the true close instant by the server's UTC offset. The 7-day boundary test on line 77 (`now - closedAt > sevenDays`) is therefore wrong by up to the host UTC offset (~14h max). On a server with a positive UTC offset this makes `now - closedAt` larger than reality, so a ticket closed at ~6.8 days can be mis-classified as >7 days and a brand-new thread is created (via openPublicModmailThreadFor) instead of reopening the existing one; on a negative-offset server the window stays open too long. This is confirmed to be an inconsistency in THIS codebase: the correct normalization pattern is used elsewhere for the same kind of SQLite timestamp (src/ui/reviewCard.ts:110 and src/features/review/card.ts:129 both do `trimmed.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'` before new Date()). The identical raw-parse bug also exists in src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304 (out of bucket) for the same field.
fix: Normalize the SQLite UTC string before parsing, e.g. `const iso = ticket.closed_at.includes('T') ? ticket.closed_at : ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'; const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(iso).getTime() : 0;` (reuse the existing helper used by reviewCard.ts / review/card.ts). Apply the same fix at dashboardBridge.ts:304.

title: Reopen does not guard against an existing open ticket and can hit the partial unique index
detail: reopenModmailThread (within-7-day path) calls reopenTicket(ticket.id) inside a transaction, which runs `UPDATE modmail_ticket SET status='open', closed_at=NULL` (tickets.ts:177). The schema defines a partial unique index idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id, user_id, status) WHERE status='open' (db.ts:195-198). If the same (guild_id, user_id) already has another open ticket (e.g., a new modmail was opened after this one closed), flipping this row to status='open' violates that unique index and throws inside the transaction, aborting the reopen. The code never checks getOpenTicketByUser first. It is caught by the surrounding try/catch and surfaced as a generic 'Failed to reopen modmail thread' message, so no corruption — but the operation fails confusingly and the staff member gets no actionable reason. The user-id reopen branch (lines 44-57) selects only the most-recent closed ticket and is the most likely trigger when a newer open ticket exists.
fix: Before reopening, check for an existing open ticket for (guildId, userId) via getOpenTicketByUser and either short-circuit with a clear message ('User already has an open modmail: <#thread>') or link to it, instead of attempting an UPDATE that the unique index will reject.

title: Tautological tests re-implement logic inline instead of calling the source (false confidence)
detail: Large blocks of this suite never invoke any function from src/features/modmail/threadClose.ts. The 'reason text' tests (lines 255-307) copy-paste the exact reason-selection ternary from threadClose.ts (source lines 466-473) into the test body and assert on the copy. Likewise the 'closing embed format' (lines 311-330), 'archive/delete strategies' (lines 332-351, re-implementing `cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== false`), 'log URL format' (lines 353-361), 'duplicate close detection' (lines 364-377), and 'ticket structure' (lines 380-408) blocks only assert against literals/inline expressions defined within the test. These tests pass unconditionally regardless of the real implementation, so if someone changes the reason wording, the embed color/title, the delete-on-close default, or the log-URL template in threadClose.ts, these tests will NOT fail. Impact: false sense of coverage for closeModmailForApplication's user-facing strings and close behavior; a real regression in those strings would ship undetected.
fix: Replace the inline-reimplemented assertions with assertions on values produced by the source. E.g. drive closeModmailForApplication() past its early-return guard with a fully mocked open ticket and assert that user.send was called with the expected embed title/description/color and reason text, rather than asserting on a locally-recomputed `text`/`description`/`color` variable.

title: Incomplete transcript.js mock would throw if a closeModmailForApplication test ever passes the open-ticket guard
detail: The mock at lines 69-71 stubs only `flushTranscript` from ../../../src/features/modmail/transcript.js, but threadClose.ts imports `flushTranscript, getTranscriptBuffer, formatTranscript` (source line 36) and calls getTranscriptBuffer(ticketId) and formatTranscript(...) at source lines 500-503 during the happy path of closeModmailForApplication. The two existing closeModmailForApplication tests only hit the early-return guards (null ticket / already-closed at source lines 457-460), so they never reach those calls and currently pass. This is a latent trap: any future test that supplies an open ticket will throw 'getTranscriptBuffer is not a function' before exercising the logic under test, masking the real code path. The 'successful close' test for closeModmailThread (lines 191-220) similarly relies on getTicketById being called before deeper unmocked dependencies and only asserts the lookup happened, so it does not actually validate the close path.
fix: Add `getTranscriptBuffer: vi.fn(() => undefined)` and `formatTranscript: vi.fn(() => "")` to the transcript.js mock factory (lines 69-71) so the happy path is exercisable, then add at least one test that drives closeModmailForApplication with an open ticket and asserts closeTicket/cleanup/flush ordering.

title: mockTransaction has wrong shape vs better-sqlite3 / source usage; only unexercised because no test hits the in-7-day reopen success path
detail: The hoisted mock is `mockTransaction: vi.fn((fn) => fn())`, which immediately INVOKES the callback and returns its (undefined) result. But the real `db.transaction(fn)` (better-sqlite3, see src/db/db.ts:96-98) returns a CALLABLE wrapper, and the source uses it as `db.transaction(() => {...})()` (threadReopen.ts:89-109). With this mock, `db.transaction(fn)` returns `undefined`, and the source's trailing `()` would call `undefined()` -> TypeError. The tests pass only because NONE of them exercise the successful within-7-days reopen branch (every success test uses a ticket closed >7 days ago, which returns at threadReopen.ts:79 before reaching the transaction; the 'error handling' test makes db.transaction throw synchronously before the trailing `()`). Net effect: the core reopen transaction logic (reopenTicket + open_modmail guard re-insert + addOpenThread + thread unarchive/unlock + applicant DM) at threadReopen.ts:87-149 is entirely untested, and the mock that exists would actually break if a test were added. Contrast with the sibling threadOpen.test.ts:16 which correctly uses `(fn) => fn`.
fix: Change the mock to `mockTransaction: vi.fn((fn: Function) => fn)` (return the function, matching better-sqlite3 and threadOpen.test.ts), then add a test for the happy path: a closed ticket within 7 days that asserts reopenTicket is called, the open_modmail UPSERT runs, addOpenThread is called with the thread_id, and the success message `Modmail thread reopened: <#...>` is returned.

title: DB-reconstruction test does not assert the to_user/to_staff -> STAFF/USER author mapping, leaving the audit-trail direction unverified
detail: `flushTranscript` reconstructs transcripts from the DB when the in-memory buffer is empty, mapping `direction === 'to_user' ? 'STAFF' : 'USER'` (transcript.ts:147-151). This mapping is the load-bearing audit-trail semantic (verified consistent with the live append calls in routing.ts:305-315 where to_user=STAFF and routing.ts:423-434 where to_staff=USER). The test feeds one `to_user` and one `to_staff` row but only asserts `result.lineCount === 2` and that the SQL contains the SELECT columns. It never inspects the resulting embed/file content, so an inversion of the STAFF/USER mapping (which would corrupt every restart-reconstructed transcript) would not be caught. The current source is correct; this is purely a missing assertion that should guard against regressions in a compliance-sensitive path.
fix: Capture the sent file/embed (as the 'creates filename' tests already do via send mock) and assert the reconstructed transcript text labels the to_user row as STAFF and the to_staff row as USER, e.g. assert the .txt buffer contains `STAFF: DB message 1` and `USER: DB message 2`.

title: Vacuous tests assert on inline string/boolean literals instead of exercising any source code
detail: The describe blocks 'modmail thread customId format', 'modmail race condition handling', and 'primary key constraint detection' (lines 350-401) construct local literals (e.g. `const customId = ` + tts + `v1:modmail:close:${ticketId}` + tts + `` then expect it to equal `v1:modmail:close:123`; `const isRace = error.message.includes('UNIQUE') || ...`) and assert on those local expressions. They import nothing from threadOpen.ts for these cases and would still pass if the corresponding production logic (customId construction at threadOpen.ts:384, race detection at threadOpen.ts:444-448) were deleted or changed. They provide false confidence in coverage of the customId format and race-detection logic without testing it.
fix: Either remove these blocks or rewrite them to assert against the real code paths: parse a customId actually emitted by openPublicModmailThreadFor, and drive openPublicModmailThreadFor with a thrown UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY/SQLITE_CONSTRAINT error to assert the 'already exists' / 'being created by another moderator' branches at threadOpen.ts:450-473.

title: Local BUTTON_RE diverges from the real BTN_DECIDE_RE it claims to test, giving false coverage of the review button router
detail: The `describe("BUTTON_RE pattern")` block defines its OWN regex `const BUTTON_RE = /^v1:decide:(\w+):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/;` and asserts against it. The production symbol it purports to cover is `src/features/review/handlers/helpers.ts:38` `export const BUTTON_RE = BTN_DECIDE_RE;`, which resolves to `src/lib/modalPatterns.ts:35`: `/^(?:v1:decide|review):(approve|accept|reject|kick|claim|unclaim|wrong_password|stale_modmail):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/`. The two differ materially: (1) the test uses `(\w+)` for the action, accepting ANY word, whereas production restricts to a fixed allowlist; (2) the test omits the `review:` prefix alias that modalPatterns.ts explicitly keeps for weeks-old button embeds.
