Because the test never imports the real regex, a regression in BTN_DECIDE_RE (e.g. dropping `kick` from the allowlist, or removing the `review:` alias) would NOT fail any of these tests. The button router gates moderation actions (approve/reject/kick/claim), so this is security-relevant code with effectively zero regression protection from this suite.
fix: Import the real constant instead of redefining it: `import { BUTTON_RE } from "../../../../src/features/review/handlers/helpers.js";` (or import `BTN_DECIDE_RE` from `src/lib/modalPatterns.js`) and assert against that. Add cases proving the action allowlist is enforced (e.g. `v1:decide:bogus:codeABCDEF` must NOT match) and that the `review:` prefix alias matches.

title: Helper tests assert against mocks/inline literals and never invoke the functions under test
detail: The `describe`s for `isStaff`, `requireInteractionStaff`, `resolveApplication`, and all the `openRejectModal`/`openAcceptModal`/`openPermRejectModal`/`openKickModal`/`openUnclaimModal` blocks do not import or call any of those real functions (defined in src/features/review/handlers/helpers.ts). Instead they call the mocked dependencies directly (e.g. `hasRole(...)`, `findAppByShortCode(...)`, `getClaim(...)`) or assert on inline-recomputed expressions like `["rejected","approved","kicked"].includes(app.status)` and `\`v1:modal:reject:code${code}\``. These are tautologies that re-test JavaScript/Vitest, not the module. The real `openRejectModal` has non-trivial ordering (status check, claimGuard, then `safeShowModal` token-age/replied checks at helpers.ts:138-202) that is entirely unverified. Concrete impact: the suite reports green while providing no protection against regressions in staff gating or modal pre-checks.
fix: Import the real functions and exercise them with mocked discord.js interaction objects, asserting on observable effects (replyOrEdit content, whether showModal is/ isn't called, return value of requireInteractionStaff). Remove the tautological assertions or convert them into behavioral tests.

title: Modal-handler tests redefine patterns locally and never call the real handlers, providing no regression coverage
detail: Every block (`handleRejectModal`, `handleAcceptModal`, `handlePermRejectModal`, `handleKickModal`, `handleUnclaimModal`, plus the `action dispatching` block) asserts on locally-declared regexes (`MODAL_RE`, `ACCEPT_MODAL_RE`, `MODAL_PERM_REJECT_RE`, `MODAL_KICK_RE`, `MODAL_UNCLAIM_RE`) and inline string/`slice`/`trim` recomputations rather than importing and invoking the handlers in src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts. The local copies happen to match src/lib/modalPatterns.ts today (so no currently-false assertion), but if those production patterns or the handlers' parsing/dispatch (e.g. `reason = raw.trim().slice(0,500) || null`, the deferUpdate-then-resolveApplication-then-runXAction sequence) regress, none of these tests fail. The `action dispatching` cases like `expect("runRejectAction").toBe("runRejectAction")` are pure tautologies. Real risk surface (staff gate via requireInteractionStaff, deferUpdate timing, dispatch to the correct runner) is untested here.
fix: Import the handlers and the canonical patterns from the source modules; drive each handler with a mocked ModalSubmitInteraction and assert the correct runner is invoked with the trimmed/truncated reason and that non-matching customIds early-return. Delete the string-equals-itself assertions.

title: serverAuditDocs helper tests reimplement logic inline instead of calling the real helpers
detail: The blocks labelled "...helper (tested via behavior)" and the `partitionIssues`/issue-sorting blocks reimplement the algorithm inside the test (e.g. the partition loop at lines 679-686, the severityOrder sort at 652-655, and md5 hashing via require('node:crypto') at 259-282) rather than importing `partitionIssues` and the hashing/sorting helpers from the source. The real `partitionIssues` is exported via src/features/serverAudit/docs.ts (re-exported by serverAuditDocs.ts). Consequently a regression in the real acknowledgment-invalidation logic (active vs acknowledged based on permissionHash match) would not be caught. No assertion here is currently false, so impact is limited to absent coverage rather than a wrong test.
fix: Import `partitionIssues` (and the real hashing/sort helpers if exported) and assert against their outputs for the same fixtures, instead of duplicating the implementation in the test body.

title: actionRunners.test.ts never imports or invokes the action runners it claims to test (vacuous coverage)
detail: The file is titled 'Unit tests for review action runner functions' and contains describe blocks named runApproveAction/runRejectAction/runPermRejectAction/runKickAction, but it never imports actionRunners.ts and never calls runApproveAction/runRejectAction/runPermRejectAction/runKickAction (grep confirms these names appear only inside describe() strings). Every 'it' asserts against a locally re-implemented literal, e.g. line 161 `const feature = ["review","approve"]; expect(feature).toContain("review")`, line 219 `expect(Object.values(conditions).every(Boolean)).toBe(true)`, line 264 a hand-written roleNote string. The only real imports (approveTx/rejectTx/kickTx from flows/index.js, getClaim/claimGuard) are mocked and then the mocks are called directly (e.g. line 124 `approveTx(...)` returns the mock). Impact: the critical moderation orchestration in actionRunners.ts -- claim-guard enforcement (lines 75-82), the 'role grant failed -> abort approval, do NOT send welcome DM' BLOCK (actionRunners.ts:128-149), modmail auto-close ordering, dmDelivered/roleApplied meta writes, and the duplicate ensureReviewMessage refresh -- has ZERO behavioral coverage from this file while the file name implies it is covered. A regression in any of those paths (e.g. removing the role-grant block, letting an unclaimed mod approve) would not fail a single assertion here. The divergence is concrete: line 124/151 mock approveTx to return {kind:"ok"}, but the real TxResult union (src/features/review/types.ts:132-136) has no "ok" kind (success is "changed"), showing the test was written against a misremembered contract.
fix: Import the real runners and drive them with the existing discord.js/db mocks (the sibling approve.test.ts shows the pattern). Assert on the mocked collaborators: that replyOrEdit gets the claim-guard string when claimGuard returns non-null, that channel.send + updateReviewActionMeta({roleApplied:false,dmDelivered:false}) fire and deliverApprovalDm is NOT called when accepted_role_id is set but roleApplied is false, etc. At minimum delete the literal-only assertions so they stop counting toward the coverage gate and misrepresenting coverage.

title: buttons.test.ts never imports the button handlers; all assertions are local re-implementations
detail: Despite describe blocks for handleReviewButton/handleModmailButton/handlePermRejectButton/handleCopyUidButton/handlePingInUnverified/handleDeletePing, the file never imports buttons.ts and never calls any handler. The customId regexes are re-declared inline (e.g. line 84 BUTTON_RE, line 155 BTN_MODMAIL_RE) instead of imported from src/lib/modalPatterns.js, so if the real regex drifts from the test copy the tests still pass. Routing assertions are tautologies, e.g. line 100-103 `const opensModal = ["reject",...].includes("reject"); expect(opensModal).toBe(true)`. Security-relevant behavior in the real handler is therefore untested: requireInteractionStaff gating (buttons.ts:77,216,286,319,637), the per-action rate-limit deferUpdate path (buttons.ts:84-92), allowedMentions hardening on the unverified ping (buttons.ts:494 `{users:[userId],parse:[]}`), and findAppByShortCode existence check before replying with a UID (buttons.ts:334). A regression that, say, dropped the staff check or widened allowedMentions would not fail here even though 'permission checks' tests exist. Impact: false confidence on a moderator-only, mention-capable surface.
fix: Import BUTTON_RE/BTN_* from src/lib/modalPatterns.js so the test exercises the real patterns, and invoke the exported handlers with mocked ButtonInteraction objects, asserting that non-staff interactions get the 'Gatekeeper role required' reply and that the ping path sends with parse:[] and only the target user. Remove the tautological `.includes(...)` literal assertions.

title: claimHandlers.test.ts never imports handleClaimToggle/handleUnclaimAction; tests assert only literals
detail: The file claims to test handleClaimToggle and handleUnclaimAction but never imports claimHandlers.ts and never calls either function. Each case rebuilds a string locally, e.g. line 72-75 `const msg = errorCode === "ALREADY_CLAIMED" ? "..." : "..."; expect(msg).toContain("already claimed")`, and the 'permanent rejection check' (line 110-112) asserts a hard-coded SQL string rather than that the handler actually runs that query. Consequently the real claim flow is untested: the post-claim permanently_rejected re-check (claimHandlers.ts:84-102), the ClaimError->message mapping, the assumption that the parent already called deferUpdate, and the audit/log/notify side effects. A regression (e.g. removing the perm-rejected block so a banned user can be claimed/approved) passes all assertions here.
fix: Import the real handlers and drive them with mocked reviewActions.claimTx/unclaimTx (throwing ClaimError instances) plus a mock db, asserting replyOrEdit content and that ensureReviewMessage/logActionPretty/notifyDashboard are invoked on the success path and skipped on the error paths.

title: Test encodes a fabricated INVALID_STATUS string and masks a real garbled-message bug for panic mode
detail: The test 'extracts status from error message' uses errorMessage = "Cannot claim: status is approved" and asserts split(" ")[2] === "status". This is not the real message and the asserted value ("status") is meaningless. The production handler (src/features/review/handlers/claimHandlers.ts:49-50) does `msg = `Cannot claim: application is already **${err.message.split(" ")[2]}**.`` against the ClaimError thrown by claimTx. claimTx throws INVALID_STATUS in TWO shapes: (a) terminal state -> "Application already approved" where split[2] = "approved" (correct), and (b) PANIC MODE -> "Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended." (src/features/reviewActions.ts:62) where split[2] = "is". So when a moderator clicks Claim during panic mode they get the nonsensical reply "Cannot claim: application is already **is**." instead of a panic-mode explanation. The vacuous test neither reflects the real message nor catches the panic-mode garble.
fix: In claimHandlers.ts, branch on the actual ClaimError content instead of positional word parsing: surface err.message directly for the panic case (it is already user-friendly), and only do the 'already <status>' phrasing for the terminal-state case (e.g. detect a leading 'Application already '). Then write a real test that calls handleClaimToggle with claimTx mocked to throw both ClaimError shapes and asserts the rendered reply.

title: approveFlow retry-path tests run real 2s timers (no fake timers), making each ~4s and risking timeouts under load
detail: approveFlow (src/features/review/flows/approve.ts:136-185) retries role granting up to 3 attempts, sleeping ROLE_GRANT_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 2000ms via real setTimeout on attempts 1 and 2. The three tests that drive the retry path -- 'captures roleError on permission failure' (canManageRole always false), 'does not report permission errors to Sentry' (always false), and 'reports non-permission errors to Sentry' (roleAddFails) -- never install fake timers, and tests/setup.ts does NOT enable fake timers globally (its header comment says it does, but the body only clears/restores in afterEach). Each of these tests therefore blocks ~4s of real wall-clock time; with the 15s testTimeout (vitest.config.ts:22) and parallel worker contention noted in that same comment, they are a latent timeout/flake source and needlessly slow the suite.
fix: Wrap these tests with vi.useFakeTimers() and advance with vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync, or inject/override ROLE_GRANT_RETRY_DELAY_MS to 0 in tests. Also fix the misleading 'use fake timers' claim in tests/setup.ts header.

title: Tests lock in claims.ts claimGuard semantics while a same-named claimGuard in reviewActions.ts has the opposite null behavior
detail: claims.test.ts imports claimGuard from src/features/review/claims.js, whose guard returns null (allow) when claim is null (claims.ts:46-49) and the test asserts exactly that (line 62-65). But there is a second exported claimGuard in src/features/reviewActions.ts:251-261 that returns an error string ('not claimed... use Claim button') when claim is null -- the opposite decision for the unclaimed case. The two share a name and signature, so a caller importing the wrong one silently flips whether an unclaimed application can be acted on. The test only pins one variant, giving no protection against importing the wrong claimGuard. (Today actionRunners.ts correctly imports the claims.ts version, so no live bug, but the duplication is a real footgun directly relevant to interpreting this test.)
fix: Collapse to a single claimGuard (re-export one from the other) so there is exactly one definition, and add a test asserting the chosen null-claim behavior at the single source. If both behaviors are genuinely needed, rename them (e.g. claimGuard vs requireClaim).

title: Entire 'modals' suite never imports or executes the module under test (tautological tests)
detail: The file is named/structured as tests for the review modal submission handlers (handleRejectModal, handleAcceptModal, handlePermRejectModal, handleKickModal, handleUnclaimModal) in src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts, and it sets up vi.mock for logger/sentry/cmdWrap as if it will drive that module. But it imports NOTHING from modals.ts. Every single 'it' block re-implements the logic inline (e.g. `reasonRaw.trim().slice(0,500)`, regex literals re-declared locally, `customId` string templates) and asserts on those local re-implementations. Concrete impact: a real regression in modals.ts (wrong field id, missing trim/slice, wrong action dispatch, removed staff check, dropped deferUpdate) would NOT fail this suite — it provides false coverage. The describe blocks 'action dispatching', 'staff validation', 'application resolution' assert hard-coded booleans/strings (`expect(checkPerformed).toBe(true)`, `expect(action).toBe('runRejectAction')`) that can never fail.
fix: Import the actual handlers from src/features/review/handlers/modals.js and invoke them with a mocked ModalSubmitInteraction (fields.getTextInputValue, deferUpdate, customId, user.id, inGuild). Assert that resolveApplication/runRejectAction/etc. (mocked) are called with the parsed code and trimmed/truncated reason, and that non-matching customIds early-return. Delete the assert-a-literal tests.

title: Trace-ID tests assert behavior the source does not implement (interactionId.slice(-8))
detail: Tests 'generates trace ID from interaction ID', 'uses last 8 chars of interaction ID', and 'converts to uppercase' assert that the error trace id equals `interactionId.slice(-8).toUpperCase()`. The real modals.ts catch blocks compute `const traceId = ctx().traceId ?? newTraceId();` (modals.ts lines 66,104,143,182,272). newTraceId() (src/lib/reqctx.ts:39) returns an 11-char random base62 string and never touches the interaction id. So the documented/asserted trace-id derivation is simply false. Because the tests only exercise their own inline slice() expression they still pass, masking that (a) the real trace logic is untested and (b) the described behavior is wrong. Anyone reading the suite is misled about how trace ids are produced.
fix: Remove these trace-id-from-interaction tests, or rewrite them to mock src/lib/reqctx (ctx/newTraceId) and assert the handler logs/replies with the value returned by newTraceId()/ctx().traceId. Do not assert a slice of interaction.id.

title: isStaff / requireInteractionStaff / resolveApplication tests never call the real functions
detail: The describe blocks for isStaff, requireInteractionStaff and resolveApplication do not import or call those functions from src/features/review/handlers/helpers.ts. They instead call the mocked primitives directly (e.g. `hasRole(member,'gatekeeper-role-id')`, `findAppByShortCode(...)`, `loadApplication(...)`) and assert the mock returns what it was told to return (e.g. line 155-159 sets findAppByShortCode -> {id:'app-123'} then asserts it returns {id:'app-123'}). The real branching logic — bypass-then-role precedence in isStaff, guild/guildId rejection + reply in requireInteractionStaff, and the guild-mismatch / null-app early returns in resolveApplication — is never executed. A bug such as inverting `shouldBypass`, dropping the `app.guild_id !== guildId` check (a real authz guard, helpers.ts:117), or failing to send the ephemeral 'Guild only.' reply would pass this suite.
fix: Import isStaff/requireInteractionStaff/resolveApplication from helpers.js and assert their real return values and side-effects (reply/replyOrEdit called with the right content/flags, null returned on guild mismatch). Keep shouldBypass/hasRole/findAppByShortCode/loadApplication mocked as inputs.

title: Local BUTTON_RE copy diverges from the real BTN_DECIDE_RE, so routing-regex tests prove nothing
detail: The suite defines its own `const BUTTON_RE = /^v1:decide:(\w+):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/` and tests claim/unclaim/approve/etc. against it. The actual pattern used by handlers (src/lib/modalPatterns.ts:35, re-exported as BUTTON_RE from helpers.ts:38) is `/^(?:v1:decide|review):(approve|accept|reject|kick|claim|unclaim|wrong_password|stale_modmail):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/`. Two concrete divergences: (1) the real regex also accepts the legacy `review:` prefix, which the test's copy rejects; (2) the real regex constrains the action to a fixed allowlist whereas the test copy accepts ANY `\w+` (so `v1:decide:garbage:codeABCDEF` would 'match' in the test but not in production). The tests therefore validate a fictional regex; a change to the real allowlist or prefix handling would not be caught.
fix: Import the real BUTTON_RE/MODAL_RE/ACCEPT_MODAL_RE from src/features/review/handlers/helpers.js (or BTN_DECIDE_RE etc. from src/lib/modalPatterns.js) instead of re-declaring local literals, then run the same match assertions plus a `review:`-prefixed case and an invalid-action negative case.

title: Modal-opener tests assert inline literals instead of exercising openRejectModal/openAcceptModal/etc.
detail: The 'modal opening functions' blocks never call openRejectModal, openAcceptModal, openPermRejectModal, openKickModal or openUnclaimModal. Resolution/claim checks are re-implemented inline (e.g. `['rejected','approved','kicked'].includes(app.status)`, `claim.reviewer_id !== 'user123'`) and customId/maxLength expectations are bare literal equality (`expect(maxLength).toBe(500)`). Notably the openPermRejectModal block (373-404) has no 'blocks already resolved' test while every other opener block does — which happens to mirror a real asymmetry in source (openPermRejectModal in helpers.ts:248-275 omits the status guard that the other openers have), but the suite cannot detect either the omission or any future regression because it never invokes the functions. Impact: zero real coverage of the modal-builder logic and claim gating.
fix: Drive each opener with a fake ButtonInteraction (replied/deferred=false, recent createdTimestamp, showModal mocked) and the mocked getClaim/claimGuard, then assert showModal was called with a modal whose customId/field ids/required/min-max match, and that already-resolved or foreign-claim cases short-circuit via replyOrEdit instead of showing a modal.

title: withTimeout never clears its setTimeout, leaking a 30s timer per DM (also in kick.ts)
detail: withTimeout races the work promise against `new Promise((_,reject)=>setTimeout(...,30000))` but never captures the timer handle, so it is never cleared. When user.send() resolves first (the normal case, exercised by reject.test.ts), the 30s timer stays pending until it fires and rejects an already-settled promise (no-op). Same pattern in src/features/review/flows/kick.ts:29-36 for fetch/send/kick — up to three dangling 30s timers per kick. Production impact is modest (timers are short-lived and self-clear) but it keeps the event loop active and, under bursts of approvals/rejections, accumulates thousands of pending timers; in tests it leaves real timers alive after the test ends since the suite uses no fake timers. Grep confirmed there is no clearTimeout anywhere in src/features/review/flows.
fix: Capture the handle and clear it in a finally: `let t; const timeout = new Promise<T>((_,rej)=>{t=setTimeout(()=>rej(new Error(...)),ms);}); try { return await Promise.race([promise, timeout]); } finally { clearTimeout(t); }`. Apply in both reject.ts and kick.ts.

title: Weak assertion `call.includes(0)` cannot distinguish the permanently_rejected flag from other zero args
detail: The 'sets permanently_rejected to 0 for standard rejection' test asserts `updateRunCalls.some((call) => call.includes(0))`. Array.prototype.includes scans every positional arg of every recorded .run() call for a strict `0`. It is not pinned to the permanently_rejected parameter position, so it would still pass if permanently_rejected were wrong but some unrelated argument happened to be 0 (or if the CASE-guard param were 0 instead). The precise positional tests added later (181-222) make this one redundant, but as written it provides false assurance about the permanent flag specifically.
fix: Assert positionally like the sibling tests do: filter the UPDATE call (length 5, call[4]==='app-123') and assert `call[2]===0` (permanently_rejected) and `call[3]===0` (CASE guard). Or simply delete this test in favour of the precise ones at 205-222.

title: Unbalanced Unicode bidi isolate characters in generated newsletter markdown
detail: Each section header in the copy-for-Discord output wraps a label in bidi isolates as `⁨`...`⁩⁩` (lines 81, 87, 91, 98). There is exactly ONE First Strong Isolate opener (U+2068) but TWO Pop Directional Isolate closers (U+2069) per header. The pair is unbalanced: one extra PDI per section. When a moderator clicks 'Copy for Newsletter' and pastes into Discord, every section header carries a stray invisible directional-isolate character. Impact is limited to the copied/pasted public newsletter text (invisible junk char, possible subtle bidi rendering quirk in clients), not bot logic. Looks like a copy-paste artifact when these isolate wrappers were authored.
fix: Drop the duplicated closer so each label is wrapped with a single matched pair: `⁨`label`⁩` (remove the second `⁩` on lines 81, 87, 91, 98). Verify the intended bidi-isolation by pasting the output into Discord and confirming no stray characters remain.

title: "preserves cause" test has a dead variable and does not test what its name claims
detail: The test creates `const cause = new Error("root cause")` and assigns it as `err.cause`, implying it verifies the original cause chain is preserved by classifyError. But the only assertion is `expect(result.cause).toBe(err)` — it asserts the classified error's `.cause` is the wrapped error itself, never referencing the `cause` variable. Per the source (src/lib/errors.ts:234, `cause: err instanceof Error ? err : undefined`), classifyError stores the passed-in error as `.cause` and silently discards any nested `err.cause` (the real root cause). So the `cause` local on line 237 and the assignment on line 239 are dead, and the test gives false confidence that cause-chain information survives classification when it does not. Impact: a future change that (correctly) starts unwrapping `err.cause` would not be caught here, and the misleading test name hides that root-cause data is dropped during error classification.
fix: Either rename the test to "stores the original error as cause" and remove the unused `cause` variable/assignment, or (if cause-chain preservation is actually desired) change the source to walk `err.cause` and update the assertion to `expect(result.cause).toBe(cause)`.

title: All leaderboardImage tests assert only `instanceof Buffer`, giving false safety because canvas is fully mocked
detail: Every test in generateLeaderboardImage/generateStatsImage mocks the entire `canvas` module so `toBuffer` always returns `Buffer.from("mock-png-image")` regardless of the rendering code path. The assertions are uniformly `expect(result).toBeInstanceOf(Buffer)`, which is true for any input because the mock unconditionally returns a Buffer. As a result, these tests cannot detect real defects in the code they ostensibly cover — e.g. the acknowledged off-by-one in `truncateText` (src/lib/leaderboardImage.ts:247-251) or the `stop = i / (gradient.colors.length - 1)` division in `drawGradientText` (src/lib/leaderboardImage.ts:285) which yields `0/0 = NaN`/`Infinity` color stops if a `nameGradient.colors` array of length 1 is ever passed. The 'handles stats with nitro gradient' / 'handles single stat entry' cases run but verify nothing about correctness. Impact: regressions in image-layout math will pass CI silently.
fix: Assert on observable side-effects of the mocked context: e.g. capture the ctx mock and assert `fillText`/`measureText`/`createLinearGradient` were called the expected number of times and with expected arguments (column counts, gradient stop values), and add a case with a single-color gradient to pin down the length===1 behavior.

title: "uses default rate when not specified" test cannot detect a broken default sample rate
detail: The test deletes WIDE_EVENT_SAMPLE_RATE to exercise the DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE (0.1) path, but it asserts using an outcome:"error" event. In wideEventEmitter.ts shouldSample() returns true for errors/timeouts BEFORE getSampleRate() is ever consulted (lines 104-105). So logger.error is called regardless of what the default rate is. The test would still pass if DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE were 0, or if getSampleRate() returned garbage, or if the default-rate branch were deleted entirely. It provides false confidence that the default sampling behavior is covered. Impact: a regression that breaks default sampling of success events (the actual purpose of the default) would not be caught here.
fix: Use a success event and assert sampling behavior deterministically. Since sampling is hashTraceId(traceId) < rate, pick a traceId whose hash is below/above 0.1 and assert logger.info is/ isn't called; or stub Math via a known traceId. At minimum test a success outcome rather than an error so the default-rate code path is actually reached.

title: "returns a copy" tests pass trivially and miss the real shallow-copy aliasing bug in getSchedulerHealth
detail: getSchedulerHealth() returns `new Map(schedulerHealth)` (schedulerHealth.ts:114) which is a SHALLOW copy: the SchedulerHealth value objects are the SAME references stored internally. recordSchedulerRun mutates those objects in place (lines 73-83: health.lastRunAt = now; health.consecutiveFailures++ etc.). Therefore a caller holding a result from getSchedulerHealth() will see its objects mutate out from under it on the next scheduler run, and could even corrupt internal state by writing to them. getSchedulerHealthByName, by contrast, returns a spread copy ({ ...health }, line 132), so the two accessors are inconsistent. The test "returns a copy of the internal map" only checks `health1 !== health2`, which is trivially true for any `new Map()` and does NOT detect the value-object aliasing. The timestamp-preservation tests (246-266) also re-read via getSchedulerHealthByName (which copies) so they never exercise the aliased map. Impact: the unit tests give false assurance that getSchedulerHealth returns an isolated snapshot; the underlying aliasing/shared-mutable-state defect is real but uncaught.
fix: In schedulerHealth.ts make getSchedulerHealth() deep-copy the values: `return new Map(Array.from(schedulerHealth, ([k, v]) => [k, { ...v }]));`. Then strengthen the test to capture a value object from getSchedulerHealth(), call recordSchedulerRun again, and assert the previously captured object did NOT change (e.g., totalRuns stayed the same).

title: environment assertion passes via real NODE_ENV, not the mocked env, masking what is actually under test
detail: The suite mocks ../../src/lib/env.js as { env: { NODE_ENV: "test" } }, implying event.environment is derived from that mock. But createEmptyEvent() in wideEvent.ts sources environment from getBuildInfo().environment (wideEvent.ts:417/424-428), and getBuildInfo()/buildInfo.ts is NOT mocked. getBuildInfo computes environment from process.env.NODE_ENV via getEnvironment(). The assertion `event.environment === "test"` (line 90) only passes because Vitest sets process.env.NODE_ENV="test" at runtime — not because of the env.js mock. The env.js mock is only actually used by setError's stack gate (env.NODE_ENV === "development"). Impact: the test misrepresents the data source; if build identity wiring changed (e.g., environment came from a different field) the test could pass or fail for the wrong reason, and the buildInfo singleton cache (_buildInfoCache) leaking across test files could make environment nondeterministic.
fix: Mock ../../src/lib/buildInfo.js (e.g., getBuildInfo returning a fixed BuildInfo with environment: "test") so the constructor's data source is controlled and deterministic, and call _resetBuildInfoCache() in beforeEach to avoid cross-file cache bleed.

title: "comparison time is consistent" test does not measure timing and cannot detect loss of constant-time property
detail: The test in the "security properties" describe block claims to verify the timing-safe nature, but it only asserts the boolean result is false for three inputs differing at start/middle/end. It never measures or compares execution time. If secureCompare were refactored to a naive short-circuiting `a === b` (reintroducing a timing side-channel), this test would still pass. The security property it names is therefore unverified. Impact: false confidence that timing-attack resistance is guarded by tests; a regression removing crypto.timingSafeEqual/hashing would go undetected by this suite.
fix: Either rename/rescope the test to "returns false regardless of diff position" (correctness only, no timing claim), or add a separate explicitly-skipped/benchmark test documenting that timing is validated out-of-band. Do not assert a security property the test does not actually exercise.

title: syncMarker tests assert only that db.run was called, not the SQL/params, so they cannot catch logic regressions
detail: touchSyncMarker (syncMarker.ts:45-51) runs an UPDATE with params (BOT_LOCATION, actionType ?? null) and the action_count increment / COALESCE logic is the meaningful behavior. The tests only assert mockFns._mockRun.toHaveBeenCalled() with no argument matching. They would still pass if the SQL were wrong, if params were swapped/omitted, or if actionType were never forwarded (the test "updates sync marker with action type" does not assert the action type reached run()). Because the prepared statements are created at module import time against the mocked db.prepare, a change that breaks parameter passing or the COALESCE/increment semantics would not be detected. Impact: weak coverage that gives false assurance over the sync-marker freshness counter, which drives local/remote DB switching.
fix: Assert call arguments: expect(_mockRun).toHaveBeenCalledWith("local", null) and ("local", "review_action"); optionally capture db.prepare's SQL and assert it contains action_count + 1 and COALESCE(?, last_action_type).

title: pretty.test.ts exercises ZERO source code — entire suite is tautological, gives false coverage for the audit-logging module
detail: This file purports to test src/logging/pretty.ts (logActionPretty / getActionMeta / the action_log INSERT / embed building). It sets up vi.mock for db, logger, time, loggingStore and features/logger (lines 10-49), but it NEVER imports anything from ../../src/logging/pretty.js. Every single `it(...)` re-declares a local literal and asserts on that literal, e.g.: line 178-182 `const meta = { title:'Application Submitted', color:0x5865f2, emoji:'📝' }; expect(meta.color).toBe(0x5865f2)`; line 266 `const query='INSERT INTO action_log'; expect(query).toContain('action_log')`; line 301-305 `const dbFailed=true; const shouldContinue=!dbFailed; expect(shouldContinue).toBe(false)`; line 287-291 `JSON.stringify({key:'value'})` equality; line 343-347 `appId.slice(-6).toUpperCase()` length. None of these call getActionMeta(), logActionPretty(), or any real symbol. Impact: the suite would stay 100% green if pretty.ts were deleted, if a getActionMeta color/emoji/title were wrong, if the action_log INSERT column list were broken, if the meta-field rendering (modmail_close archive label, role_grant reward-roles pluralization, etc.) regressed, or if the embed/JSON fallback path broke. For a module that is the single source of truth for the moderation audit trail and powers /modstats analytics, this is dangerous false confidence — reviewers will believe the behavior is covered when it is not.
fix: Import the real symbols (import { logActionPretty } from '../../src/logging/pretty.js') and assert on actual behavior: call logActionPretty(mockGuild, params) and verify mockPrepare/mockRun received the expected action_log INSERT with the right bound params; verify getActionMeta is invoked indirectly by checking the embed title/color via the mocked EmbedBuilder; verify the no-channel branch calls the mocked logActionJSON with the correct payload. Delete the literal-only assertions.

title: "clamps odds to minimum/maximum" tests are vacuous: odds=0 is coerced to 1000 before the clamp, and mocked constants diverge from production
detail: Two problems. (1) The test 'clamps odds to minimum' (line 265-272) sets dadmode_odds: 0 and expects a reply. But the source (src/listeners/messageDadMode.ts:73) computes `odds = Math.max(DADMODE_ODDS_MIN, Math.min(DADMODE_ODDS_MAX, Number(cfg.dadmode_odds || 1000)))`. Because `0 || 1000` evaluates to 1000 (0 is falsy), the value 0 is replaced by 1000 BEFORE reaching Math.max, so the DADMODE_ODDS_MIN clamp branch is never exercised — the test name is misleading and the lower-bound clamp is effectively untested. (2) The test mocks src/lib/constants.js (line 27-30) with DADMODE_ODDS_MIN:1, DADMODE_ODDS_MAX:10000, but the real constants (src/lib/constants.ts:34-35) are DADMODE_ODDS_MIN:2, DADMODE_ODDS_MAX:100000. So 'clamps odds to maximum' (line 274-282) asserts a 10000 ceiling that does not exist in production (real ceiling 100000). A regression that changed the real MIN/MAX constants would not be caught by these tests. Impact: false confidence that odds clamping is validated; the actual production clamp bounds are untested.
fix: Use a non-falsy out-of-range value to exercise the lower clamp (e.g. dadmode_odds: -5 or 1, which survives the `|| 1000` guard and reaches Math.max(DADMODE_ODDS_MIN,...)). Do NOT mock constants.js (or mock it with the real values) so the test validates the production bounds; assert the effective odds via the number of Math.random buckets or by spying on the computed odds.

title: Skullmode clamp tests are vacuous (odds=0 coerced to 1000) and mock SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX=10000 while production is 1000
detail: Same defect class as the dadmode test. 'clamps odds to minimum' (line 146-153) sets skullmode_odds: 0 and expects a react, but src/listeners/messageSkullMode.ts:44 does `Number(cfg.skullmode_odds || 1000)` so 0 becomes 1000 and the SKULLMODE_ODDS_MIN clamp (Math.max) is never exercised. 'clamps odds to maximum' (line 155-163) and 'does not react when roll is non-zero' (line 136-144) run against a MOCKED SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX of 10000 (test line 27-30), but the real constant (src/lib/constants.ts:39) is SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX = 1000 — a 10x divergence. The max-clamp behavior the test claims to verify (cap at 10000) is not what production does (cap at 1000). A change to the real bound would not be caught. Impact: false confidence; production odds bounds untested.
fix: Exercise the lower clamp with a value that is not falsy (e.g. 1 or a negative number). Stop mocking constants.js with non-production values; import the real bounds or assert the clamped odds explicitly so the test reflects SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX=1000.

title: Logging-channel resolution test omits priority-1 (DB row) and the cache layer entirely
detail: The suite header documents a three-tier priority (DB > env > null) and imports both getLoggingChannelId AND setLoggingChannelId (line 16), but only asserts priority 2 (env fallback, line 39-46) and priority 3 (null, line 53-58). It never sets a DB row via setLoggingChannelId and then reads it back to prove priority 1 wins over env, and never exercises the LRU cache in src/config/loggingStore.ts (getCached/setCache/invalidateCache, lines 51-77) — including the subtle null-vs-undefined CachedValue wrapper and the cache-after-write invalidation ordering that the source comments call out as bug-prone. setLoggingChannelId is imported but unused. Impact: the highest-priority resolution path and the entire caching/invalidations logic ship with no behavioral coverage from this file; a regression where DB no longer overrides env, or where a stale cached null is served after a write, would not be caught here.
fix: Add a priority-1 test: setLoggingChannelId(guildId, 'db-channel') with LOGGING_CHANNEL also set, assert getLoggingChannelId returns 'db-channel'. Add a cache test: read (caches env null), then setLoggingChannelId, then read again and assert the fresh value (proves invalidateCache works). Remove the unused setLoggingChannelId import if no DB test is added.

title: Test encodes a malformed bot reply (stray closing quote) as expected output
detail: The 'matches with leading quotes' test sends content '"I'm confused"' and asserts the bot replies exactly `Hi confused", I'm dad.` (line 186) — i.e. with a stray double-quote embedded in the name. The DAD_RE in src/listeners/messageDadMode.ts:36 strips leading decoration chars including '"' but the trailing close-quote is captured by `(.+?)` and survives normalization (only @ and # are stripped, src line 108-111). The test documents this as intended (comment line 185), but it is a genuine output-quality bug: user-supplied quoting leaks into the bot's public reply. Low severity (cosmetic, the @/# ping-safety strip is intact), but the test cements buggy behavior as a contract, making future cleanup look like a regression. Impact: minor malformed output; risk that the wrong behavior is treated as correct.
fix: If the trailing-quote leak is undesired, trim a matching set of trailing decoration chars from the captured name in the source and update the assertion to `Hi confused, I'm dad.`; otherwise leave as-is but relabel the test so it is clear this is a known-imperfect edge case, not a guaranteed contract.

title: `expect.any(Number)` misused as a mock return value, not an assertion
detail: The test "uses current timestamp when joinedAt not provided" passes an asymmetric matcher (`expect.any(Number)`) inside `mockGet.mockReturnValueOnce({ joined_at: expect.any(Number), flagged_at: expect.any(Number), ... })`. `expect.any(...)` only has meaning inside an `expect(...).toEqual(...)`/`toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` comparison; used as raw data it just stores a matcher object on the returned row. The test never asserts on `result` (the variable is assigned on line 245 but unused), and only checks `expect(mockRun).toHaveBeenCalled()`. So the intended verification (that `now` is used for joined_at/flagged_at when joinedAt is omitted) is not actually performed — the test would pass even if the source forwarded the wrong values. No production impact; it is a weak/ineffective test.
fix: Assert on the real call: capture `insertManualFlagStmt().run` arguments and assert `expect(mockRun).toHaveBeenCalledWith('guild-123','user-456', expect.any(Number), expect.any(Number), 'No join date', 'mod-789')`, verifying joined_at === flagged_at === a recent epoch. Remove the matcher from the mock return object.

title: All prepared statements share one mock object, so tests cannot verify the correct statement is used
detail: The `vi.mock` factory returns a single `statementFns` object for every `db.prepare(...)` call (`prepare: vi.fn(() => statementFns)`). auditSessionStore prepares 7 distinct statements at module load, all of which alias the same `run`/`get`/`all` mocks. Consequently assertions like `expect(mockFns.run).toHaveBeenCalled()` in the updateProgress/markUserScanned/complete/cancel tests cannot distinguish which SQL ran — a copy-paste bug that pointed `updateProgress` at, say, the cancel statement would not be caught. It works today only because each test invokes exactly one store function. Fragile, not currently failing.
fix: Have the prepare mock key off the SQL string (e.g., `vi.fn((sql) => stmtFnsBySql(sql))`) and assert against the specific statement, or at minimum assert `toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` on the exact bind parameters so the intended statement/argument order is pinned.

title: Test uses 0-100 nsfw scores while real callers pass a 0-1 scale, so the test does not pin the score contract
detail: `upsertNsfwFlag` is a passthrough, so these tests (passing nsfwScore 80/85/95) correctly verify argument forwarding. However the actual callers disagree on units: src/commands/audit/nsfw.ts and src/features/auditRunner.ts pass `visionResult.adultScore` (0-1, threshold 0.8), while src/features/avatarNsfwMonitor.ts passes `visionScore`. The store test asserting 0-100 values neither documents nor enforces the real-world scale, so a future unit mismatch among callers (e.g., one site storing 0.85 and another 85 into the same nsfw_flags.nsfw_score column) would not be detected by this suite. The store interface comment (src/store/nsfwFlagsStore.ts:50) says "0-1 probability", contradicting the test data and at least one caller.
fix: Pick one canonical scale for nsfw_score, document it on the store, and update the test to use that scale; add a caller-level test (or a normalization in upsertNsfwFlag) so mixed 0-1 vs 0-100 values cannot reach the column.

title: createMockInteraction clobbers the enriched member/user/guild mocks with the caller's raw partial via trailing `...rest` spread
detail: The factory builds a full `user` (l274), `guild` (l275) and `member` (l276, which injects `roles`, `permissions`, `user`, `send`, `kick`, `ban`). It sets `user`/`member`/`guild` in the returned object (l280-282), but then spreads `...rest` again at l301. Because `rest` still contains the caller's original `user`/`guild`/`member` partials, those raw partials overwrite the enriched mocks. So `createMockInteraction({ member: { permissions: { has: () => true } } })` yields `interaction.member` === just `{ permissions: {...} }` — `member.roles`, `member.user`, `member.send`, etc. are now `undefined`. Note `guildId: guild.id` (l283) is computed before the clobber so it still points at the default guild id even when a custom `guild` partial without an `id` is supplied, producing an inconsistent interaction (guildId from default guild, guild object from the partial). Concrete impact: any test that overrides member/user/guild (e.g. tests/commands/stats/approvalRate.test.ts:109 `createMockInteraction({ member } as any)`) silently receives a degraded mock; code under test that reads member.roles.cache or member.user can hit undefined and either throw or take an unintended branch, making the test weaker/greener than it appears. Same pattern exists in createMockButtonInteraction (l315-339, `...overrides` at l338) and createMockModalInteraction (l353-380, `...rest` at l379).
fix: Drop user/guild/member out of the trailing spread so the enriched objects win, e.g. destructure them out: `const { user: _u, guild: _g, member: _m, ...restNoEntities } = rest;` and spread `...restNoEntities`, OR merge instead of replace: build the return object then deep-merge only the remaining keys. Apply the same fix to the button and modal factories.

title: "allows direct ID routes when enabled" test never exercises the direct-ID path it claims to cover
detail: src/web/badgeEndpoint.ts captures `ALLOW_DIRECT_ID_ROUTES` at module import time (badgeEndpoint.ts l40-42), so setting `process.env.BADGE_ALLOW_DIRECT_DISCORD_ID_ROUTES = 'true'` inside the test (l141) has no effect on the already-loaded module — the test's own comment (l142-145) admits this. The request it then issues, `/badges/movie-tier-1.svg`, is served by `tryServeRegistryBadge` because a matching manifest entry was seeded (l147-148); that branch returns 200 regardless of the direct-ID flag. So the assertion `expect(r.status).toBe(200)` (l151) passes via the registry path, not the direct-ID-enabled path. The genuinely flag-gated code (badgeEndpoint.ts l163-187, the `/badges/(roles|channels|users)/<id>.svg` branch and its enabled behavior) is therefore never tested. Impact: false confidence — a regression that broke direct-ID-route serving when the env flag is on would not be caught by this test.
fix: Make the flag injectable so it can be toggled per-test (e.g. read `process.env` at call time inside handleBadgeRequest, or thread an `allowDirectIdRoutes` option through `BadgeStoreConfig`), then assert against a real `/badges/roles/<digits>.svg` request returning a rendered badge (200 + image/svg+xml) when enabled and 404 `direct_id_routes_disabled` when disabled.

title: Linked Roles "security" test suite never imports the module under test — every assertion is tautological
detail: The file's header claims it is "Unit tests for Discord Linked Roles OAuth2 server module" verifying "rate limiting, state validation, and HTML escaping". In reality it never imports src/web/linkedRoles.ts. Every test re-declares the value it then asserts (e.g. lines 26-28 `const RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = 60*1000; expect(RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS).toBe(60000)`; lines 49-69 reimplement checkRateLimit logic locally; lines 104-138 define a private copy of escapeHtml and test that copy). These assertions pass unconditionally regardless of what the real module does. Concrete impact: this is the only test coverage for an UNAUTHENTICATED, internet-facing HTTP server that performs OAuth2 token exchange, CSRF state validation (validateState), per-IP rate limiting, and HTML escaping of attacker-controlled query params (error/state -> escapeHtml) into HTML responses. A regression in the real escapeHtml (XSS), in validateState (CSRF bypass / replay), in checkRateLimit's `>=` boundary (off-by-one allowing an extra request), or in the redirect_uri/scope construction would be completely invisible to CI because no test exercises the real code. The suite gives false confidence that these security behaviors are pinned when they are not.
fix: Import the real functions from src/web/linkedRoles.ts (export them or extract the pure helpers — escapeHtml, checkRateLimit, generateState, validateState, evictOldestEntries — into a testable module) and assert against those exports. For escapeHtml/validateState/checkRateLimit drive the actual implementation with adversarial inputs (e.g. expired/replayed state tokens, count == maxRequests boundary, `<script>` payloads) instead of local copies.

title: "timestamp is NaN" test does not exercise the NaN guard it claims to cover
detail: The test builds its body as `{ ...validEvent, timestamp: NaN }` (the `body` path, not `rawBody`). makeEvent serializes it via JSON.stringify, and JSON.stringify converts NaN to `null` (verified: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify({timestamp:NaN})).timestamp === null, typeof === 'object'). So by the time the handler (web/src/routes/api/internal/events/+server.ts) parses the body, `event.timestamp` is null. The handler returns 400 via the `typeof event.timestamp !== "number"` branch (line 67) — the same branch the "timestamp is not a finite number" test ('yesterday' string) already covers. The dedicated `!Number.isFinite(event.timestamp)` guard (line 68) therefore has ZERO test coverage from this suite: no test ever feeds the handler a value that is a number but non-finite. A regression that deletes the `!Number.isFinite(...)` check (e.g. allowing Infinity, which a buggy bot serializer or a non-JSON caller could send) would not be caught. The test passes, giving false confidence.
fix: Drive the handler with a raw body so NaN/Infinity survive to the parser, e.g. `evt({ secret: SECRET, rawBody: JSON.stringify({...validEvent, timestamp: 1}).replace('1','Infinity') })` or post a literal `{"type":"x:y","timestamp":Infinity,"payload":{}}` as rawBody (note: invalid JSON, so instead inject via a number that bypasses stringify). Simplest: add a case that posts rawBody `'{"type":"x:y","payload":{},"timestamp":1e999}'` (1e999 parses to Infinity) and assert 400; that actually exercises the Number.isFinite branch.

title: GUILD_ID env var set at module load and never restored (inconsistent with sibling tests)
detail: Line 16 does `process.env.GUILD_ID = "g1";` at top-level module scope with no afterAll/afterEach restore. Sibling route tests in the same directory (export.test.ts:32-42, welcome.mentionables.test.ts:35-45, art.users.search.test.ts:34-44) deliberately snapshot `ORIG_GUILD_ID` and restore it in afterEach to avoid leaking. This test (and review.profile.test.ts:33, which also sets it without restore) mutates global process.env without cleanup. Under Vitest's default isolated per-file pool this does not currently leak across files, so it is not actively breaking; but it is a latent isolation hazard if the suite is ever switched to a shared/non-isolated pool (e.g. `pool: 'threads'` with `isolate: false`) — a test that asserts behavior when GUILD_ID is *unset* would then see the leaked "g1".
fix: Mirror the sibling pattern: capture `const ORIG_GUILD_ID = process.env.GUILD_ID;` and restore it in an afterAll/afterEach (`if (ORIG_GUILD_ID === undefined) delete process.env.GUILD_ID; else process.env.GUILD_ID = ORIG_GUILD_ID;`). Apply the same to review.profile.test.ts.

title: failed (image-error) state never resets when src prop changes
detail: `let failed = $state(false)` is set to true in the onerror handler (line 46) and `resolved = $derived(src && !failed ? src : null)` (line 23). There is no $effect that resets `failed` when `src` changes. Because this component is reused for the same keyed entity (ReviewCard list is keyed by item.id in web/src/routes/dashboard/reviews/+layout.svelte:275, and avatarUrl is passed straight through), if a Discord CDN avatar URL 404s once (expired signed CDN URL is common) `failed` latches true. If that same instance later receives a new, valid `src` for the same application (e.g. via SSE-driven live update of the queue), `resolved` stays null and the component permanently shows the initials placeholder instead of the now-valid avatar until the instance is destroyed. Same applies anywhere Avatar is given a changing src.
fix: Reset the error state when src changes, e.g. add `$effect(() => { void src; failed = false; });` (or `$effect.pre`) so a new src clears the stale failure. Alternatively key the on src.

title: navigator.clipboard.writeText promise not awaited — shows false 'Copied!' on failure
detail: copy() calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(value)` without awaiting or catching the returned promise, then unconditionally sets `copied = true` and shows the 'Copied!' toast (lines 11-14, 27). clipboard.writeText rejects in insecure contexts (non-HTTPS), when the document is not focused, or when permission is denied. In those cases the value is NOT on the clipboard yet the UI reports success, and the unhandled rejection surfaces as an uncaught promise error. For a copy-the-Discord-ID affordance used throughout the review/config UI, the user is misled into thinking the ID was copied.
fix: Make copy() async and gate the success UI on the resolved promise: `try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(value); copied = true; ... } catch { /* show failure or fallback to execCommand */ }`. Also guard for `navigator.clipboard` being undefined.

title: Numeric coercion keyed off rule.type while input rendering keyed off type prop (dual source of truth)
detail: saveEdit() decides whether to coerce editValue to a Number using `rule.type` (line 102), but the template decides whether to render a <input type="number"> using the separate `type` prop (line 208). These come from two independently maintained maps: the `type` prop originates from FIELD_META in web/src/lib/server/queries/config.ts, while `rule` originates from CONFIG_FIELD_RULES in web/src/lib/shared/configValidation.ts. They currently agree for every key, but if the two maps ever diverge for a field (easy to do since both must be hand-edited), the row could render a number input yet submit the raw string (no coercion), or coerce a non-numeric field — sending a wrong-typed value to /api/config/update. There is also a latent NaN path: if a field is numeric and non-nullable, an empty input is coerced to `Number('') === 0`-> actually `editValue===''` branch sends null, but a value like 'abc' yields Number('abc')=NaN which validateConfigField rejects, so that case is safe.
fix: Derive both the input type and the coercion decision from a single source (prefer `rule.type` everywhere, falling back to `type` only when rule is undefined), or assert at build/test time that FIELD_META[key].type === CONFIG_FIELD_RULES[key].type for all keys.

title: onPaste re-renders the whole editor and forces caret to end, dropping paste position
detail: onPaste() inserts pasted text via document.execCommand('insertText', ...) (line 323), then immediately calls readEditor() and renderEditor(raw) to rebuild every node (lines 324-325), and finally moves the selection to the end of the editor with range.collapse(false) (lines 327-332). Two issues: (1) pasting in the middle of existing text yanks the caret to the very end of the message, so subsequent typing appends rather than continuing at the paste point — a real editing-correctness/UX defect for a multi-paragraph welcome template; (2) document.execCommand is deprecated, but more importantly the full re-render on every paste is unnecessary churn. Functionality (token/chip parsing) still works, so impact is limited to caret/UX.
fix: Avoid the destructive full re-render on paste: insert the plain text at the current range and only re-parse the affected text node, restoring the caret to just after the inserted text rather than collapsing to the editor end. If a full re-render is required, compute and restore the caret offset instead of jumping to the end.

title: Flat (no-change) delta emits the green UP-vote emoji in the copied newsletter
detail: In numDelta (line 36-37) and pctDelta (line 50-51) the `direction` is computed as `abs > 0 ? 'up' : abs < 0 ? 'down' : 'flat'`, but the `emoji` is computed as `abs >= 0 ? UP_EMOJI : DOWN_EMOJI`. When the current and previous values are equal and non-zero (the `prev===0 && cur===0` early-returns do not fire), `abs === 0`, so `direction` is correctly 'flat' but `emoji` is UP_EMOJI. The Discord markdown builder (discordMarkdown, lines 76 and 92-102) unconditionally prints `d.X.emoji` next to the percentage, so a metric that did not change week-over-week renders a green up-vote (<:Iup_Vote:...>) beside a '+0.0%' line. The text copied for the public newsletter therefore signals growth where there was none.
fix: Derive the emoji from `direction` instead of the `>= 0` sign, e.g. `emoji: direction === 'down' ? DOWN_EMOJI : direction === 'up' ? UP_EMOJI : NEUTRAL_EMOJI` (or reuse UP only for true 'up'). At minimum compute emoji from the already-correct `direction` value so flat never maps to the up emoji.

title: toLocaleString() used in an SSR+hydrated component despite the repo's explicit locale-safe formatting convention
detail: This component is rendered on the server and then hydrated on the client (the /dashboard/pulse route does NOT set csr=false; it uses SSE, onDestroy, invalidateAll). Every numeric value here is formatted with Number.prototype.toLocaleString() (newMembers, voiceMinutes, memberCount, onlineCount, boostCount, channel minutes, previewRows values, etc.). The codebase deliberately avoids toLocaleString on the server: web/src/lib/server/queries/pulse.ts (lines 35-38) and web/src/lib/components/observatory/format.ts (lines 1-13) both implement a regex-based `fmt()` precisely because 'locale APIs vary by server locale.' If the server's default ICU locale and the visitor's browser locale group/format numbers differently (e.g. server '1,234' vs a de-DE browser '1.234'), the hydrated DOM will not match the SSR HTML, producing a Svelte hydration mismatch for these text nodes. The copied Discord markdown (discordMarkdown) is computed identically on both sides too, so the same locale dependence leaks into newsletter output.
fix: Reuse the existing locale-safe formatter (import `fmt` from server queries is server-only, so add/import a shared client-safe `fmtInt` like the one in observatory/format.ts) for all displayed and markdown numbers instead of toLocaleString(), matching the rest of the dashboard.

title: Copy-to-clipboard silently no-ops in non-secure contexts with no user feedback
detail: copyToClipboard() awaits navigator.clipboard.writeText(...). In a non-secure context (HTTP) or older browser, `navigator.clipboard` is undefined and the access throws a TypeError that is swallowed by the empty `catch {}` (the comment even says 'Fallback for non-secure contexts' but no fallback is implemented). The `copied` state never flips, so the 'Copy for Newsletter' button appears to do nothing when clicked and the user gets no error indication. Impact is limited to UX, but the labelled-but-missing fallback is misleading.
fix: Either implement an actual fallback (e.g. a hidden textarea + document.execCommand('copy'), or surface a toast on failure) or feature-detect `navigator.clipboard` and disable/relabel the button when unavailable.

title: fmtDayShort returns 'undefined D' for an out-of-range month instead of falling back to the raw string
detail: fmtDayShort guards against a non-3-part string and against m/d being 0 or NaN (`if (!m || !d) return day`), but does not bound-check m to 1..12. For an input like '2025-13-05' (or any month > 12), `months[m-1]` is undefined and the function returns the string 'undefined 5'. Inputs come from DB day/week buckets so this is unlikely in practice, but a malformed or off-by-one bucket value would render literal 'undefined' in the Observatory axis/labels (DivergingBars, LineChart, QotdFunnel all call it) rather than degrading to the raw value like the other guard paths do.
fix: Add a range check: `if (m < 1 || m > 12 || d < 1 || d > 31) return day;` before indexing months, so any out-of-range value falls back to the raw `day` string consistent with the existing guards.

title: Case-insensitive handbook href rewrite is effectively case-sensitive; mixed-case .md links 404
detail: rewriteHandbookHref() looks up the slug via HANDBOOK_FILENAME_TO_SLUG[filename] ?? [filename.toUpperCase()] ?? [filename.toLowerCase()]. The map keys store a lowercase extension (e.g. 'BOT-HANDBOOK.md', 'TICKET-SYSTEM-GUIDE.md'). filename.toUpperCase() converts 'bot-handbook.md' into 'BOT-HANDBOOK.MD' (extension uppercased too), which does NOT match the key 'BOT-HANDBOOK.md', and filename.toLowerCase() yields 'bot-handbook.md' which also does not match an uppercase-prefixed key. So the two fallbacks are dead for every key except the all-lowercase one ('slash-commands.md'). A cross-reference href written with any non-canonical casing (e.g. 'Bot-Handbook.md' or 'bot-handbook.MD') falls through all three lookups and is returned unmodified, so the rendered link points at a raw '.md' path that 404s instead of '/handbook/<slug>'. The comment explicitly promises 'Case-insensitive lookup', so behavior contradicts intent.
fix: Normalize once and compare against a normalized map, e.g. build a lowercase-keyed index: `const byLower = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(HANDBOOK_FILENAME_TO_SLUG).map(([k,v])=>[k.toLowerCase(),v]));` then `const slug = byLower[filename.toLowerCase()];`. This makes the lookup truly case-insensitive across the whole filename including extension.

title: `exactOnly` ([GK]-only) permission is parsed but ignored when computing canRun, mislabeling locked commands as runnable
detail: parsePermissionLine() distinguishes '[GK]' (GK exclusively, exactOnly=true) from 'GK+' (GK and above). decorate() sets canRun = meetsTier(viewerTier, requiredTier), which only checks the viewer sits at or above the required tier and never consults permission.exactOnly. For a command documented as '[GK]' (exclusive), an admin/owner viewer gets meetsTier()=true, so PermissionBadge renders 'You can run this.' (title at PermissionBadge.svelte:20) even though, per the exactOnly semantics and the bot's isGatekeeper() gate in web/src/lib/server/roles.ts, only the literal Gatekeeper role may act. The badge also shows '(exclusive)' (PermissionBadge.svelte:12) while simultaneously claiming the higher-tier viewer can run it — contradictory guidance. This is a documentation/affordance correctness bug only; it grants no real capability (actual authorization is enforced server-side in the bot/API), hence low severity.
fix: When permission.exactOnly is true, compute canRun as an exact-tier match (viewerTier === requiredTier) rather than meetsTier(), or pass exactOnly into a dedicated check. Thread permission.exactOnly through SectionToken too if exclusive narrative sections are possible.

title: push.db default location diverges from main DB default directory when DB_PATH is unset
detail: When DB_PATH is unset, push-db.ts derives dbPath = path.dirname(path.join('data','data.db')) + '/push.db' = '<cwd>/data/push.db' (relative to process.cwd()). The main read-only connection in web/src/lib/server/db.ts uses a different default for the same unset DB_PATH: path.resolve(process.cwd(), '..', 'data', 'data.db'), i.e. '<cwd>/../data/'. So with DB_PATH unset the two modules resolve their data directories to different places (sibling '../data' vs '<cwd>/data'). Because push.db is an independent file this is not data corruption, but it makes the push subscription store land in an unexpected directory (and a different one than operators expect alongside data.db), risking 'lost' subscriptions after a deploy/path change and inconsistent behavior between the two DB modules. In production DB_PATH is presumably set (mitigating this), so severity is low.
fix: Resolve the push DB relative to the same base as db.ts. Mirror db.ts's default: `const mainDb = process.env.DB_PATH || path.resolve(process.cwd(), '..', 'data', 'data.db'); const dbPath = process.env.PUSH_DB_PATH || path.join(path.dirname(mainDb), 'push.db');` so both modules agree on the data directory regardless of DB_PATH being set.

title: Heatmap can include messages outside the requested range when span isn't a multiple of 7 days
detail: getHeatmapDataForRange computes weeksCount = ceil(spanS / 7d) and then carves 7-day windows strictly backwards from endS: weekEndS = endS - offset*7d, weekStartS = weekEndS - 7d. The oldest window therefore starts at endS - weeksCount*7d, which is EARLIER than the requested range.startS whenever (endS - startS) is not an exact multiple of 7 days. For a custom window (e.g., a 10-day or 40-day range from the dashboard time picker), this pulls message_activity rows from before the user-selected start into the totals/trends, so totalMessages, avgMessagesPerHour, busiest/least-active hours and week-over-week growth are computed over a wider span than requested. The COUNT/trends silently over-report.
fix: Clamp the oldest window to startS: compute weekStartS = Math.max(weekStartS, startS) for the final iteration (or derive weeksCount so the earliest weekStartS == startS). Alternatively iterate forward from startS and let the last week be the partial one, clamping weekEndS to endS.

title: Rolling 7-day window bucketed into a Mon–Sun grid double-counts a weekday and mislabels dates
detail: buildWeek receives an arbitrary [weekStartS, weekEndS) 7-day window (endS comes from nowS() snapped to the minute, not midnight/Monday). It then (a) builds the `dates` label array from the ISO Monday of weekStartS, and (b) buckets each message into grid[dayIndex][hour] purely by the message's UTC weekday. Because the window boundaries are not aligned to midnight, a 7-day span covers two partial occurrences of the same weekday (e.g., Wed 14:00 → next Wed 14:00 contains two Wednesdays). Both partial Wednesdays collapse into the same grid row, while the `dates`/startDate/endDate labels claim a clean Mon–Sun calendar week that does not correspond to the rows actually populated. The per-cell counts and the date headers shown to the user disagree.
fix: Align week windows to UTC midnight / ISO Monday before querying (floor weekStartS to the Monday 00:00:00 UTC and query [monday, monday+7d)), so each weekday appears exactly once and the grid matches the `dates` labels. Keep query window and label anchor identical.

title: Stale push subscriptions keep receiving tier-gated PII after a user is demoted or removed
detail: Tier on a push subscription is only refreshed reactively when a 'role:changed' SSE event arrives (updateTier on lines 87-96). If a moderator is demoted or leaves the guild while the bot/web is down, or if the role:changed event is never emitted for that user, their stored `tier` stays at the old (higher) value. pushBroadcast then still passes the hasMinTier check (line 122) and sends notifications whose body/data include sensitive content — applicant display names (review:submitted body, line 63) and appId, and modmail/audit context — to a device that should no longer have access. There is no authoritative re-check of the subscriber's current roles at send time; tier is trusted from the local push.db row.
fix: Treat the stored tier as a cache only: re-resolve the user's current tier at send time (or on a short TTL) via the Discord role source / session, and/or proactively delete subscriptions on demotion and guild-leave events. At minimum, run deleteStaleSubscriptions on role loss and verify tier against a fresh roles lookup before sending tier-restricted payloads.

title: setInterval cleanup timer is never cleared and is not unref'd
detail: A 24h setInterval is registered at module import for stale-subscription cleanup. The handle is never stored or cleared, and not .unref()'d. In the long-lived server this is benign, but in test/SSR module re-import or graceful-shutdown scenarios it leaks a timer and (without unref) can keep the event loop alive, preventing clean process exit. Combined with the side-effecting eventBus.subscribe(pushBroadcast) on import, repeated imports also stack duplicate subscribers/timers.
fix: Store the interval handle, call .unref() on it, and expose a disposer (or guard the module against double-initialization) so shutdown/tests can clear it.

title: getAuditSessionDetail has no guild scoping (latent IDOR) and is currently unused
detail: Unlike its guild-scoped siblings getAuditSessions/getActiveAuditSession, getAuditSessionDetail selects an audit_sessions row by sessionId alone with no guild_id predicate. It has no callers in the web app today (dead code), so it is not currently exploitable, but if wired to a route that takes a user-supplied id it would allow reading another guild's audit session in a multi-guild deployment. The deployment is currently single-guild (callers pass process.env.GUILD_ID), which also masks the impact.
fix: Add a guildId parameter and `AND guild_id = ?` predicate to match the other accessors, or delete the function if it stays unused.

title: getConfigSections does SELECT * and renders every non-hidden column verbatim, risking future secret leakage
detail: getConfigSections selects all guild_config columns and, for any column not in the small HIDDEN_COLUMNS set, renders the raw value to the admin dashboard under an 'Other' section (the doc comment explicitly states new columns appear automatically). guild_config currently holds no secrets, so this is not an active leak. However, the auto-include design means any future column that stores a webhook URL, API token, or verification secret would be exposed in plaintext on the config page without any code change, and HIDDEN_COLUMNS is easy to forget to update.
fix: Invert the model to an allow-list: only render columns present in FIELD_META (or an explicit visible set), and drop unknown columns instead of dumping them. This fails closed when new sensitive columns are added.

title: activeClaims counts all of a reviewer's claims with no guild or app-status filter
detail: activeClaims = COUNT(*) FROM review_claim WHERE reviewer_id = ? with no guild_id scope and no join to application status. Unlike pendingYours (which joins application and filters status IN submitted/needs_info), this counts every claim row the reviewer holds, including claims left attached to applications that were already decided (if claims are not deleted on decision) and, in a multi-guild setup, claims in other guilds. The dashboard 'active claims' figure can therefore overstate the reviewer's actually-open workload.
fix: Join review_claim to application and filter on a.guild_id = ? and a.status IN ('submitted','needs_info') (mirroring pendingYours), so 'active' reflects claims on still-open applications in this guild.

title: Artist-rotation 'next artist' selection is a check-then-act race (TOCTOU) across /redeemreward issue→confirm and concurrent invocations
detail: getNextArtist(guildId) (redeemreward.ts:192) is a pure SELECT (src/features/artistRotation/queue.ts:264-279) — it does NOT mutate the queue. The selected artistId is baked into the Confirm button customId (redeemreward.ts:283). The queue is only mutated by processAssignment() when Confirm is clicked (src/features/artistRotation/handlers.ts:228). handleConfirm trusts the command-time artistId and never (a) re-checks that this artist is still next, (b) consumes/dedupes confirmId, nor (c) applies any per-button cooldown (the cooldown in src/features/review/handlers/buttonCooldown.ts is review-only). Two realistic triggers: (1) two staff run /redeemreward (no override) before either confirms — getNextArtist returns the SAME artist both times, both confirm, the artist is assigned twice, gets two art jobs (createJob, handlers.ts:258), and processAssignment runs twice; (2) one staff double-clicks the single Confirm button — interactionCreate (src/events/interactionCreate.ts:599-613) dispatches each click as an independent interaction with no in-flight guard, so handleConfirm runs twice, creating two jobs and double-incrementing assignments. processAssignment itself is transactional, but the decision that feeds it is made far earlier, so the transaction does not close the window. Contrast: the byte-token confirm path explicitly added a race mitigation (src/features/byteTokenHandler.ts:353-382) while this path has none.
fix: Make the assignment idempotent and re-validated at confirm time: (a) persist pending redemptions keyed by confirmId and atomically consume the row inside processAssignment's transaction (reject if already consumed); and/or (b) for non-override flows, re-run getNextArtist INSIDE the same db.transaction() as processAssignment and assign whoever is actually next at confirm time rather than trusting the customId; and (c) add a short per-(user,confirmId) cooldown / disable the button immediately on first click (interaction.update removing components) to swallow double-clicks.

title: Recurring schedulers run on setInterval(async …) with no re-entrancy guard — overlapping ticks duplicate work
detail: Every scheduler uses `const i = setInterval(async () => { try { await work() } … }, MS)` with no 'is a previous run still in flight?' flag (securityAuditScheduler.ts:349, guildSnapshotScheduler.ts:117, staleApplicationCheck.ts:393, modMetricsScheduler.ts:100, byteMultiplierScheduler.ts:210, diskSpaceScheduler.ts:247, eventTimeoutScheduler.ts:83). setInterval does not await the callback, so if one run's awaited work (Discord REST, guild.fetch(), generateAuditDocs which walks all roles/channels + saves a snapshot) exceeds the interval, the next tick starts a second concurrent run. For securityAudit this means two overlapping runs each call generateAuditDocs/saveSnapshot (src/store/securitySnapshotStore.ts:243) and each post to the logging channel with leadership pings (securityAuditScheduler.ts:195) — duplicate critical-alert pings and a diff computed against a snapshot the other run just wrote. guildSnapshotScheduler additionally mutates module state `_snapshotCount` (guildSnapshotScheduler.ts:94) non-atomically across overlapping async runs, perturbing the 'fetch online every 6th run' cadence. Lower-frequency than finding #1 but unbounded if any single run hangs on a slow API call.
fix: Add a module-level `let running = false` (or a shared promise) guard at the top of each interval callback: `if (running) { logger.warn('previous run still in flight, skipping'); return; } running = true; try { await work() } finally { running = false; }`. This is the standard fix and also fixes the _snapshotCount/_lastAlertTime ordering issues for free.

title: verify_thread creation is check-then-act: concurrent guildMemberAdd can create duplicate/orphaned private threads
detail: ensureVerifyThreadForMember reads the verify_thread row (threadGate.ts:172) and, if absent, falls through to createVerifyThreadForUser, which performs an awaited Discord thread create (threadGate.ts:231) and only THEN upserts the verify_thread row (threadGate.ts:256). The check and the insert straddle multiple awaits with no lock or pre-claim. If guildMemberAdd fires twice in quick succession for the same user (Discord occasionally re-delivers gateway events; a fast leave→rejoin also triggers it), both invocations observe no existing row, both create a private thread, and the second upsert (ON CONFLICT(guild_id,user_id) DO UPDATE) overwrites thread_id with the second thread — orphaning the first thread (it lingers under the parent channel, invisible-leak). The ON CONFLICT keeps the DB single-valued (so no data corruption), which is why this is low severity, but it leaks Discord threads and can post two welcome pings to the user.
fix: Pre-claim the slot before creating the Discord thread: INSERT the verify_thread row with a placeholder state in a transaction using INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and check changes — if 0, another handler is already creating it, so bail. Alternatively guard ensureVerifyThreadForMember with a per-(guildId,userId) in-process async mutex so concurrent joins for the same user serialize.

title: Byte-token redemption confirm can be double-processed despite partial mitigation (stale role-cache check)
detail: handleConfirm gates redemption on guildMember.roles.cache.has(tokenConfig.tokenRoleId) (byteTokenHandler.ts:283) using a member object fetched at 268. On a rapid double-click the two interactions are dispatched independently (interactionCreate.ts:616-630) with no confirmId consumption and no cooldown; both can pass the cache.has() gate before either roles.remove (line 314) propagates, so the token role can be 'spent' once but the redemption body (upsertActiveMultiplier at 385 and the audit log at 397) can execute twice. The 'Step 3.5' cleanup (353-382) only removes duplicate *multiplier roles* to prevent stacking; it does not prevent the duplicate DB upsert or duplicate audit entry, and it relies on a refetch that may also be stale. This is materially better than /redeemreward (which has no mitigation at all) but is not race-free.
fix: Treat the token-role removal as the atomic claim: only proceed if roles.remove succeeds AND a fresh fetch (force, not cache) confirmed possession, OR persist+consume the confirmId in a DB transaction so the second click is rejected. Disable the Confirm button on first click via interaction.update to swallow double-clicks.

title: notifyLimiter canNotify()→send→recordNotify() is non-atomic; concurrent forum posts can exceed the hourly cap
detail: The limiter is a read-then-act pair: callers invoke canNotify() (notifyLimiter.ts:73), then perform an awaited Discord send, then call recordNotify() (113). Because recordNotify only records AFTER the async send completes, multiple forum-post events arriving within the same window all observe the pre-increment count in canNotify() and all pass, then each records — so the effective rate can exceed notify_max_per_hour / ignore the cooldown under burst. The file itself documents 'if someone calls recordNotify without calling canNotify first they bypass the rate limit' and that ordering is trust-the-caller. Single-process, but Node interleaves at each await, so this is a genuine TOCTOU for the abuse-prevention control it is meant to enforce (mass thread-creation spam).
fix: Make reserve-and-record atomic: have canNotify() itself record the timestamp (reserve a slot) when it returns ok, and add a release/rollback path if the send fails, rather than recording only after the await. Since better-sqlite3/JS is single-threaded, doing the check+push synchronously in one function with no await between them closes the window.

title: Analytics CSV export can hang forever (retaining full CSV buffer + interaction) due to end-listener race
detail: In the /stats export flow the handler builds a PassThrough, attaches a 'data' listener that accumulates the entire CSV into `chunks: Buffer[]`, then calls `streamReviewActionsCSV(opts, stream)` and `await`s it. Inside src/lib/csv.ts (line 253) `streamReviewActionsCSV` itself calls `stream.end()` on the success path and then resolves. Only AFTER the await resolves does command.ts register `await new Promise(resolve => stream.on('end', resolve))` (line 444-446). Because the PassThrough is already flowing (a 'data' listener is attached) and `end()` was already called inside the awaited promise, the terminal 'end' event can be emitted before this late listener is attached. When that happens the Promise never resolves: the command handler is stuck awaiting forever, permanently retaining the accumulated `chunks` array (the entire CSV, up to many MB for large exports), the PassThrough, the AttachmentBuilder closure, and the un-replied Discord interaction. Repeated exports that lose this race accumulate retained buffers and pending promises in the bot process. This is a cross-file trust bug: command.ts assumes 'end' will fire after it awaits, but csv.ts ends the stream before returning.
fix: Register the completion listener BEFORE awaiting the producer, e.g. capture `const done = once(stream, 'end')` (or use `stream.promises.finished(stream)` / `pipeline`) prior to calling streamReviewActionsCSV, then `await Promise.all([exportPromise, done])`. Better: have streamReviewActionsCSV NOT call stream.end() and let the caller own lifecycle, or collect via `await text(stream)` from node:stream/consumers. Also add an `'error'` handler so a producer error rejects the collection promise instead of leaving it pending.

title: streamReviewActionsCSV does not end/destroy the stream on error path
detail: On the happy path `stream.end()` is called at line 253. In the catch block (lines 268-271) the function logs and re-throws without calling `stream.end()` or `stream.destroy(err)`.
