The sole current caller (src/features/analytics/command.ts) wraps the call in a try/catch and lets the PassThrough go out of scope, so today this only fails to propagate an 'error'/'close' to the consumer rather than leaking a long-lived resource. However the function is exported as a general utility (Writable param), and any future caller that pipes this stream somewhere persistent (file handle, HTTP response) would be left with a stream that never ends or errors — a half-open resource leak. The producer should always terminate the stream it was handed.
fix: In the catch block call `stream.destroy(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)))` (or `stream.end()`), before/instead of re-throwing, so the writable is always terminated exactly once regardless of success or failure.

title: Cleanup interval is never unref'd or cleared (inconsistent with every other scheduler/limiter)
detail: `setInterval(cleanupOldCooldowns, CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS)` at module load is neither stored, `.unref()`'d, nor cleared on shutdown. Every other interval in this codebase (notifyLimiter, traceStore, all src/scheduler/* schedulers, badge live updates, dmVerification, movieNight) is explicitly `.unref()`'d and most expose a stop/destroy. The code comment even acknowledges 'This interval is never cleared'. Functional impact in production is small because gracefulShutdown calls `process.exit(0)` explicitly, but: (a) it keeps the event loop alive, so if the explicit exit path is ever bypassed the process will not exit on its own; and (b) it leaks the timer in tests/embedding scenarios that import this module (the very hang the comment warns about). It is the one outlier from an otherwise consistent, leak-safe pattern.
fix: Capture the handle (`const cleanupTimer = setInterval(...)`), call `cleanupTimer.unref()`, and export a `stopRateLimiterCleanup()` that does `clearInterval`. Optionally wire that into the gracefulShutdown cleanup block in src/startup/ready.ts alongside the other limiter teardowns.

title: Initial-delay setTimeout is not tracked or cleared by stopStaleApplicationScheduler
detail: startStaleApplicationScheduler schedules a one-shot `setTimeout(..., 15000)` for the initial check but never stores the handle; stopStaleApplicationScheduler (line 419) only clears the periodic interval `_activeInterval`. The same pattern exists in opsHealthScheduler.ts (line 117, 10s) and diskSpaceScheduler.ts (line 236, 15s). If the bot receives SIGTERM within the initial delay window, gracefulShutdown runs stopSchedulers() but this pending timer survives, holding the Client reference and able to fire its async check (DB query + Discord API calls) after teardown has begun closing the DB/destroying the client. The timer is not `.unref()`'d either, so it briefly keeps the loop alive. Low impact because the window is short and process.exit follows, but it is a genuine untracked timer that can run work post-shutdown.
fix: Store the initial-delay timeout in a module variable (e.g. `_initialTimer`), call `.unref()` on it, and `clearTimeout(_initialTimer)` inside the stop function. Apply the same fix to opsHealthScheduler.ts and diskSpaceScheduler.ts.

title: Byte token redemption is non-atomic and has no rollback — a failed grant destroys the token entitlement with nothing in return
detail: handleConfirm() mutates Discord and the DB in this order inside one try/catch with no compensating action: (1) remove the token role (line 314), (2) remove other multiplier roles (lines 321-345), (3) add the multiplier role (line 348), (3.5) refetch + cleanup (lines 357-382), (4) upsertActiveMultiplier writes the DB source-of-truth (lines 385-394). If ANY step after the token removal throws (e.g. roles.add at 348 hits a 50013/permission change, a 429, or the gateway hiccups), control jumps to the catch at 449 which only shows an error embed. The token role is already gone, the multiplier role was never granted, and NO row was written to active_byte_multipliers. The user has permanently spent a finite token entitlement and received zero value, with no automatic recovery path (the scheduler only removes roles; nothing re-grants tokens). Because the multiplier roles ARE the economy (see byteMultiplierStore multiplier_value is never read — XP boost is driven purely by role possession), this is direct, silent value destruction. The DB write should be the authoritative claim and should happen first/atomically, or the whole sequence must be made compensatable.
fix: Make the token claim the atomic gate before any irreversible Discord mutation. Insert into a redeemed-tokens ledger (or upsert active_byte_multipliers) inside a transaction FIRST; only on a successful insert proceed to Discord role changes. On any Discord failure after the token role is removed, re-add the token role in a finally/catch (compensating action) and delete the just-written DB row, so the user keeps their token. Alternatively, add the multiplier role BEFORE removing the token role, so a mid-flight failure leaves the user holding the token (recoverable) rather than holding nothing.

title: Byte token double-click TOCTOU: entitlement gated only by eventually-consistent Discord role cache; concurrent confirms re-grant and reset expiry
detail: The sole entitlement check before redeeming is guildMember.roles.cache.has(tokenConfig.tokenRoleId) at line 283. The confirm button is never disabled and the ephemeral message's components are not cleared until the final editReply, so a user can fire two ButtonInteractions on the same button. interactionCreate routes each to a separate concurrent handleUseByteButton invocation (events/interactionCreate.ts:616-629); discord.js does NOT serialize interactions for a user. Both invocations deferUpdate, both fetch the member, both observe the token role still present (it is only removed at line 314, after several awaited REST calls), and both proceed. The CHANGELOG (line 322) and the Step-3.5 cleanup (lines 357-382) only address stacking of DISTINCT multiplier roles — and that cleanup explicitly excludes the role just added (roleId !== tokenConfig.multiplierRoleId at 361), so two same-rarity redemptions both add the same role (idempotent) and both reach upsertActiveMultiplier. The upsert's ON CONFLICT (byteMultiplierStore.ts:66-79) overwrites expires_at with a brand-new full-duration value every time, so the second click silently refreshes/extends the multiplier window for a single token. There is no atomic DB claim of the token. Worse, for the epic/legendary pair that share multiplier role 1405369052829974543 (usebyte.ts:87,96), holding both tokens and redeeming epic then legendary extends the same role's expiry to the longer 72h with the de-stack logic seeing nothing to remove.
fix: Gate redemption on an atomic DB claim, not Discord role state. Before any role mutation, run an INSERT OR IGNORE / UPDATE...WHERE into a per-token redemption ledger keyed by (guild_id, user_id, token_rarity) (or a UNIQUE claim row) and bail if changes===0. Additionally disable the confirm button immediately (interaction.update components disabled) at the very start of handleConfirm before deferring, and key the confirmId so a replayed click is rejected. Make the ON CONFLICT path additive/longest-wins on expires_at rather than blindly overwriting, so a stray second write can't silently shorten or refresh a window.

title: Patreon art entitlements with quantity > 1 are permanently under-granted — the second emoji ticket is lost on first redemption
detail: PATREON_ART_ENTITLEMENTS gives '[Patreon] Legendary Fiona' emoji:2 (line 39 region). handlePatreonArtRewards computes delta = entitlement - alreadyGranted, assigns the ticket ROLE exactly once regardless of delta (comment at 187-188 says 'For delta > 1 ... we assign the role once'), then sets quantity_granted to the full entitlement via the high-water-mark MAX() upsert (lines 96-104). The ticket role is a single binary 'has an emoji ticket' marker. Redemption (src/features/artistRotation/handlers.ts:125-145) removes that role after ONE use and tracks nothing about remaining quantity — there is no redeemed/remaining counter anywhere (confirmed: patreon_art_granted has only quantity_granted, migrations/062, and roles.ts:725-730 only displays it). After the first emoji redemption the role is gone, but getGrantedQuantity returns 2 >= entitlement 2, so the periodic sweep (patreonRoleDedup.ts:149-159 → handlePatreonArtRewards every 10 min) hits 'entitlement <= alreadyGranted' (line 180) and never re-grants. Net result: a Legendary Fiona patron pays for 2 emoji tickets but can only ever redeem 1. The economy under-pays the highest-tier supporter.
fix: Track redemptions, not just grants. Add a redeemed counter (or remaining = quantity_granted - redeemed) to patreon_art_granted; decrement/increment it in the /redeemreward confirm handler. Re-grant the ticket role whenever remaining > 0 and the user lacks it. Alternatively, model quantity>1 entitlements as multiple distinct redeemable units rather than one binary role. Until fixed, no tier should define quantity>1 for a single binary ticket role.

title: Scheduler deletes the multiplier DB row even when panic mode blocks role removal, and SELECT-then-DELETE is non-atomic across overlapping ticks
detail: cleanupExpiredMultipliers calls removeExpiredMultipliers() (store line 37) which SELECTs all expired rows and then DELETEs them (byteMultiplierStore.ts:182-204) as two separate statements, not inside a db.transaction. The scheduler runs an immediate startup pass (lines 197-207) AND a periodic interval (lines 210-218); if the startup pass is still awaiting Discord REST when the first interval fires (or any tick runs long), a second invocation can SELECT the same not-yet-deleted rows and process them twice — double-removing roles and double-logging byte_multiplier_expired to the audit trail. Separately, processExpiredMultiplier returns early under panic mode (lines 100-109) AFTER the row has already been deleted from the DB, so the multiplier role is left on the member with no tracking row; when panic clears, nothing will ever remove it (the comment at 105-108 acknowledges this requires manual cleanup). Both issues stem from deleting the authoritative row before the side effect that the row exists to drive is confirmed.
fix: Wrap the SELECT+DELETE in a single db.transaction so a batch is claimed atomically (better-sqlite3 transactions are synchronous/ACID), and guard cleanupExpiredMultipliers with a reentrancy lock so overlapping ticks can't both run. For panic mode, check isPanicMode BEFORE deleting the row (or re-insert the row when skipping due to panic) so expired-but-unremoved multipliers are retried after panic clears instead of being orphaned.

title: redeemreward override path increments artist stats via non-atomic read-modify pattern outside the rotation transaction
detail: The non-override path uses processAssignment() which is a proper db.transaction (queue.ts:374-427) and is explicitly there to prevent two simultaneous /redeemreward confirms double-assigning the same next artist (queue.ts comment 366-369). But the override branch (handlers.ts:237-242) instead calls getArtist() at line 224 and then incrementAssignments() at 240 as two separate statements with no transaction. incrementAssignments itself is a single atomic UPDATE (queue.ts:357-359), so the count won't be lost, but the surrounding read (oldPosition via getArtist at 224) and the assignment-log write (logAssignment at 245) are not coordinated with it, so concurrent overrides on the same artist can interleave and produce inconsistent oldPosition reporting in the result embed/log. Impact is limited to stats/log accuracy (no economy double-spend, since override intentionally does not rotate), hence low severity.
fix: For consistency and future-proofing, route the override path through a small transaction that re-reads state and increments atomically (mirroring processAssignment but without the position move), rather than mixing a cached getArtist() read with a separate incrementAssignments() write.

title: replyOrEdit silently drops the ephemeral flag and edits the source message after deferUpdate(), clobbering shared review/confirmation cards
detail: replyOrEdit() decides between editReply/followUp/reply purely on interaction.deferred/replied, but discord.js sets deferred=true for BOTH deferReply() and deferUpdate(). The deferred branch (line 503-506) strips flags (`const { flags, ...editPayload } = withFlags`) and calls editReply(). After a component interaction has called deferUpdate(), editReply() edits the ORIGINAL message the component was attached to — it does NOT create an ephemeral reply. So every caller that does `deferUpdate()` then `replyOrEdit({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral })` (1) loses ephemerality and (2) overwrites the source message. Concrete, routinely-triggered case: src/features/review/handlers/claimHandlers.ts handleClaimToggle — two mods click Claim at once; the loser hits ClaimError ALREADY_CLAIMED and calls replyOrEdit({content:'This application is already claimed by another moderator.', flags: Ephemeral}) (claimHandlers.ts:62-67). Because handleReviewButton already called deferUpdate() (buttons.ts:177-181), this becomes editReply on the review card: the embed, applicant info, and all action buttons are replaced with the bare public sentence, destroying the shared card for every mod. Same pattern: claimHandlers.ts:74,91,178,190,243 (the 'unclaimed successfully' / 'not owner' / perm-rejected messages all request Ephemeral and all instead wipe the card publicly).
fix: Distinguish deferReply-state from deferUpdate-state. Track how the interaction was acknowledged (e.g., set a flag when deferUpdate is used, or check interaction.isMessageComponent() && deferred) and in that case send feedback via interaction.followUp({ ..., flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) instead of editReply. Also stop discarding `flags` on the editReply branch when the intent is an ephemeral follow-up. At minimum, callers that did deferUpdate() should use followUp for ephemeral side-messages rather than replyOrEdit.

title: Review modal/button error handlers overwrite the review card with a public plaintext error after deferUpdate()
detail: handleRejectModal (and handleAcceptModal:87-112, handlePermRejectModal:126-151, handleKickModal:165-190, handleVoteOutModal:203-228) all call interaction.deferUpdate() first, then on any thrown error call replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: 'Failed to process ... (trace: X).' }) with no flags. Via the cmdWrap.ts bug above, deferred=true routes this to editReply(), which edits the ORIGINAL review card message — replacing the applicant embed and action buttons with a bare public error string. The same defect exists in handleReviewButton's catch (buttons.ts:200-204) for the already-deferred actions (claim/wrong_password/stale_modmail) and in handleModmailButton's catch (buttons.ts:270-275). Net effect: a transient failure (DB hiccup, Discord 50013, etc.) during a moderation action not only fails the action but visibly destroys the review card for all staff, with the internal trace string leaked publicly into the staff channel.
fix: In these post-deferUpdate catch blocks, send the failure via interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) (the message component interaction still supports followUp after deferUpdate) instead of replyOrEdit/editReply, so the card is preserved and the error stays private to the acting mod.

title: resolveApplication failure replies wipe the review card when called after deferUpdate()
detail: resolveApplication() emits its not-found / guild-mismatch feedback with replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: ... }) and no ephemeral flag. It is invoked from the modal handlers (modals.ts) and from the claim/wrong_password/stale_modmail button paths (buttons.ts) AFTER deferUpdate() has run. Because deferred=true, replyOrEdit -> editReply edits the source review card, replacing it with 'No application with code XXXXXX.' publicly and stripping its buttons. This turns a benign 'card references a since-deleted app' situation into destruction of the live card. (When invoked from the modal-opening button paths before any defer it is fine — there it correctly uses reply.)
fix: Have resolveApplication detect an already-acknowledged component interaction and use followUp({ flags: Ephemeral }) for its failure messages, or pass a flag from callers indicating whether the interaction was deferUpdate'd so it can choose followUp vs reply.

title: Router error-card fallback uses ensureDeferred (ephemeral deferReply) + editReply, clobbering the source message for component interactions
detail: The catch-all safety net calls ensureDeferred(interaction) then postErrorCard(...). ensureDeferred (cmdWrap.ts:437-474) only ever does deferReply({Ephemeral}); it never handles component interactions via deferUpdate. For a button/select that threw BEFORE acknowledging itself, ensureDeferred issues a deferReply (valid), so postErrorCard's editReply targets the ephemeral reply — OK. But for a button handler that already called deferUpdate() and then threw (e.g. redeemreward confirm in features/artistRotation/handlers.ts:120 onward, byteToken confirm), ensureDeferred sees deferred=true and returns, then postErrorCard -> replyOrEdit -> editReply edits the ORIGINAL component message, overwriting the confirmation/panel embed with the public error card. Note buttons are routed directly (not through wrapCommand), so their post-defer throws land here. The 'public so staff can see' comment in errorCard.ts:224-227 is also wrong on the common path where the prior defer was ephemeral.
fix: Make the router fallback component-aware: if interaction.isMessageComponent() and not yet acknowledged, deferUpdate() (or just followUp) rather than deferReply; and deliver the error card via followUp({ flags: Ephemeral }) when the interaction was acknowledged with deferUpdate, instead of editReply over the source message.

title: Unrecognized modal customId prefixes are silently dropped with no ack and no error card
detail: The isModalSubmit() block handles a fixed set of prefixes (tk:closemod:, help:modal:search, v1:modal:/v1:avatar:confirm18:, v1:gate:reset:, isitreal_modal_). A route-miss error card is posted ONLY inside the v1:modal:/v1:avatar: branch (lines 981-1000). A modal whose customId matches none of these prefixes falls through to the end of the function and returns without ever acknowledging the interaction — no reply, no deferUpdate, no error card, not even a route-miss log. The user sees Discord's generic 'Something went wrong' and there is no trace ID. This is exactly the failure mode that occurs after renaming a modal customId or shipping a new modal without registering its route — the symptom is invisible in logs. Contrast with the slash path (line 234-251) and the inner modal route-miss, both of which respond/log.
fix: Add a final else at the end of the isModalSubmit() block that logs evt:'ix_route_miss' and posts the same postErrorCard route-miss as the inner v1:modal: branch, so any unhandled modal yields an acknowledgement and a reportable trace ID.

title: armWatchdog only auto-defers modals; slow button/select/context-menu handlers can hit 10062 with no safety net, contradicting the router's own comment
detail: armWatchdog's timer returns immediately unless the interaction isModalSubmit() (lines 156-159), so it only rescues modals near the 3s deadline. Buttons, string-select menus, and context-menu commands get no auto-defer. Meanwhile interactionCreate.ts:217-218 documents the watchdog as a generic 'bark if we don't respond within Discord's 3-second SLA ... doesn't actually cancel anything - just yells', which is doubly wrong: it does take action (deferReply) and only for modals. Any component/context-menu handler that performs >3s of work before its own deferUpdate/deferReply (e.g. handleModmailContextMenu does guild/channel work before deferReply at modmail/handlers.ts:190; redeemreward/byteToken confirm do role fetches) will 10062 unrescued. Low severity because most handlers defer early, but the protection is asymmetric and mis-documented.
fix: Either extend armWatchdog to also auto-deferUpdate component interactions (and deferReply context-menu commands) near the deadline, or correct the comment in interactionCreate.ts to state the watchdog only covers modals so future handlers know they must defer themselves.

title: Wide-event Response State is inaccurate for handlers that defer/reply directly instead of via cmdWrap helpers
detail: markDeferred() is only emitted inside ensureDeferred() and markReplied() only inside replyOrEdit(). The large majority of component/modal handlers call interaction.deferUpdate()/deferReply()/update()/reply()/editReply() DIRECTLY (e.g. byteTokenHandler, artistRotation/handlers, modmail/handlers, qotd/handlers, tickets/handlers, dmVerification). For those flows the wide event's responseState.deferredAt/repliedAt stay null, so the error card's 'Response State' section (errorCardV2.ts:288-325) reports 'Deferred: No (direct reply or error before defer)' and 'Replied: No' even though the user definitely received a response. This degrades the exact debugging signal the wide-event system was built to provide ('did the user see anything?').
fix: Either funnel direct defer/reply calls through the cmdWrap helpers, or add lightweight enrichEvent(e=>e.markDeferred()/markReplied()) calls in the shared handler entry points, so response-state telemetry reflects reality.

title: Entire /analytics command module is dead (never registered or imported)
detail: command.ts exports executeAnalyticsCommand, executeAnalyticsExportCommand, and parseWindow — full slash-command handlers for an /analytics command. But "analytics" is NOT in src/commands/runtimeManifest.ts SLASH_COMMAND_NAMES, is not registered in src/index.ts, and the module is imported by nothing in src/ (only tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts references it). The functionality was reimplemented under src/commands/stats/ (the consolidated /stats command). A startup drift guard in index.ts (lines 274-294) enforces that registered handlers match the manifest, so this module can never be reached at runtime. ~481 lines of dead handler code plus a test suite that only exercises dead code.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/command.ts and tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts. Confirm /stats fully covers the prior /analytics summary + export behavior before removal.

title: analytics/queries.ts is transitively dead (only consumer is the dead command.ts)
detail: queries.ts exports getActionCountsByMod, getTopReasons, getVolumeSeries, getLeadTimeStats, getOpenQueueAge. Across src/ the only importer is src/features/analytics/command.ts (itself dead) plus tests/features/analytics/queries.test.ts. The single non-test mention elsewhere (src/db/ensure.ts:267) is a comment, not an import. The live /stats command uses src/features/analytics/approvalRate.ts and src/commands/stats/* queries, not this file. ~528 lines dead.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/queries.ts and its test once command.ts is removed. Verify none of stats/* re-imports these names (they do not).

title: /approval-rate standalone handler is fully orphaned
detail: approvalRateCommand.ts exports executeApprovalRateCommand. Grep across the whole repo shows zero importers — not src/, not even a test. The live approval-rate feature is the /stats approval-rate subcommand (src/commands/stats/approvalRate.ts -> src/commands/stats/index.ts case 'approval-rate'), which imports the shared query module features/analytics/approvalRate.ts directly. This standalone command handler was superseded and left behind. ~196 lines dead.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/approvalRateCommand.ts. The shared query module src/features/analytics/approvalRate.ts must be kept (it is used by stats/approvalRate.ts).

title: streamReviewActionsCSV export is dead (only consumer is dead command.ts)
detail: csv.ts exports two functions: generateModHistoryCsv (used by the live src/commands/stats/history.ts) and streamReviewActionsCSV. streamReviewActionsCSV is imported only by the dead src/features/analytics/command.ts (line 37) and tests/lib/csv.test.ts. Once command.ts is removed, streamReviewActionsCSV becomes a dead export inside an otherwise-live file. Side note: the inline comment at csv.ts:43-49 claims RFC4180 quoting 'prevents CSV injection attacks where =,+,-,@ could trigger formula execution' — that is false (Excel still evaluates =cmd inside a quoted field); but since this exporter is dead the claim has no runtime impact.
fix: Remove streamReviewActionsCSV (and CSVExportOptions if it becomes unused) from src/lib/csv.ts when deleting command.ts, keeping generateModHistoryCsv. Separately, do not propagate the misleading CSV-injection comment into the live generateModHistoryCsv.

title: avatar_confirm18 modal route is dead infrastructure and has no handler (latent route-miss bug)
detail: modalPatterns.ts defines MODAL_18_RE (/^v1:avatar:confirm18:code([0-9A-F]{6})$/), the ModalRoute union member { type: 'avatar_confirm18' }, and identifyModalRoute returns it (lines 149-152). However: (1) No code anywhere in src/web/scripts ever creates/shows a modal with customId 'v1:avatar:confirm18:' — grep finds the string only in modalPatterns.ts and interactionCreate.ts, never in a ModalBuilder/showModal call, so the route is unreachable in practice. (2) Even if such a modal were shown, the router in src/events/interactionCreate.ts handles gate_submit_page, review_reject/perm_reject/accept/kick/vote_out/unclaim, report_resolve, qotd_suggest, qotd_reject — but has NO branch for route.type === 'avatar_confirm18'. It would fall through to the catch-all at interactionCreate.ts:984-1000 and post an 'Unhandled modal' error card. So the union member is both dead and a latent bug.
fix: Either remove MODAL_18_RE, the 'avatar_confirm18' union member, its identifyModalRoute branch, and the '|| customId.startsWith("v1:avatar:confirm18:")' clause in interactionCreate.ts:769; or, if the 18+ avatar-source confirmation is intended to exist, wire the showModal producer AND add a matching route.type === 'avatar_confirm18' handler in the router.

title: Dead prefix clause for v1:avatar:confirm18 modals in the router guard
detail: The modal dispatch guard `if (customId.startsWith("v1:modal:") || customId.startsWith("v1:avatar:confirm18:"))` includes the second clause solely for the avatar_confirm18 route. Since no modal with that customId is ever shown (see modalPatterns.ts finding) and there is no handler branch inside the block for it, the clause only serves to route such an ID into the block where it immediately hits the catch-all 'Unhandled modal' error card. The clause is effectively dead and misleading.
fix: Drop the `|| customId.startsWith("v1:avatar:confirm18:")` clause (coordinated with removing MODAL_18_RE), or implement the avatar_confirm18 handler if the feature is meant to ship.

title: fireAndForget helper is never used anywhere
detail: fireAndForget(promise, label) was added to 'replace the .catch(() => {}) anti-pattern throughout the codebase' (per its own JSDoc), but a repo-wide search of src/, scripts/, web/, workers/, and tests/ finds zero importers or call sites — only the definition itself. The codebase still uses inline .catch(() => undefined)/.catch(err => logger.warn(...)) (e.g. throughout interactionCreate.ts and movie.ts), so the intended adoption never happened. Dead utility module.
fix: Either delete src/lib/fireAndForget.ts, or actually adopt it by replacing the scattered fire-and-forget .catch patterns with fireAndForget(...). Prefer deletion unless adoption is planned.

title: commandSync.ts is an empty module husk with no exports
detail: After syncGuildCommandsInProcess() and its helpers were removed (v4.4.5, per the file's own comment), the file was 'retained for potential future command sync utilities' but now contains only comments — no code, no exports. Nothing imports it (repo-wide search finds only the file itself). It is a zero-value placeholder that shows up as a source module and in import-graph tooling.
fix: Delete src/lib/commandSync.ts. Re-create it later if/when real command-sync helpers are actually needed; an empty placeholder file adds noise without value.

title: BTN_AUDIT_MEMBERS_RE and BTN_AUDIT_NSFW_RE exports are used only by tests
detail: The audit button router (src/events/interactionCreate.ts:434) matches the combined BTN_AUDIT_RE only. The granular BTN_AUDIT_MEMBERS_RE and BTN_AUDIT_NSFW_RE exports are not referenced anywhere in src/ — only tests/lib/modalPatterns.test.ts imports them. They are effectively unused production exports (the audit handler must parse the specific subtype another way). Low impact but they are exported solely to satisfy tests of themselves.
fix: Confirm src/commands/audit/buttonRouter.ts does its own sub-parse (it does not use these), then either delete the two granular patterns or actually use them in the audit button handler instead of re-deriving subtype. If kept only for documentation, downgrade to non-exported or add a real consumer.

title: Some auditFindingsStore exports (getFindingsByRun, getFindingsBySeverity, listAuditRuns) appear unused outside the module/tests
detail: The module is NOT fully dead: insertFinding, generateReportData, and generateMarkdownReport are used by scripts/record-audit-findings.ts. However getFindingsByRun and getFindingsBySeverity are only called internally by generateReportData (and listAuditRuns is not called by any production consumer found — the web audit-findings dashboard routes use their own queries). These exported-but-externally-unused functions are minor dead exports. Note the prepared statements at module load assume the audit_findings table (migration 043) exists; that is fine while a real importer exists, but worth tracking if the module's only importer is a dev-only script.
fix: Make getFindingsByRun/getFindingsBySeverity module-private (drop export) since only generateReportData uses them, and remove listAuditRuns if no consumer is found; verify the web dashboard audit-findings pages do not import this store before pruning.

title: Pulse insights engine runs 18 detectors with ~50 synchronous SQLite queries per request, several non-sargable
detail: getInsights() loops over 18 detector functions sequentially (line 1483). Each detector fires 1-6 synchronous better-sqlite3 queries: e.g. detectMessageAnomaly runs 1 + 4-in-a-loop COUNT(*) over message_activity (lines 827-846), detectCommunicatorRatioDecline runs 2 queries x4 windows = 8 queries (lines 910-926), detectVoiceTrend runs 4, detectAppBacklog/ModWorkloadImbalance/RejectionRateShift each scan review_action via 'app_id IN (SELECT id FROM application WHERE guild_id=?)' semi-joins. Conservatively this is ~40-55 blocking queries on a single SSR request, all on the synchronous DB handle, several aggregating over the million-row message_activity / action_log / review_action tables. Because better-sqlite3 is synchronous (web/src/lib/server/db.ts), the entire Node event loop is blocked for the full duration on every cold cache load, stalling all other concurrent dashboard requests. The page-level cache (CACHE_TTL.medium=60s, pulse/+page.server.ts:37) only masks this between refreshes and per time-window; every distinct window and every 60s expiry pays the full cost.
fix: Collapse the per-window repeated COUNT(*) loops (detectMessageAnomaly, detectCommunicatorRatioDecline, detectVoiceTrend) into single GROUP BY queries that return all buckets at once. Share one pass over message_activity / user_activity / review_action across detectors instead of re-querying per detector (pass a small pre-aggregated context into the detectors). Consider precomputing insights in the existing cron rollup (like observatory does) and reading a rollup table at request time.

title: detectNsfwFlagSurge and detectModmailResponseTime use strftime() on TEXT timestamp columns, forcing full scans
detail: detectNsfwFlagSurge filters nsfw_flags with strftime('%s', flagged_at) >= ? (lines 1216,1222). nsfw_flags.flagged_at is TEXT (migration 032_nsfw_flags.ts:45) and the only indexes are (guild_id) and (guild_id, reviewed) (migration 032:53-54). Wrapping the column in strftime() makes the predicate non-sargable, so SQLite cannot use any time index and scans every flag row for the guild twice (this-window + prev-window). detectModmailResponseTime has the same problem: it computes strftime('%s', mt.created_at) in both the WHERE and via correlated MIN per ticket (lines 1176-1180), defeating any index on modmail_ticket. On servers with large flag/modmail history this is a repeated full/partial scan on the SSR path.
fix: Store/compare timestamps as INTEGER unix seconds (as action_log/message_activity already do) or add a generated/stored *_s column with an index, then filter with plain range comparisons (flagged_at_s >= ? AND flagged_at_s < ?). At minimum add an index on the raw text column and compare against ISO string literals (datetime(?, 'unixepoch')) so the index can be used instead of strftime per row.

title: Review queue layout runs uncached query with ~3 correlated modmail subqueries per application row on every navigation
detail: getReviewQueue() is invoked from dashboard/reviews/+layout.server.ts:14 with NO caching, so it executes on every page load and every client-side navigation into any /dashboard/reviews/* route (the layout re-runs). The query attaches, per pending application row, two correlated scalar subqueries in the SELECT (has_unread_modmail EXISTS at 404-411, modmail_awaiting_since at 412-419) plus a third correlated EXISTS in the ORDER BY (432-439). Each of those contains a further nested 'SELECT MAX(mm2.id) ... WHERE ticket_id = mt.id' subquery. So the work is roughly 3 x (pending app count) correlated subqueries, each doing a nested aggregate. idx_modmail_message_ticket_id(ticket_id, id DESC) (migration 063) helps the MAX lookups but the per-row fan-out and the ORDER BY recomputation remain. Synchronous handle => blocks event loop per load.
fix: Precompute the 'latest message direction + timestamp per open ticket' once via a single GROUP BY / window-function CTE joined to applications, instead of three correlated subqueries per row (the ORDER BY repeats the same EXISTS a fourth time). Cache the queue with the existing cached() helper (short TTL) since the same payload is recomputed on every reviews navigation.

title: Modmail thread list runs 2 correlated subqueries per row and is recomputed on every modmail navigation (uncached)
detail: getModmailThreads() (called uncached from dashboard/modmail/+layout.server.ts:13 on every navigation) selects, per ticket row, two correlated subqueries that each re-scan modmail_message for the same ticket ordered by created_at DESC LIMIT 1 (latest_message at 55-56, latest_direction at 57-58) in addition to the LEFT JOIN+GROUP BY used for message_count. That is two redundant ordered lookups per ticket on top of the aggregate; both pull the same 'latest row'. Bounded by LIMIT 50 so impact is modest, but it is pure repeated work executed on every layout load.
fix: Fetch the latest message once per ticket via a window function (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ticket_id ORDER BY created_at DESC)) joined to the ticket aggregate, returning content+direction in a single pass. Optionally wrap in cached() with a short TTL.

title: Heatmap builder issues one query per week (up to 26) and pulls every raw message row into JS instead of aggregating
detail: getHeatmapDataForRange() loops weeksCount (capped MAX_WEEKS=26) and calls buildWeek() each iteration (lines 180-183). buildWeek() runs 'SELECT created_at_s FROM message_activity WHERE guild_id=? AND created_at_s>=? AND created_at_s<?' (122-127) returning EVERY raw message row for that week, then buckets them in a JS loop (144-150). So a 26-week window = 26 separate queries, each potentially returning tens of thousands of rows, all materialized and iterated in Node on the SSR path. message_activity already has hour_bucket plus idx_message_activity_guild_hour, so the entire grid could be one GROUP BY. Mitigated by the 60s page cache (heatmap/+page.server.ts:20) but every cold load / new window pays it.
fix: Replace the per-week raw-row fetch with a single query over the whole range that GROUPs BY hour_bucket (or by day-of-week/hour), e.g. SELECT (created_at_s/3600)%24 ... COUNT(*) GROUP BY ..., then distribute counts into the week grids in JS. This turns 26 row-streaming queries into one aggregate query and removes the per-row JS bucketing.

title: getModmailThreads interpolates statusFilter directly into SQL; route casts unvalidated query param into the type
detail: statusClause is built by string interpolation: `AND t.status = '${statusFilter}'` (line 42). The function parameter is typed 'open'|'closed'|'all', but dashboard/modmail/+layout.server.ts:12 produces it via `(url.searchParams.get('filter') ?? 'all') as 'open'|'closed'|'all'` — a TypeScript cast with no runtime validation. A crafted ?filter= value flows unescaped into the SQL string. The web DB handle is opened with query_only=ON (web/src/lib/server/db.ts:18), which blocks writes, so this is not an injection-to-mutation, but it still permits read-side SQL tampering / errors and is a latent injection if query_only is ever relaxed or the helper is reused elsewhere. Off the strict performance axis but a real cross-file trust gap (route trusts the cast; query trusts the route).
fix: Validate the param against an allowlist before use (e.g. ['open','closed','all'].includes(raw) ? raw : 'all') and/or bind status as a parameter instead of interpolating: build the clause as `AND t.status = ?` and push the value into the params array.

title: Failed remote DB migration is swallowed, then PM2 restarts new code against an un-migrated database
detail: Step 6.5 runs the migration as: ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js" || echo "Migration step completed (may have warnings)". Because the failure branch is `echo` (which always exits 0), a non-zero exit from the migration is discarded even under `set -euo pipefail`. Control then proceeds to Step 7 (lines 449-455) which unconditionally runs `pm2 startOrRestart ecosystem.config.cjs`, bringing up the new bot + web code against a database whose schema was NOT migrated (or was left half-migrated). docs/reference/database-schema-safety.md:13 explicitly promises the opposite: 'If a migration fails, the rest of the deploy bails.' This is the single highest-impact ops defect: a migration error produces a green-looking deploy and a running bot that will throw at runtime on missing columns/tables (see src/config/flaggerStore.ts:211 which already handles 'column missing - migration may not have run'). The pre-deploy backup (maybe_backup_remote_db) does not help because the code is still rolled forward on top of the old schema.
fix: Do not swallow the migration exit code. Either remove the `|| echo ...` so `set -e` aborts, or capture status explicitly and abort before the PM2 restart, e.g.: `if ! ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js"; then echo 'ERROR: migration failed, aborting deploy (code NOT restarted)'; exit 1; fi`. Keep the lock trap so the lock is released on abort.

title: Migration runner reports success when the child is killed by a signal (result.status null)
detail: spawnSync returns { status, signal }. When the child tsx process is terminated by a signal (e.g. OOM-killer during a large migration, or SIGTERM from pm2/kill_timeout), `result.status` is null and `result.signal` is set. `process.exit(result.status || 0)` then exits 0, reporting success for a migration that never completed. Even when status is a real non-zero, the upstream caller in deploy.sh:435 throws the code away via `|| echo`, but this line independently masks signal kills for ANY caller (deploy-no-tests.sh:25, docs/development-guide.md:175 step 7, manual runs). Combined with the swallowed-exit bug it means a killed migration looks fully successful end to end.
fix: Propagate failure faithfully: `if (result.error) { console.error(result.error); process.exit(1); } process.exit(result.signal ? 1 : (result.status ?? 1));`. Use `?? 1` (not `|| 0`) so a null status fails closed.

title: Wrong/missing DB_PATH silently creates an empty DB, 'backs it up', and migrates the empty file
detail: The DB is opened with `new Database(dbPath, { fileMustExist: false })` (line 50) — the in-file comment at 48-49 even warns 'we'll happily create a fresh DB if the path is wrong. You'll only notice when all your data is mysteriously gone.' createBackup() (line 142) then does `copyFileSync(dbPath, backupPath)` AFTER the connection already created the file, so the backup is of the freshly-created empty DB, not the real data. All pending migrations then 'succeed' against the empty DB and get stamped into schema_migrations. On the server this is reachable: if DB_PATH in the remote .env is wrong, or the deploy extracts into a path where ./data/data.db doesn't yet exist (relative cwd mismatch), the bot boots against an empty database with a clean migration log and no recoverable pre-state. There is no assertion that the DB existed and was non-empty before migrating.
fix: Open with `fileMustExist: true` for the migrate path (or stat the file before opening and abort if it is missing/zero-bytes when not explicitly bootstrapping). Take the backup via the filesystem BEFORE opening the connection, and skip/abort backup if the source does not exist instead of copying a just-created empty file. Gate fresh-DB creation behind an explicit `--init`/`--bootstrap` flag.

title: Parallel '--no-tests' deploy path lacks lock/backup/health-check and duplicates the swallowed-migration bug
detail: deploy-no-tests.sh is a second, fully independent deploy script targeting the same prod host/path/PM2 process as deploy.sh. It (a) repeats the exact swallowed-migration defect at line 25 (`node scripts/migrate-remote.js || echo "Migration step completed (may have warnings)"`), (b) has no deploy lock, so it can race a concurrent deploy.sh run (deploy.sh's mkdir lock at line 83 does not protect against this script, which never acquires it), (c) takes no pre-deploy DB backup, and (d) has only a best-effort `pm2 show | grep` status check with no Discord-ready verification. Two scripts mutating the same server with different safety guarantees is a cross-file hazard: an operator using this 'fast' path silently loses every protection that was added to deploy.sh in the 2026-05-02 hardening pass.
fix: Delete deploy-no-tests.sh and fold its behavior into `deploy.sh --fast` (which already exists, lines 159-162), so there is exactly one hardened deploy path with the lock, backup, and migration-abort logic.

title: Third legacy deploy script skips migrations entirely and uses set -e without pipefail/-u
detail: scripts/deploy.sh (distinct from the root deploy.sh) is yet another deploy path to the same prod host. It uses only `set -e` (line 12) — no `-u` (undefined vars silently empty) and no `pipefail` (a failing command upstream of a pipe is masked). More importantly it has NO migration step at all: it extracts the tarball, runs `npm ci --omit=dev`, and `pm2 restart` (lines 122-133), so deploying through this script ships new code that expects a new schema without ever running migrations. Its tarball (line 108) also omits .env.build, web/build, and ecosystem.config.cjs that the root deploy.sh ships, so the build-info/runtime env and web app drift. Having three divergent deploy scripts (root deploy.sh, deploy-no-tests.sh, scripts/deploy.sh) all pointed at PM2 process 'pawtropolis' is a maintenance trap where the safe behavior depends entirely on which file the operator happens to run.
fix: Remove or clearly archive scripts/deploy.sh; converge on the root deploy.sh. If kept, add `set -euo pipefail` and the migration step, and make the tarball contents identical to the canonical deploy.

title: Standalone migration 046 records into a different bookkeeping table than the migration framework
detail: The canonical migration tracker is schema_migrations (scripts/migrate.ts:71-78 and migrations/lib/helpers.ts:149-213 via recordMigration). migrations/046_extend_user_cache_profile.ts:32 correctly calls recordMigration(db, '046', ...) which writes to schema_migrations. But the hand-run helper scripts/run-migration-046.mjs:24-27 writes to a separate `migration_log` table instead. Its filename invites manual use during incident response; if an operator runs it, the ALTERs are applied but schema_migrations is NOT updated, so the next deploy's migrate.ts sees 046 as pending and re-runs migrations/046_*.ts. The 046 migration guards each ALTER with columnExists, so the re-run is non-destructive today, but the divergence is a latent footgun: any future standalone fix script following this pattern for a non-idempotent migration would double-apply.
fix: Make run-migration-046.mjs either call into the same recordMigration logic (write to schema_migrations) or, better, delete it in favor of `npm run migrate`. At minimum, stamp schema_migrations, not migration_log, so the two paths agree.

title: Per-migration transaction does not roll back side effects that do not throw, and version is stamped even for no-op-but-wrong migrations
detail: applyMigration wraps migrateFn in db.transaction (lines 209-213), but as the in-file GOTCHA at 206-208 notes, the transaction only rolls back on a thrown exception. A migration that performs a partial/incorrect change without throwing still commits, and because each migration calls recordMigration itself (inside the same transaction), the version is permanently marked applied. Since the deploy harness above (deploy.sh:435) also swallows failures, a migration that logs an error but exits the function normally will be recorded as applied and never retried. Combined, there is no end-to-end guarantee that 'recorded as applied' means 'schema is correct'.
fix: Have the runner (not each migration) own the stamping: only call recordMigration after migrateFn returns AND after a post-condition check where feasible. Surface any migration-internal error by throwing rather than logging-and-returning. Pair with fixing the deploy.sh swallow so a throw actually aborts.

title: Full deploy ships and extracts src/ and scripts/ over the live tree, widening blast radius
detail: The full-deploy tarball includes `dist src migrations scripts assets ...` (line 408) and is extracted in place on the remote (line 416, `tar -xzf`). The bot actually runs from dist/ (ecosystem.config.cjs:5). Shipping src/ and overwriting scripts/ on every deploy means a partially-built or stale src tree, or a tarball created mid-edit, can replace the server's scripts/ (including migrate-remote.js and migrate.ts themselves) right before step 6.5 runs them. tar extraction is not atomic, so an interrupted upload/extract can leave a mixed old/new scripts tree that the very next migration step executes.
fix: Ship only what the runtime needs (dist, migrations, scripts required for migrate, package manifests, .env.build, ecosystem config, web/build). Drop src/ from the production tarball. Consider extracting into a fresh release dir and atomically symlinking, rather than extracting over the live tree.

title: Destructive cleanup deletes all home-dir tarballs with a weak y/N gate and no set -euo pipefail
detail: CLEANUP-ALL.sh has no `set -euo pipefail`. After a single `read -p "Continue? (y/N)"` prompt (line 84), it runs `rm -fv /home/ubuntu/*.tar.gz` and `rm -fv /home/ubuntu/pawtropolis-tech/*.tar.gz` (lines 98-99). The summary text claims it 'Preserves /home/ubuntu/archives/' but the glob is unconstrained for the top-level home dir, so any intentional archive placed directly in /home/ubuntu (e.g. a deploy-archive.tar.gz like the 2.3MB one in the repo root) would be deleted. The DB-backup pruning (lines 104-119) is keyed on filename pattern data.db.backup* and is fine, but the tarball deletion is broader than the messaging implies.
fix: Add `set -euo pipefail`. Scope tar.gz deletion to a known throwaway prefix (e.g. deploy.tar.gz / deploy-*.tar.gz) instead of `*.tar.gz`, and/or move intentional archives to the explicitly-preserved /home/ubuntu/archives/ before globbing. Echo the exact file list and require typing the count to confirm.

title: DB sync pulls remote WAL/SHM over a freshly-replaced main DB without re-checkpoint, risking divergent WAL application
detail: In sync_db_remote_preferred the main DB is checkpointed PASSIVE on the remote (line 313, best-effort, may time out while the bot runs), copied to a temp file and integrity-checked, then moved into place (line 339). Afterwards the remote -wal and -shm files are copied on top of the just-replaced local main DB (lines 343-350). If the passive checkpoint did not fully fold the WAL (explicitly possible per the line 313 message 'WAL checkpoint timed out (bot may be running)'), the local now has a main file from one instant and a WAL from a later instant; SQLite will replay that WAL against the main on next open, which is only safe if they are a matched set. Because the copy is non-atomic and spans a running writer, the pulled set can be inconsistent even though the standalone integrity_check on the main file passed. Backup rotation also runs through best-effort `|| true` pipes (line 289) so a failed rotation is invisible.
fix: Either copy main+wal+shm as one consistent set taken after a TRUNCATE checkpoint with the writer stopped, or pull only the checkpointed main DB and do NOT copy the remote WAL/SHM. Verify integrity after WAL files are in place, not just on the bare main file.

title: redeemreward confirm button has no reentrancy guard: double-click duplicates art jobs and double-rotates the artist queue
detail: handleConfirm() runs the assignment side effects with NO idempotency/lock and only clears the buttons at the very end (interaction.editReply({components:[]}) at lines 282-285). The flow is: deferUpdate -> (await) remove ticket role -> (await) grant artist access / post `$add` -> processAssignment() -> createJob() -> logAssignment() -> editReply(clear buttons). Because the confirmation is a NON-ephemeral reply (src/commands/redeemreward.ts:294-297, no MessageFlags.Ephemeral) and handleConfirm never verifies the clicker is the invoker, the live button can be clicked twice in quick succession (or by two different staff) before the first invocation reaches the final editReply. Each click is a distinct Discord interaction with a distinct interaction.id, so the interactionCreate dedup map (src/events/interactionCreate.ts:69-97, which only de-dupes identical IDs from Discord network re-delivery) does NOT prevent it. The downstream operations are NOT idempotent: processAssignment (src/features/artistRotation/queue.ts:374-427) unconditionally rotates the artist to the end of the queue and increments assignments_count by 1 each call; createJob (src/features/artJobs/store.ts:114-161) always INSERTs a new art_job row with the next sequential job number. The random `confirmId` embedded in the customId is parsed but never recorded or consumed anywhere, so it provides no protection. Result of a double-fire: the artist is rotated twice (losing their fair queue position), assignments_count is over-counted, two art_job rows are created for one commission, two assignment_log rows, and for legacy Ticket Tool channels two `$add` commands are posted. This is a cross-file trust gap: the handler trusts that the queue/job stores enforce single-execution, but they only guarantee per-call atomicity, not idempotency. Note the codebase already solves this exact problem elsewhere (modmail threadOpen.ts uses a 'pending' PRIMARY-KEY lock row; byteTokenHandler.ts has explicit 'Step 3.5 race condition' cleanup and an initiator check), confirming this is an oversight rather than intentional.
fix: Guard the confirmation against re-entry before doing any work. Cheapest robust option: in handleConfirm, immediately after deferUpdate(), do an atomic 'consume' of the confirmation -- e.g. INSERT the confirmId into a small consumed_confirmations table (or art_job/assignment_log keyed by a UNIQUE confirmId) inside a transaction and bail if it already exists (ALREADY_PROCESSED), mirroring the review claimTx pattern. Alternatively, edit the message to remove the buttons (interaction.update / editReply with components:[]) as the FIRST action so a second click can't hit the live component, and add an initiator check like byteTokenHandler (reject if interaction.user.id !== the original invoker). Also make processAssignment + createJob run under a single guard so they cannot both execute twice.

title: ensureReviewMessage check-then-create race posts duplicate review cards (and double Gatekeeper ping) under concurrent calls
category: Concurrency / check-then-act on shared external state
detail: ensureReviewMessage reads the existing review_card mapping once near the top (lines 799-801) and then decides create-vs-edit based on that snapshot. The decision and the create are separated by many awaits (embed render via inSpan at 837-851, several dynamic imports). On the no-mapping path it does `await channel.send(...)` to post a brand-new card (lines 919-929, including a one-time Gatekeeper/bot-dev role ping) and only writes the review_card row at the very end (upsert at line 958, after the send). If two callers invoke ensureReviewMessage for the same appId while no card exists yet, both read mapping===undefined, both fall into the create branch, both channel.send a card, and the second upsert (review_card.app_id is PRIMARY KEY, db.ts:127-135) either throws a PRIMARY KEY constraint or overwrites -- but two physical Discord messages have already been posted with duplicate role pings, and only one survives in the mapping table (the orphan keeps live buttons). This concurrent no-mapping window is real and acknowledged in-tree: src/features/gate/scan.ts:66-102 added waitForReviewCardMapping() specifically because the avatar-scan job (fired via setImmediate on submit) calls ensureReviewMessage concurrently with the submit handler's own ensureReviewMessage. That poller is only a mitigation with a 5s timeout, and scan.ts:210-217 explicitly calls ensureReviewMessage even when the wait times out (cardReady===false), so a slow initial card-create re-opens the double-post window. ensureReviewMessage has no internal mutex; the comment at scan.ts:71-73 admits 'Polling is simpler than adding cross-module eventing.'
fix: Make card creation atomic against the PRIMARY KEY instead of relying on a pre-read snapshot. Move the channel.send into a flow like modmail threadOpen: first INSERT a placeholder review_card row (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) to claim ownership; only the caller whose INSERT changed a row proceeds to channel.send and then UPDATEs with the real message_id; losers re-read the mapping and edit instead. Alternatively serialize ensureReviewMessage per-appId with an in-process promise chain keyed by appId (as inviteTracker.ts does with trackingQueue). At minimum, re-query the mapping immediately before the create branch (after all awaits) and switch to edit if a row now exists.

title: Periodic schedulers have no overlap guard; staleApplicationCheck can emit duplicate alerts because markAlertSent runs after the awaited send
detail: Every scheduler in src/scheduler/* uses the pattern setInterval(async () => { await longJob() }) with no re-entrancy flag (grep for _running/isRunning/_busy across src/scheduler returns zero matches). setInterval does not wait for an async callback, so if a run outlasts its interval the next tick starts while the previous is still in flight. For most schedulers the work is idempotent UPSERTs (guildSnapshotScheduler.ts upsertSnapshot ON CONFLICT, modMetricsScheduler recalc), so overlap only wastes work. staleApplicationCheck is the one with user-visible impact: checkStaleApplications() reads stale apps via getStaleApplications() (which filters on stale_alert_sent), then for each guild does `await (channel).send(alert)` and only THEN calls markAlertSent() (sendAlertForGuild lines 252-263 and 277-279). The 'already alerted' flag is therefore not persisted until after the awaited Discord send. Two overlapping runs (or the 15s-delayed initial run overlapping the first interval tick) both read the same not-yet-marked apps and both send the alert, pinging the Gatekeeper role twice for the same applications. guildSnapshotScheduler additionally mutates shared module state _snapshotCount across overlapping runs (lines 17, 94-95), perturbing the every-6th online-fetch cadence.
fix: Add a per-scheduler in-flight guard: a module-level boolean set true at the start of the async body and cleared in finally; if already true, log-and-skip the tick. For staleApplicationCheck specifically, also mark the apps as alerted BEFORE (or atomically with) the send, or move the markAlertSent into the same synchronous step that selects them, so a concurrent/overlapping run cannot re-select unmarked rows after the send has been initiated.

title: Periodic Patreon role-dedup sweep interval is never unref'd and has no stop function (only un-cleanable long-lived interval in the bot)
detail: sweepPatreonRoleStacks() creates a periodic 10-minute setInterval (line 178) but, unlike every other recurring timer in the bot process, it (a) does NOT call .unref() and (b) does not store the handle anywhere, so there is no way to clearInterval it. Cross-file impact: the entire shutdown contract in src/startup/ready.ts -> gracefulShutdown and src/startup/schedulers.ts -> stopSchedulers() assumes every recurring job is either unref'd or has a stopX() that is called during SIGTERM/SIGINT. Every scheduler (byteMultiplier, securityAudit, staleApplication, modMetrics, guildSnapshot, opsHealth, diskSpace, eventTimeout, badgeRefresh) and every feature timer (movieNight/gameNight persistence, dmVerification cleanup, modmail forwardedMessages cleanup, interactionCreate dedup, traceStore prune, notifyLimiter) follows that pattern. This one does not: there is no stopPatreonRoleDedup() anywhere in the source (verified by grep), and ready.ts never tears it down. Concrete impact is limited because the sweep callback is async and idle-cheap and gracefulShutdown ultimately calls process.exit(0), which terminates regardless. But the un-unref'd ref-counted timer means this module alone can keep Node's event loop alive (delaying a clean, signal-less exit), and it is uncancellable in tests/embeds (no opt-out, no handle), forcing test harnesses to either rely on process.exit or hang. It is the single defensible deviation from an otherwise airtight resource-cleanup convention.
fix: Match the established pattern: store the handle in a module-level let (e.g. let sweepInterval: NodeJS.Timeout | null), call sweepInterval.unref() right after creation, and export a stopPatreonRoleDedup() that clears it; then call that from the gracefulShutdown feature-cleanup section in src/startup/ready.ts alongside the other cleanups. Minimal fix if a stop hook is not wanted: append .unref() to the setInterval(...) call at line 178 (mirrors src/events/interactionCreate.ts:80 and src/features/modmail/routing.ts:144).

title: Module-side-effect 24h cleanup setInterval in web process is never unref'd or cleared
detail: push-sender.ts runs a 24h setInterval as an import side-effect with no .unref() and no stored handle, and rateLimiter.ts:149 does the same for the bot process (the latter is explicitly acknowledged in a comment as 'never cleared'). In normal production both are harmless singletons: the module is imported exactly once per process, the interval fires rarely, and the process is long-lived, so nothing accumulates. The reason this is worth flagging rather than dismissing is the dev/test angle: under Vite/SvelteKit HMR or repeated vi importing of the module graph, a re-evaluated module installs an additional uncancellable interval each time (the previous one cannot be cleared because the handle was discarded), and because it is not unref'd it also keeps the event loop alive, which can make Vitest workers hang on teardown. This is a latent test-hygiene/leak risk, not a production memory leak.
fix: Append .unref() to both setInterval calls (push-sender.ts:161 and src/lib/rateLimiter.ts:149) so they cannot pin the event loop, and/or store the handle behind an idempotent init guard so HMR/test re-import does not stack duplicate intervals.

title: SSE fan-out client removal depends solely on ReadableStream cancel(); error path clears the heartbeat timer but does not call removeClient()
detail: addClient() registers the connection in the module-level clients Map in fan-out.ts (cap 200). The only call to removeClient(clientId) is in the stream's cancel() callback (line 64). Inside the heartbeat, if send() throws because the controller is already closed/errored, the code clears heartbeatTimer (line 57) but does NOT call removeClient, trusting cancel() to run. This is a cross-file trust: the +server.ts handler assumes the platform always invokes cancel() on a dead stream. If the stream transitions to errored rather than cancelled (or the adapter/proxy drops it without surfacing a cancel), the clients entry persists. In practice this is self-healing -- fan-out.ts safeSend() (lines 113-121) deletes any client whose send() throws on the next broadcast -- so a stale entry is reclaimed at the next published event and the MAX_CLIENTS=200 cap bounds worst-case growth. Hence low severity: a transient over-count that resolves on the next broadcast, not an unbounded leak. Worth noting because the cleanup correctness here rests entirely on safeSend compensating for the missing removeClient on the error path.
fix: In the heartbeat catch block (and any send-failure path) call removeClient(clientId) in addition to clearing the timer, so client removal does not depend exclusively on cancel() firing. This makes the two cleanup paths (cancel vs send-error) symmetric and removes the implicit dependence on safeSend for reclamation.

title: Level-reward dedup row is committed BEFORE grants succeed, so a transient grant failure permanently skips the reward
detail: handleLevelRoleAdded() writes the dedup marker first: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO level_reward_granted (guild_id,user_id,level)` (lines 130-133). It then loops over rewards calling assignRole() (line 180). I confirmed in src/features/roleAutomation.ts:298-318 that assignRole()'s `member.roles.add()` call is wrapped in try/catch and returns `{success:false, action:'skipped'}` on ANY error (Discord 429 rate-limit, 5xx, network blip) WITHOUT throwing. levelRewards.ts records these in `failedRewards` and logs 'reward_error' (lines 198-209) but never deletes the dedup row. On the next guildMemberUpdate for the same level (the code explicitly notes Amaribot re-syncs and re-joins are normal, lines 268-269), `dedupResult.changes === 0` triggers the early return at line 143, so the previously-failed reward role is never retried. The user permanently loses that reward. A repo-wide grep confirms there is NO DELETE from level_reward_granted anywhere (only the migration backfill + this insert). docs/INCIDENTS.md:57 documents the dedup-first design as the INC-005 TOCTOU fix, but the ordering converts a transient failure into a permanent one — the code carefully distinguishes granted/skipped/failed yet treats all three identically for dedup purposes.
fix: Only write the dedup marker after a reward is actually granted, OR delete/avoid the dedup row when failedRewards.length>0. Concretely: move the INSERT OR IGNORE to run per-reward after `result.action === 'add'` succeeds, or wrap the dedup-insert + grants in a transaction and `throw` to roll back the marker if any reward returns success:false (so the next event retries). At minimum, on failure execute `DELETE FROM level_reward_granted WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND level=?` so the failed grant can be retried.

title: handleArtistRoleChange is awaited without try/catch in guildMemberUpdate, so an artist-role error aborts all downstream handlers (NSFW scan, Patreon dedup, level rewards)
detail: In the guildMemberUpdate handler, `await handleArtistRoleChange(oldMember, newMember)` (line 264) is the only top-level call NOT wrapped in its own try/catch — every sibling (handleAvatarChange line 269-277, handlePatreonRoleDedup 288-296, handlePatreonArtRewards 299-308, handleLevelRoleAdded 313-325) is individually guarded precisely so one failure cannot block the others. handleArtistRoleChange (src/features/artistRotation/roleSync.ts:159-172) calls handleArtistRoleAdded/Removed which do DB writes and Discord API calls and can throw. If it throws, execution leaves the callback before reaching NSFW avatar scanning and level-reward granting for that member update. wrapEvent() catches the rejection so the bot does not crash and the failure is logged, but the user silently loses level-up rewards / NSFW monitoring for that event. The inconsistency with its siblings makes this a clear oversight rather than intentional.
fix: Wrap the call in try/catch like its siblings: `try { await handleArtistRoleChange(oldMember, newMember); } catch (err) { logger.error({ err, userId: newMember.id, guildId: newMember.guild.id }, '[guildMemberUpdate] artist role change failed'); }`

title: handleSubmit passes `guild!` (non-null asserted) to logActionPretty when the guild may be a cache miss, silently dropping the gate_submit audit log
detail: At line 534, `const guild = interaction.client.guilds.cache.get(session.guildId)` can return undefined (cache miss, e.g. shortly after a gateway reconnect before guild hydration). Line 535 guards `if (guild)` for cacheUser, but line 565 dereferences `guild!` to call logActionPretty(guild!, ...). logActionPretty is async and first touches guild at pretty.ts:488 (`guild.id`) inside its body, so a cache-miss produces a rejected promise that IS swallowed by the `.catch()` at line 571 — no crash, but the 'gate_submit' action is never written to action_log, creating a silent audit-trail gap for a successfully submitted application. The `guild!` assertion also defeats the type checker's null-safety here.
fix: Guard the log call: `if (guild) { await logActionPretty(guild, {...}).catch(...); }` and remove the `!` assertion. Optionally fall back to `await interaction.client.guilds.fetch(session.guildId)` if the cache miss matters, or log a warning when guild is unexpectedly absent.

title: Remote migration wrapper exits 0 when the migration child is killed by a signal
detail: spawnSync runs scripts/migrate.ts and then `process.exit(result.status || 0)`. When the child process is terminated by a signal rather than a normal exit (OOM kill, SIGTERM during deploy), spawnSync sets `result.status` to null and `result.signal` to the signal name. `null || 0` evaluates to 0, so this wrapper reports SUCCESS even though the migration was killed mid-run. A deploy script keying off this exit code would proceed as if migrations completed. (A normal migration failure is fine: migrate.ts exits 1, status=1, 1||0=1.)
fix: Treat signal death and null status as failure: `if (result.status === null) process.exit(1); process.exit(result.status);` (or `process.exit(result.status ?? 1)` and also check result.signal/result.error).

title: Migration 039 never records itself and runs on a different DB connection outside the runner transaction
detail: Of all 70 migrations, 039 is the only one that (a) does NOT call recordMigration(...) and (b) imports the long-lived singleton `db` from ../src/db/db.js (line 12) instead of using the `db` argument the runner passes. The runner (scripts/migrate.ts:209-213) executes `db.transaction(() => migrateFn(db))` and itself NEVER inserts into schema_migrations -- recording is delegated entirely to each migration via recordMigration (see helpers.ts:149). Consequences: (1) Because 039 never writes a schema_migrations row, getAppliedVersions() never sees '039', so scanMigrations keeps it in `pendingMigrations` and it re-runs on EVERY `npm run migrate` / deploy. (2) migrateFn(db) ignores the passed handle; all of 039's writes go through the src/db/db.js singleton connection (a second connection to the same WAL file, opened with different pragmas and a prepare() wrapper). So 039's work happens OUTSIDE the runner's transaction -- if a later statement in that wrapped transaction threw, 039's index/renumber changes would NOT roll back, breaking the atomicity guarantee the runner advertises. The dedup + `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` + `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` body is itself idempotent so re-running is not catastrophic, but the migration is permanently 'pending', runs un-transactionally, and may touch a different DB path than the one the runner backed up.
fix: Change the signature to `export function migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint(db: Database): void`, drop the `import { db } from "../src/db/db.js"` line so it uses the passed-in handle, and add `recordMigration(db, "039", "fix_art_job_unique_constraint")` at the end (importing it from ./lib/helpers.js), matching every other migration.

title: review_claim.claimed_at is written as an integer into a TEXT column, so normalizeTimestamp always returns null and the dashboard 'claimed at' time is permanently blank
detail: review_claim.claimed_at is declared `TEXT NOT NULL` (src/db/db.ts:129-133 and tests/fixtures/schema.sql:766-770). The production writer reviewActions.ts:110 inserts `nowUtc()` (an integer, e.g. 1748000000) with a comment claiming it is 'matching both table schemas' -- but the column has TEXT affinity, so SQLite coerces the integer to the STRING '1748000000.0' (verified empirically with better-sqlite3). The reader getReviewQueue/getApplicationDetail passes claimed_at through normalizeTimestamp (shared.ts), whose string branch does `value.replace(' ','T') + 'Z'` -> '1748000000.0Z' -> new Date(...) -> NaN -> returns null. Verified: normalizeTimestamp('1748000000.0') === null. Net effect: ReviewQueueItem.claimedAt and ApplicationDetail.claimedAt are ALWAYS null in the dashboard, so reviewers never see when an application was claimed. This is masked by the test suite because the test fixture (tests/utils/dbFixtures.ts:334) inserts claimed_at as `new Date().toISOString()` (a real ISO string that normalizeTimestamp parses fine) -- the fixture does not match how production writes the column, so tests pass while production is broken.
fix: Make normalizeTimestamp recognize numeric strings (e.g. if `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(value)` treat it as a unix-seconds/ms number and reuse the numeric branch), OR change the writer to store ISO text via tsToIso(nowUtc()) into the TEXT column, OR migrate review_claim.claimed_at to INTEGER and store seconds. The numeric-string guard in normalizeTimestamp is the lowest-risk fix and also hardens every other TEXT-affinity timestamp reader.

title: Command-center decisionsToday and weekStats omit 'perm_reject', undercounting decisions and skewing avg response time
detail: decisionsToday (line 74) and the weekStats decisions+avg query (line 88) filter `action IN ('approve', 'reject', 'kick')`, omitting 'perm_reject'. Permanent rejections ARE written to review_action with action='perm_reject' (src/features/review/flows/reject.ts:69-77: `const action = permanent ? 'perm_reject' : 'reject'`). Every other decision query in the codebase consistently uses the 4-verb set `('approve','reject','perm_reject','kick')` (see web/src/lib/server/queries/stats.ts and observatory refresh). A grep confirms home.ts lines 74 and 88 are the ONLY occurrences of the 3-verb set anywhere. Result: the home dashboard's 'decisions today' and 'this week' counts under-report by the number of permanent rejections, and the weekly avg-response-time computation excludes perm_reject decisions entirely, so its mean is biased.
fix: Add 'perm_reject' to both IN lists so home.ts matches the rest of the system: `action IN ('approve', 'reject', 'perm_reject', 'kick')`.

title: getApplicationFunnel counts status='perm_rejected', a status the bot never writes, so permRejected is always 0 and permanent rejections are silently bucketed as 'rejected'
detail: The funnel query has `SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'perm_rejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as perm_rejected` and also lists 'perm_rejected' in the 'submitted' rollup. But there is no 'perm_rejected' application status anywhere: the application CHECK constraint only allows ('draft','submitted','approved','rejected','needs_info','kicked') (tests/fixtures/schema.sql:201) and the reject transaction sets status='rejected' (with permanently_rejected=1) for BOTH normal and permanent rejections (src/features/review/flows/reject.ts:82-91). This is documented in src/features/gate/drafts.ts:193 and src/commands/listopen.ts:46: 'Permanently rejected apps have status=\'rejected\' with permanently_rejected=1'. Consequences: FunnelMetrics.permRejected is permanently 0, and every permanent rejection is counted in the `rejected` bucket -- the funnel cannot distinguish them. The query ignores the application.permanently_rejected flag entirely.
fix: Count permanent rejections via the real signal: `SUM(CASE WHEN status='rejected' AND permanently_rejected=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS perm_rejected` and, if `rejected` should exclude them, `SUM(CASE WHEN status='rejected' AND COALESCE(permanently_rejected,0)=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rejected`. Drop 'perm_rejected' from the status IN-lists.

category: JOIN/source correctness (event-log assumption on a current-state table)
title: Observatory leaves / cumulative_net / cohort retention treat user_activity as a join/leave event log, but it stores one current-state row per user that is mutated on rejoin
detail: rebuildDailyMetrics derives daily `leaves` from `COUNT(*) ... WHERE left_at IS NOT NULL GROUP BY date(left_at)` and `joins` from `date(joined_at)`, and cumulative_net accumulates joins-leaves. rebuildCohortRetention buckets members by join-week. But user_activity has PRIMARY KEY (guild_id, user_id) and is upserted: trackJoin (src/features/activityTracker.ts:40-48) does `ON CONFLICT(guild_id,user_id) DO UPDATE SET joined_at = excluded.joined_at, left_at = NULL`. So a member who leaves and later rejoins has their prior leave ERASED (left_at reset to NULL) and their original join day MOVED to the latest join. This makes historical daily `leaves` and `cumulative_net` change retroactively on every rejoin, undercounts gross churn, and shifts cohort membership/size for past weeks. The rollup faithfully reflects stored data, but it trusts user_activity to be an append-only event log when activityTracker maintains it as mutable current-state. (Same assumption underlies the pulse leave-spike / rapid-join-leave detectors in queries/pulse.ts.)
fix: Either source join/leave events from an append-only log (e.g. action_log member_join/member_leave events or invite_usage.joined_at_s) instead of user_activity, or explicitly document leaves/cohort as 'net current-state' metrics. If event-accurate churn is required, stop resetting left_at to NULL on rejoin and record each membership span separately.

category: NULL handling / restart-spanning sessions not capped
title: Pulse voice-minute sums count open sessions to the window end with no per-session cap, so restart-swept sessions inflate voice minutes (observatory caps these; pulse does not)
detail: Every pulse voice aggregation computes duration as `CASE WHEN left_at_s IS NOT NULL THEN left_at_s - joined_at_s ELSE <boundary> - joined_at_s END` with no upper bound per session (weekStats line 334-339, getTopVoiceChannels 454, engagementBucket 555-560, detectVoiceTrend 963-965). On bot shutdown, dangling sessions are swept by setting left_at_s = now (voiceSessionTracker.ts closeAllStmt: `UPDATE voice_session SET left_at_s = ? WHERE left_at_s IS NULL`), as the design brief explicitly warns (docs/stats-observatory/design-brief.md item 7). A session that spanned a multi-day outage thus gets an artificially long duration and spikes daily/weekly voice minutes around deploys. The public observatory rollup guards against exactly this with a 6h per-session cap (refresh.ts:35,209-217, verified correct), but the internal pulse/newsletter queries do not, so the two surfaces disagree and pulse over-reports voice minutes after any restart with users in voice.
fix: Apply the same per-session cap pulse-side, e.g. `MIN(21600, COALESCE(left_at_s, :boundary) - joined_at_s)`, mirroring VOICE_SESSION_CAP_S in refresh.ts, so internal and public voice totals agree and restart sweeps cannot inflate them.

title: Byte token redemption is non-atomic: token role is removed before the multiplier is granted/tracked, so a mid-flow failure destroys the entitlement with nothing in return
detail: handleConfirm performs a multi-step Discord+DB sequence with no transaction or rollback: Step 1 removes the token role (line 314-317), Step 3 adds the multiplier role (line 348-351), Step 4 writes the DB tracking row via upsertActiveMultiplier (line 385-394). These are independent awaited Discord REST calls plus a SQLite write. If the bot crashes, the process is killed, or roles.add() throws (rate-limit 429, transient 500, hierarchy change between the pre-flight canManageRole check at line 245 and the actual add) AFTER the token role has already been removed at line 314, the user has permanently lost their byte token (the giveaway/shop entitlement) and received no multiplier. The catch block at line 449 only edits the reply with a generic error; it does NOT re-add the removed token role. Because the token role IS the entitlement (there is no separate balance ledger - see usebyte.ts findMemberByteTokens which reads role presence as the source of truth), this is an irreversible economic loss. Cross-file: usebyte.ts treats role presence as the wallet, while byteTokenHandler.ts mutates that wallet non-transactionally and trusts that every step after the destructive remove() will succeed.
fix: Reorder to grant-then-consume (add multiplier + write DB row FIRST, remove token role LAST), so a failure leaves the user still holding the token. Alternatively, on any failure after the token removal, compensate by re-adding the token role in the catch block. Best: record an intent/ledger row before touching Discord and reconcile on restart.

title: Byte token confirm is a check-then-act race: entitlement is gated only on the eventually-consistent Discord role cache, with no DB guard, so concurrent confirms can re-grant and reset expiry from a single token
detail: The only guard preventing double-redemption is guildMember.roles.cache.has(tokenConfig.tokenRoleId) at line 283, read from a member fetched per-interaction. The interaction-dedup in interactionCreate.ts (line 69-97, keyed on interaction.id) does NOT help here because two distinct clicks - or two confirmation messages produced by running /usebyte twice - carry distinct interaction IDs. There is no DB-level idempotency: upsertActiveMultiplier (byteMultiplierStore.ts line 66-79) uses ON CONFLICT(guild_id,user_id) DO UPDATE, which unconditionally rewrites expires_at to now+duration on every call. So a user who double-clicks Confirm can have both handlers pass the role.has() check before either removal propagates, and both call upsert; the second call resets the boost expiry to a fresh full duration off a single consumed token. The post-add race cleanup at line 353-382 only removes OTHER multiplier roles, not the duplicate grant of the same role, and does nothing about the duplicated expiry reset.
