There is no per-user lock around handleConfirm.
fix: Make consumption atomic in SQLite: gate redemption on a conditional write (e.g., an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING into a redemption-claim table keyed by a single-use token instance, or a transaction that both records the spend and refuses if already spent) BEFORE removing the Discord role, and only proceed if changes===1. Add a short per-(guild,user) in-process mutex as defense in depth.

title: Level-reward dedup marker is written before checking whether any reward exists, permanently blocking rewards added to that level later (silent under-grant)
detail: handleLevelRoleAdded writes the permanent dedup row INSERT OR IGNORE INTO level_reward_granted (guild_id,user_id,level) at line 130-133, and only AFTERWARD calls getLevelRewards(guild.id, level) at line 146. When a user reaches a level that currently has zero configured rewards, the function still commits the dedup marker, then returns at line 147-154 because rewards.length===0. The dedup table has UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,level) and is never cleared (migration 057; only roles.ts:538 deletes from level_rewards config, not from level_reward_granted). Consequently, if staff later add a token/ticket reward for that level (a normal economy operation), every user who already passed that level can NEVER receive it: the dedup INSERT OR IGNORE returns changes===0 and the function short-circuits at line 135-143 before getLevelRewards is ever consulted. Cross-file: the reward catalog (level_rewards, edited via roles.ts) and the dedup ledger (level_reward_granted) are decoupled, and the ordering here makes the ledger record a 'granted' fact that never happened.
fix: Check getLevelRewards FIRST and return early when there are no rewards, WITHOUT writing the dedup row. Only insert the dedup marker once you have a non-empty reward set to grant (ideally insert it inside the same transaction that performs/records the grants). This preserves idempotency while letting newly-added level rewards reach users who level past that tier afterward.

title: Art-ticket redemption (/redeemreward) trusts a stale role snapshot captured at command time and the only spend-guard (Discord ticket-role removal) is non-atomic, allowing double-spend of one ticket across two confirmations
detail: redeemreward.ts builds the confirmation when staff invokes the command, encoding recipientId+artType into the button customId (line 283). The actual debit happens later in handlers.ts handleConfirm: after deferUpdate (line 120) it fetches the member and removes the ticket role only if member.roles.cache.has(ticketRoleId) (line 131-134). There is no DB-backed entitlement for art tickets in the redeem path - the Discord ticket role IS the single-use token (see redeemreward.ts comment line 81-83 'we remove the role so they can't double-dip'). Because the has()-check + remove() is a check-then-act on the eventually-consistent cache with no transactional claim, two confirmations for the same recipient+type (e.g., staff double-clicks, or two staff each run /redeemreward for the same person before either confirms) can both observe the role present, both 'succeed', and produce TWO assignments + TWO art_job rows (createJob, line 258) while only one ticket existed. The branch at line 135-137 ('User did not have ticket role') still proceeds to assign an artist and create a job, so even a redemption against a user with NO ticket is logged as a successful assignment with only a soft warning embed. This is the spend half of the same economy whose grant half is patreon_art_granted; neither side reconciles against the other.
fix: Tie the spend to an atomic DB claim instead of (or in addition to) the Discord role: in handleConfirm, perform a conditional decrement/claim against a per-user art-ticket ledger inside a transaction and abort if nothing was claimed. At minimum, hard-fail (do not create a job or rotate the artist) when the recipient does not actually hold the ticket role, and de-duplicate concurrent confirms with a per-(recipient,artType) guard.

title: Patreon art entitlements with quantity>1 collapse onto a single binary ticket role, so a tier promising 2 emoji tickets only ever yields one redeemable ticket
detail: PATREON_ART_ENTITLEMENTS defines quantity>1 for some tiers (Legendary Fiona emoji: 2, line 38). handlePatreonArtRewards computes delta = entitlement - alreadyGranted (line 182) and then assigns the single ticket role exactly once (assignRole, line 189-195) regardless of delta, while upsertGrant sets quantity_granted to the full entitlement via MAX() (store.ts line 96-103). The DB high-water mark therefore records '2 emoji granted' but the user only ever holds ONE binary emoji ticket role. On the spend side (artistRotation/handlers.ts line 131-134) /redeemreward removes that one role, and because patreon_art_granted already reads 2 the periodic sweep (patreonRoleDedup.ts sweepOnce -> handlePatreonArtRewards every 10 min) sees entitlement(2) <= alreadyGranted(2) and never re-grants, so the second emoji ticket is silently lost. The grant ledger (quantity_granted) and the redeem mechanism (binary role presence) are two different representations that disagree whenever quantity>1. Note: a redemption-counter audit already on file (audit/2026-05-31) corroborates this; reported here as an independently-confirmed economy defect.
fix: Track redeemed vs remaining (e.g., remaining = quantity_granted - redeemed) on patreon_art_granted, decrement remaining in the /redeemreward confirm handler, and re-grant the ticket role whenever remaining>0 and the user lacks it. Alternatively model quantity>1 as multiple distinct redeemable units. Until fixed, no tier should declare quantity>1 against a single binary ticket role.

title: Expiry cleanup deletes the DB tracking row before (and regardless of whether) the Discord multiplier role is removed; panic mode and member-fetch failures orphan the boost role with no record to retry
detail: removeExpiredMultipliers (byteMultiplierStore.ts line 182-204) fetches expired rows and DELETEs them in the same call. cleanupExpiredMultipliers then tries to strip the Discord role per entry. But if the guild is in panic mode the handler returns early at line 100-109 AFTER the row is already deleted (the code comment at line 105-107 acknowledges staff must remove the role manually). The same orphaning occurs on any non-thrown early return: guild not cached (line 90-97) or member fetch returning null (line 112-120). Because the authoritative record was already destroyed, the scheduler can never retry these, so an expired XP multiplier role persists indefinitely on the member - a continuing economic over-grant (free boost) that no automated process will reclaim. Cross-file: the store's 'delete-on-read' design (intended to prevent double-processing) trades away the ability of the scheduler to recover from its own skipped work.
fix: Only delete rows that were actually reconciled. Either (a) select expired rows, attempt role removal, and DELETE only the successfully-processed ids; or (b) keep the row and mark a processed/last_attempt column, deleting only after confirmed Discord removal. Skip-and-retain on panic mode / fetch failure so the next run can finish the job.

title: Legendary and Epic tokens map to the same multiplier role and value, so the single-row tracking model lets a consumed higher token silently downgrade an active boost with no real warning
detail: BYTE_TOKEN_CONFIG.epic and .legendary share multiplierRoleId '1405369052829974543' and multiplierValue 5, differing only in durationHours (48 vs 72). active_byte_multipliers enforces UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id) (migration 044 line 87), so a user can hold only one tracked multiplier. If a user redeems Legendary (role X, 72h) and later redeems Epic while X is still active, byteTokenHandler upsert overwrites expires_at to now+48h (byteMultiplierStore.ts line 71-78) - the consumed Epic token strictly shortens their remaining boost. The confirmation UI's replace-warning (usebyte.ts line 224-231 / byteTokenHandler.ts line 568-574) shows both as '[5x] Byte'/5x, so the user sees no indication they are trading down. Net effect: a redeemed token can be wasted (or actively reduce value) with no surfaced downside, and the two rarities can never be 'active simultaneously' despite being distinct entitlements.
fix: Either give legendary its own multiplier role, or, before overwriting, compare expiries and keep the longer-lived boost (only extend, never shorten, when the incoming multiplierValue is equal). Make the replace-warning show actual remaining time vs proposed time so users can see a downgrade. Confirm with product whether legendary collapsing into the epic role is intended.

title: Watchdog auto-defers modals with deferReply, racing handlers that ack via deferUpdate
detail: armWatchdog() is armed in interactionCreate.ts (line 219) for EVERY interaction before dispatch, and its 2500ms timer calls modalInteraction.deferReply({ephemeral}) for any unacked ModalSubmitInteraction. However, the review modal handlers (src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts handleRejectModal/handleAcceptModal/handleKickModal/handleUnclaimModal/handleVoteOutModal, all lines ~49/87/126/166/203) and the QOTD reject handler (src/features/qotd/handlers.ts:288-290) acknowledge the SAME modal via deferUpdate(), NOT deferReply. These handlers do meaningful pre-ack work first: requireInteractionStaff -> resolveApplication (findAppByShortCode + loadApplication SQLite) before calling deferUpdate. If that work plus event-loop contention pushes past 2500ms, the watchdog wins the race and calls deferReply first. The handler's later deferUpdate() then fails with 40060 (caught/swallowed by the .catch). Net result: a stray ephemeral 'Bot is thinking...' spinner that never resolves to content (the action's real output goes to interaction.channel.send / interaction.message.edit, not the deferred reply), and the response-state telemetry in the wide event is corrupted (markDeferred recorded, deferUpdate path not). The watchdog and the deferUpdate-based handlers were written against different ack models and only coexist safely because handlers are usually <2500ms. cmdWrap's own comment claims the watchdog 'Only defers modals; slash/button defers are handled by higher-level wrappers' but does not account for handlers that deliberately use deferUpdate.
fix: Make the watchdog ack-type aware, or do not arm it for routes that ack via deferUpdate. Simplest: have armWatchdog use deferUpdate() for modals that originate from a message component (interaction.message != null) and deferReply() only for showModal-from-slash modals; OR drop the global watchdog and let each wrapCommand-wrapped handler own its defer. At minimum, raise WATCHDOG_MS only matters if handlers are slow; the correct fix is to not let two code paths defer the same token with different methods.

title: replyOrEdit silently drops ephemeral (and all) flags on the deferred path
detail: replyOrEdit destructures and discards `flags` when the interaction is deferred: `const { flags, ...editPayload } = withFlags; result = await interaction.editReply(editPayload);` (lines 504-506). editReply genuinely cannot change ephemerality (it's fixed at defer time), so the discard is technically necessary, but the function accepts `flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral` from callers and silently ignores it with no warning. Multiple callers pass ephemeral expecting privacy and trust replyOrEdit to honor it: e.g. handleUnclaimModal's 'You must type UNCLAIM' branch (src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts:259-261), runVoteOutAction's 'Vote out requires a reason' (actionRunners.ts:830-833), and the openRejectModal/openAcceptModal already-resolved branches (helpers.ts:187, 212) all pass flags:Ephemeral. Today these are visually correct only by luck because the preceding ack on those paths was already ephemeral (deferUpdate on the source message keeps the response component-scoped, or ensureDeferred deferred ephemeral). The cross-file trust hazard: any handler that defers PUBLIC (e.g. handleModmailContextMenu deferReply() with no flag, modmail/handlers.ts:190) and then routes a sensitive message through replyOrEdit({flags:Ephemeral}) will leak it publicly with zero indication the flag was dropped.
fix: If a caller passes Ephemeral on a deferred interaction whose deferral was public, log a warning (the flag cannot be honored) so the mismatch is visible. Better: track the deferral's ephemerality on the wide event and assert callers' flags match; or split the API into replyOrEditPublic / replyOrEditEphemeral so the intent is fixed at defer time, not silently reconciled at edit time.

title: safeShowModal dead-ends the user (no ack, no message) past the 2500ms token boundary; caller ignores the false return
detail: safeShowModal returns false (a) if the interaction is already acked, (b) if Date.now()-createdTimestamp > 2500ms, or (c) if showModal throws — and in cases (b)/(c) it sends NO user-facing feedback and performs NO acknowledgement. handleReviewButton (buttons.ts) calls openRejectModal/openAcceptModal/openKickModal/openUnclaimModal/openVoteOutModal which call safeShowModal, and NONE of these call sites inspect the boolean return. For reject/accept/kick/unclaim the button path runs resolveApplication (two synchronous SQLite lookups) BEFORE reaching safeShowModal; under DB lock contention (the codebase elsewhere retries SQLITE_BUSY, see dmVerification.ts:378-389) or event-loop pressure the interaction can cross 2500ms, after which safeShowModal silently bails and the moderator's click resolves to Discord's generic 'This interaction failed' with no modal, no ephemeral error, and no logged trace surfaced to them. Because the interaction was never acked, no error card fires either. This is a cross-file trust gap: buttons.ts trusts safeShowModal to either show the modal or surface a failure, but safeShowModal's contract is 'return false and stay silent'.
fix: Have safeShowModal's caller act on the false return: when it returns false and the interaction is still unacked, send an ephemeral reply ('That action timed out, click again.'). Alternatively move the resolveApplication DB work to AFTER showModal where possible, since showModal needs the fresh token most; for reject/accept the app existence can be revalidated in the modal-submit handler (which it already is via resolveApplication).

title: Modmail context-menu defers and replies PUBLICLY, unlike the button path which keeps failures ephemeral
detail: handleModmailContextMenu calls interaction.deferReply() with no MessageFlags.Ephemeral (line 190) and then interaction.editReply({content: result.message}) (line 239), so both the 'Bot is thinking…' state and the final outcome message (including failure strings like 'Failed to create modmail thread. Check bot permissions.') are PUBLIC in whatever channel the staffer right-clicked a message in. The sibling button handler handleModmailOpenButton deliberately keeps the failure path ephemeral (followUp with flags:Ephemeral, lines 125-131) and only posts success publicly. The inline comment at line 188 ('Context menus don't support deferUpdate, so we use deferReply') justifies the deferReply but not the missing Ephemeral flag. Impact: a permission/setup failure when opening modmail from a context menu is broadcast to the channel rather than shown privately to the acting moderator, and the public 'thinking' bubble appears in a potentially user-visible channel.
fix: Pass flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral to deferReply() in handleModmailContextMenu so the staffer's interaction matches the ephemeral semantics of the button path; post the public 'thread created' confirmation via interaction.channel.send (as the button path does) instead of via the public editReply.

title: Router catch-all error card visibility is non-deterministic: ephemeral for unacked interactions, public for buttons already acked via deferUpdate
detail: The router's catch-all (interactionCreate.ts:1103-1119) handles uncaught throws from UNWRAPPED handlers (buttons, selects, context menus — only slash + the explicitly wrapCommand'd modal routes get V2 cards internally). It calls ensureDeferred(interaction) then postErrorCard. ensureDeferred only defers if NOT already deferred/replied (cmdWrap.ts:449). Many button handlers call interaction.deferUpdate() early (review buttons.ts:177-181, modmail handlers.ts:92/150, qotd handlers.ts:126), which sets interaction.replied=true. For those, ensureDeferred is a no-op, and postErrorCard -> replyOrEdit takes the `interaction.replied` branch -> followUp(withFlags) with flags defaulting to 0 (cmdWrap.ts:500,509) -> a PUBLIC error card carrying technical 'Code/Last SQL/Hint' fields (errorCard.ts:204-215) is posted into the channel. For a handler that threw BEFORE acking, the same path produces an EPHEMERAL card (ensureDeferred deferred ephemeral, then editReply). So the same failure is sometimes private, sometimes a public channel post with internal diagnostics, determined solely by how far the handler got before throwing. errorCard.ts's own comment (line 224) claims cards are intentionally public 'so staff can see them', but the ensureDeferred path makes them ephemeral, so the two modules disagree on intent.
fix: Decide the error-card visibility policy in one place. If cards should be ephemeral, force the followUp in the replied branch to flags:Ephemeral when the original ack was a component deferUpdate. If they should be public, drop the ensureDeferred(ephemeral) call in the router catch-all. Either way, make postErrorCard explicit about ephemerality rather than inheriting it from prior ack state.

title: Gate Start button does heavy work before showModal/DM with no defer, relying on staying under the 3s window
detail: handleStartButton (the Verify flow entry) is a button handler that for page>0 runs getQuestions + paginate + getOrCreateDraft + getDraft + buildModalForPage and THEN calls interaction.showModal(modal) (lines 55-69) with no defer — correct, because showModal cannot follow a defer. For page 0 it delegates to startDmVerification which, in DM mode (non-thread), also must stay unacked so it can fall back to showModal (dmVerification.ts:171-178 only defers in thread mode). The cross-file subtlety: armWatchdog is armed for this button (interactionCreate.ts:219) but is a no-op for non-modal interactions, so it provides NO protection here. If the synchronous DB work (getOrCreateDraft can run inserts) or a slow interaction.user.send() in startDmVerification exceeds 3s, the token expires and showModal/reply throws 10062; the catch (handlers.ts:70-81) then tries interaction.reply which also 10062s. The user sees 'interaction failed' with no recovery. This is acceptable-by-design (defer is impossible before showModal) but the work done before the ack is larger than ideal and there is no fast-path ack.
fix: Minimize pre-showModal work on page navigation: build the modal from already-cached question data and defer all DB writes (draft creation) to the modal-submit handler (handleGateModalSubmit already creates the draft on 'NEW'). For page>0, prefer showing the modal from in-memory paginated questions without re-hitting getOrCreateDraft.

title: ensurePokeConfigColumns() is never called -> poke config columns missing in prod DB -> /config poke crashes
detail: ensurePokeConfigColumns (config.ts:492) is the ONLY code path that adds guild_config.poke_category_ids_json and poke_excluded_channel_ids_json. There is no migration for them (grep 'poke' across migrations/ = zero hits) and they are absent from tests/fixtures/schema.sql. The startup self-heal runner src/startup/schema.ts wires in 7 other config ensure* functions (lines 67-73) but omits ensurePokeConfigColumns, despite its own comment (schema.ts:11-12) saying new ensure* functions must be appended. git log -S 'ensurePokeConfigColumns' confirms the function was never referenced from index.ts/schema.ts. I opened the live production DB (DB_PATH=./data/data.db, 5GB, actively used) and confirmed both columns are ABSENT. Meanwhile /config poke (config/poke.ts) calls upsertConfig({ poke_category_ids_json: ... }); poke_category_ids_json is in the upsertConfig ALLOWLIST (config.ts:659) so it is NOT filtered out, and upsertConfig builds 'UPDATE guild_config SET poke_category_ids_json = ?' (config.ts:682). Against a table lacking the column this throws SqliteError: no such column: poke_category_ids_json. So setting poke target categories / excluded channels is currently a hard runtime failure in production, caused purely by an ensure function that is dead because nobody wired it in.
fix: Add ensurePokeConfigColumns and ensurePulseConfigColumns to the import block and call list in src/startup/schema.ts:runSchemaSelfHeal() (alongside ensureSkullModeColumns etc.). Alternatively delete the dead ensure functions and add a real numbered migration under migrations/ that ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN the poke/pulse columns, then run npm run migrate on prod. Either way the column-add must actually execute before /config poke is used.

title: ensurePulseConfigColumns() never called and migration 059 not applied -> pulse query SELECT crashes on prod DB
detail: pulse_excluded_category_ids_json is created by two redundant mechanisms: migration 059 (manual-only; migrations are NOT run at startup, only via npm run migrate) and ensurePulseConfigColumns (config.ts:534, never called by schema.ts or anything else). On the production DB, schema_migrations shows only 39 rows with the highest applied = 045, so migration 059 was never applied, and PRAGMA table_info(guild_config) confirms pulse_excluded_category_ids_json is ABSENT. Because the ensure function that would self-heal it is unwired, the column simply does not exist. The web dashboard reads it with an UNGUARDED query: web/src/lib/server/queries/pulse.ts:242 does db.prepare('SELECT pulse_excluded_category_ids_json FROM guild_config WHERE guild_id = ?').get(guildId). The subsequent 'if (!row?.pulse_excluded_category_ids_json)' guard only handles a NULL value, not a missing column, so the prepare/get throws 'no such column' before that guard runs. /config pulse writes via upsertConfig hit the same no-such-column failure as the poke case. This is the same root cause as the poke finding: an ensure helper that is dead because it was never added to the startup runner.
fix: Wire ensurePulseConfigColumns into src/startup/schema.ts:runSchemaSelfHeal(), OR run the existing migration 059 on prod (npm run migrate) and keep migrations as the single source of truth (then delete the dead ensure function). Pick one mechanism; having an unrun migration AND an unwired ensure function is what produced the gap.

title: Entire /analytics command module is unreachable (not registered); 481 lines kept compiling only by tests
detail: command.ts exports executeAnalyticsCommand, executeAnalyticsExportCommand, parseWindow. Outside its own file and tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts, the module has zero importers (verified: grep for the symbol names and 'analytics/command' returns only the file itself + the test). The command name 'analytics' is NOT in src/commands/runtimeManifest.ts (full SLASH_COMMAND_NAMES list dumped and checked) and is not registered in src/index.ts. The functionality was consolidated into /stats (src/commands/stats/* with handlers wired in stats/index.ts). So this is a fully unreachable command handler: it can never be invoked at runtime. It only survives the noUnusedLocals/typecheck gate because its test imports it. This also drags src/features/analytics/queries.ts (528 lines: getActionCountsByMod/getLeadTimeStats/getTopReasons/getVolumeSeries/getOpenQueueAge) into deadness -- queries.ts is imported ONLY by this dead command.ts (verified per-symbol).
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/command.ts and src/features/analytics/queries.ts plus their test files (tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts, queries.test.ts). Keep src/features/analytics/approvalRate.ts -- it is still live (used by src/commands/stats/approvalRate.ts). Confirm nothing in /stats relies on queries.ts (it does not; /stats uses its own handlers) before removal.

title: Entire /approval-rate command module is unreachable (not registered); 196 dead lines
detail: executeApprovalRateCommand (approvalRateCommand.ts:39) is the handler for a standalone /approval-rate command. The module is imported by nobody (verified: only self-references in its own header/docstring; no import of 'approvalRateCommand' anywhere in src/web/scripts/tests). 'approval-rate' is not a standalone entry in runtimeManifest -- only '/stats approval-rate' exists (stats/index.ts:50 routes to handleApprovalRate in commands/stats/approvalRate.ts). So this old top-level handler is unreachable; the live approval-rate path is the /stats subcommand, which independently consumes analytics/approvalRate.ts. Dead since the stats consolidation.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/approvalRateCommand.ts. Verify no test imports it (none found) and that analytics/approvalRate.ts query functions remain referenced by commands/stats/approvalRate.ts (they are).

title: review/index.ts is a fully unused duplicate barrel; the live back-compat barrel is review.ts
detail: There are two barrels for the review module: src/features/review.ts (128 lines) and src/features/review/index.ts (113 lines). Both headers claim to provide 'backwards compatibility with imports from ./features/review.js'. Only review.ts is actually imported (e.g. gateMain.ts:30 renderWelcomeTemplate, web/routes/review.ts:23 ensureReviewMessage). review/index.ts would only be reached via an import from '...features/review' with no further path segment, and grep for that exact pattern (from '<...>features/review') returns ZERO matches across src/web/scripts/tests. It contains only re-exports (no side effects), so it is pure dead source. Its re-exports of DEFAULT_WELCOME_TEMPLATE and buildWelcomeNotice are doubly dead -- those symbols are also re-exported by review.ts and used only internally inside review/welcome.ts.
fix: Delete src/features/review/index.ts. Keep src/features/review.ts (the one consumers actually import). If a directory-style barrel is desired long-term, consolidate to one and update review.ts importers, but do not keep both.

title: archiveMessageRowSync / archiveReactionRowsSync are dead; 'used by backfill' comment is false
detail: Both functions are exported with the comment 'Direct synchronous insert used by backfill (bypasses buffer).' But the only importer of messageArchive is src/events/guildEvents.ts via 'import * as archive', and that namespace only ever accesses archive.archiveMessage, markMessageDeleted, recordReaction, removeReaction (verified by listing archive.* member access). Neither *RowSync function is referenced anywhere in src/scripts/tests/web (verified by name grep, no dynamic/string refs). The backfill command (commands/backfill.ts) contains no 'archive' reference at all. So these are dead exports with a misleading comment that implies a live consumer that does not exist.
fix: Remove archiveMessageRowSync and archiveReactionRowsSync (and the ArchiveRow/ReactionRow plumbing if it becomes unused), or actually wire them into the backfill path the comment references. Confirm backfill genuinely does not need synchronous inserts first.

title: pruneOldMessages() exported but never called -> message_activity retention never enforced
detail: pruneOldMessages(guildId, daysToKeep=90) is exported but has zero references outside its own file (verified across src/tests/scripts/web, no dynamic refs). This is a retention/cleanup function for the message_activity table that nothing schedules or invokes, so old message-activity rows are never pruned. Low severity as dead code, but note the latent operational consequence: unbounded growth of message_activity (consistent with the 5GB data.db observed).
fix: Either schedule pruneOldMessages from a periodic task (e.g. the scheduler used for other maintenance) so retention actually happens, or delete it if retention is intentionally handled elsewhere. Do not leave it as an exported no-op.

title: getAllActiveMultipliers() exported but never used
detail: getAllActiveMultipliers (byteMultiplierStore.ts:231), backed by the getAllActiveMultipliersStmt prepared statement (line 99), is exported but referenced nowhere outside its own file (verified; no dynamic refs). Dead read-side API. The prepared statement is initialized at module load regardless, so it is wasted work, though negligible.
fix: Delete getAllActiveMultipliers and its getAllActiveMultipliersStmt if no caller is planned, or wire it into whatever admin/debug surface intended to list active multipliers.

title: saveHeatmap() exported but never called
detail: The async saveHeatmap (activityHeatmap.ts:643) has no references outside its own file across src/tests/scripts/web (verified, including no dynamic-import string usage). It appears to be a persistence helper for heatmap data that nothing invokes; the live heatmap path on the web side uses getHeatmapDataForRange (web/src/lib/server/queries/heatmap.ts) which is a separate computation.
fix: Confirm no scheduler/job is meant to persist heatmaps; if not, delete saveHeatmap. If it is intended to back a cache/rollup, wire it into the relevant refresh task.

title: detachBadgeLiveListeners() exported but never called (paired attach has no teardown caller)
detail: detachBadgeLiveListeners(client) is exported but referenced nowhere outside its own file (verified). It is the teardown counterpart to the live badge listener attachment; nothing ever calls it (no shutdown hook in startup/ready.ts references it). Dead code; minor risk that listeners are never detached on the paths this was meant for, but practically the process exits anyway.
fix: Remove detachBadgeLiveListeners if listener teardown is not needed, or call it from the graceful-shutdown path if it is. Verify the attach side does not rely on a matching detach for correctness.

title: clearAllRulesCache() exported but never called
detail: clearAllRulesCache (rulesCache.ts:68) has no references outside its own file (verified across src/tests/scripts/web, no dynamic refs). It is a cache-invalidation helper that nothing triggers, so the rules cache is only ever invalidated by whatever per-entry mechanism exists (if any) and never globally. Dead export.
fix: Delete clearAllRulesCache, or invoke it where a full rules-cache flush is needed (e.g. on rules-channel reconfiguration) if that was the intent.

title: traceStore clearTraces() and stopAutoPrune() are dead (clearTraces comment claims 'for testing' but no test uses it)
detail: clearTraces (traceStore.ts:118, documented 'Clear all traces (for testing)') and stopAutoPrune (traceStore.ts:135) are exported but never imported anywhere, including tests (verified). startAutoPrune is auto-invoked at module load (line 143) and pruneExpired is used internally by it, so only the externally-facing teardown/test hooks are dead. Harmless but the 'for testing' comment is misleading since no test exercises it.
fix: Either add a test that uses clearTraces (justifying the comment) or remove clearTraces and stopAutoPrune. Keep startAutoPrune/pruneExpired (live).

title: Dashboard query helpers getFlaggedUsers() and getApplicationStatus() are unused
detail: Both exports in web/src/lib/server/queries/flags.ts have no consumers across web/src (.ts and .svelte) or tests (verified). SvelteKit load functions and components would reference them by name if used; they are not. Dead read-path code in the dashboard.
fix: Remove getFlaggedUsers and getApplicationStatus, or wire them into the flags route/+page.server.ts load if a flagged-users view is planned. Note SvelteKit does not tree-shake server-only modules into reachability guarantees, so manual confirmation (done) is the right check.

title: getHeatmapData() is a dead wrapper superseded by getHeatmapDataForRange()
detail: getHeatmapData(guildId, weeks=1) at heatmap.ts:197 is a thin wrapper whose own docstring (line 195) says callers should 'use getHeatmapDataForRange directly.' The live route web/src/routes/dashboard/heatmap/+page.server.ts:3,21 imports and uses getHeatmapDataForRange, not getHeatmapData. getHeatmapData has no other references (verified). Dead superseded wrapper.
fix: Delete getHeatmapData; the route already uses getHeatmapDataForRange.

lines: qotd.ts:164 getRecentSuggestions; fan-out.ts:62 getClientCount; format.ts:47 fmtMinutes
title: Several web exports unused: getRecentSuggestions, getClientCount, fmtMinutes
detail: Three independent dashboard exports have no references outside their declaring files across web/src (.ts/.svelte) and tests (verified per-symbol): getRecentSuggestions (qotd query), getClientCount (SSE fan-out client counter -- not surfaced anywhere), and fmtMinutes (observatory formatting helper alongside other fmt* helpers that ARE used). Dead exports, no runtime impact.
fix: Remove each unless it is about to be consumed by a new view/diagnostic. getClientCount in particular looks like it was meant for an SSE health/metrics surface that was never built -- decide build vs delete.

title: detectModmailResponseTime wraps indexed TEXT column in strftime(), forcing a full ticket scan
detail: The Pulse insights detector filters modmail_ticket with `WHERE mt.guild_id = ? AND strftime('%s', mt.created_at) >= ? AND strftime('%s', mt.created_at) < ?` (line 1179) and also computes `strftime('%s', mm.created_at) - strftime('%s', mt.created_at)` per message. Wrapping the column `mt.created_at` in strftime() makes the time-range predicate non-sargable: SQLite cannot use the available index on modmail_ticket(guild_id, status) (migration 038) to seek on the time bound, and there is no expression index on strftime(created_at). The query runs twice per Pulse load (this-window + prior-window) inside getInsights, and joins every matching ticket to modmail_message. created_at is declared TEXT (confirmed via modmail_message migration 021 / modmail_ticket schema and the strftime usage), so this is a genuine scan, not an index seek. A secondary correctness smell: strftime('%s', ...) returns a string compared against a numeric bind param, relying on SQLite type coercion. Impact is bounded today because (a) the whole Pulse bundle is cached (CACHE_TTL.medium, in-flight dedup) and (b) ticket volume is moderate, so this is a latent scaling cost rather than an active outage.
fix: Store/compare modmail timestamps as unix-seconds, or compare the raw TEXT column directly against an ISO bound computed in JS (e.g. `mt.created_at >= ?` with an ISO string), so the predicate is sargable against an index on modmail_ticket(guild_id, created_at). Alternatively add an expression index on strftime('%s', created_at). Same treatment applies to the mm.created_at delta if you start filtering on it.

title: detectNsfwFlagSurge filters nsfw_flags.flagged_at via strftime(), bypassing the guild/reviewed index
detail: detectNsfwFlagSurge runs two counts of the form `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nsfw_flags WHERE guild_id = ? AND strftime('%s', flagged_at) >= ? AND strftime('%s', flagged_at) < ?`. nsfw_flags.flagged_at is declared `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))` (migrations/032_nsfw_flags.ts:45) and the only indexes are idx_nsfw_flags_guild(guild_id) and idx_nsfw_flags_pending(guild_id, reviewed) (lines 53-54). Wrapping flagged_at in strftime() makes the time bound non-sargable, so after the guild_id prefix narrows the set SQLite still scans every flag row for that guild and recomputes strftime per row. Bounded in practice: nsfw_flags has UNIQUE(guild_id, user_id) so row count is capped near member count, and the Pulse bundle is cached. Real but low impact.
fix: Compare flagged_at as a raw ISO string against JS-computed ISO bounds (`flagged_at >= ?`) so an index on nsfw_flags(guild_id, flagged_at) can seek, or store flagged_at as unix-seconds INTEGER. Mirrors the modmail fix.

category: Performance / repeated work + uncached hot path
title: getReviewQueue evaluates the same correlated modmail-EXISTS subquery three times per row and is loaded uncached on every /dashboard/reviews navigation
detail: getReviewQueue is called directly from web/src/routes/dashboard/reviews/+layout.server.ts:14 (no cached() wrapper, unlike the stats/pulse loaders), so it runs on every navigation to /dashboard/reviews and /dashboard/reviews/[appId]. The query embeds the same correlated subquery pattern (`SELECT 1 FROM modmail_ticket JOIN modmail_message ... AND mm.id = (SELECT MAX(mm2.id) FROM modmail_message WHERE ticket_id = mt.id) AND mm.direction = 'to_staff'`) three separate times: twice in the SELECT list (has_unread_modmail at 404-411, modmail_awaiting_since at 412-419) and once again inside the ORDER BY (432-439). SQLite re-derives the per-row max-message lookup for each occurrence. The modmail_message subqueries are index-backed (idx_modmail_message_ticket_id, migration 063) and the outer set is bounded to applications with status IN ('submitted','needs_info'), so cost scales with the pending-queue size (typically tens). Defensible but not severe.
fix: Compute the latest-message-per-ticket once via a LEFT JOIN to a subquery/CTE that resolves the newest modmail_message per (guild_id,user_id), exposing direction + created_at, then reference it in SELECT and ORDER BY instead of three correlated subqueries. Consider wrapping the layout load in the existing cached() helper (short TTL) since the queue changes infrequently between renders.

title: rebuildDailyMetrics issues one COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) query per day in a 95-iteration loop
detail: The per-day finalize loop runs `wauStmt.get(guildId, dayStartS-6d, dayStartS+1d)` once for every day in the window (WINDOW_DAYS = 95, line 30), i.e. ~95 separate `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM message_activity WHERE guild_id = ? AND created_at_s >= ? AND created_at_s < ?` executions per refresh, each scanning a 7-day rolling slice of the message_activity table (overlapping windows re-read the same rows ~7x). All other aggregates in this function are already single GROUP BY scans, so this rolling-WAU is the one N+1. It is an out-of-band cron/CLI job (scripts/refresh-public-stats.ts, ~every 15 min) on a writable connection, not a request path, so user-facing impact is zero; it only lengthens refresh wall-time as message_activity grows. The index idx_message_activity_guild_time_user_channel (migration 070) keeps each query cheap but cannot eliminate the 7x row re-read.
fix: Replace the per-day loop query with a single windowed pass: compute distinct-author-per-day once, then derive the 7-day rolling distinct count in SQL (e.g. a self-join/window over a daily distinct-author CTE) or accept daily DAU and compute 7d WAU approximately. At minimum, hoisting it out of the per-day JS loop into one GROUP BY removes 94 prepared-statement round-trips.

title: Server-side cached() defeats SSE live-refresh on pulse/stats; invalidate() is never called by any mutation
detail: The two-tier cache exposes invalidate(key), but a repo-wide search shows it has ZERO callers anywhere in web/src (only the definition matches). Meanwhile the mutation API routes (/api/review/[action], /api/modmail/*, /api/config/update, etc.) mutate state through the bot and return without touching the cache. The Pulse page (web/src/routes/dashboard/pulse/+page.svelte:83-92) explicitly subscribes to review:*, modmail:*, flag:* and calls invalidateAll() on each event to deliver 'Live pulse updates'; the Stats page does the same on stats:updated. But the data those pages render comes from cached(guildKey, CACHE_TTL.medium=60_000, ...) (pulse) and cached(personalKey/teamKey, CACHE_TTL.medium, ...) (stats), keyed by rangeCacheKeyParts(range,60) whose minute bucket is stable inside any 60s window. So after a moderator approves an application: the DB changes, the SSE event arrives (~150ms debounce), invalidateAll() re-runs the server load, and cached() returns the SAME pre-mutation L1 object for up to ~60s. The counters (Pending Applications, Open Modmail, Decisions/Approvals, team leaderboard) visibly fail to update despite the live wiring, until the TTL lapses. The reviews queue itself is unaffected because its layout load (reviews/+layout.server.ts) is uncached.
fix: Wire invalidate() into the mutation handlers (or invalidate by key prefix) so a review/modmail/flag/config mutation drops the matching pulse:*/stats:* cache entries. Since keys embed guildId + range bucket + (for personal) userId, add a small prefix-scan invalidation (e.g. track keys per namespace, or switch the L1 Map to allow deleting by startsWith('pulse:guild:'+guildId)). Alternatively, have the SSE-triggered reload pass a cache-busting flag the load honors. Minimum: call invalidate for stats:team:* and pulse:guild:* on any review/modmail mutation so the live refresh shows fresh counts.

lines: 49-74 (Promise.race + timeout); queries in web/src/lib/server/queries/audit.ts:55-60 are synchronous better-sqlite3
title: Audit query 8s timeout is ineffective: Promise.race cannot interrupt synchronous better-sqlite3 work
detail: The audit load wraps cached(key, ...) in Promise.race against a setTimeout(8000) that rejects with 'audit-query-timeout' and maps to a 504 ('Narrow the date range...'). But getAuditLog/getActionTypes run synchronously via better-sqlite3 (db().prepare(...).all/get) and block the Node event loop for their entire duration. While the synchronous query runs, the setTimeout callback cannot fire; by the time control returns to the loop, the cached() promise has already resolved and wins the race. The timeout therefore provides no protection at all: a genuinely heavy audit query (broad FTS search over a large window) freezes the whole web process (all concurrent requests, SSE heartbeats, other tabs) for its full runtime, and the 504 branch is effectively dead code. The load trusts Promise.race to bound work that is fundamentally uninterruptible from JS.
fix: Either (a) remove the timeout and bound the work at the SQL/data layer instead (hard LIMITs, mandatory date window, FTS prefix caps, a covering index, or a statement-level progress-handler/interrupt on the better-sqlite3 connection), or (b) move audit queries to a worker_thread so a watchdog timer can actually cancel/abandon them. Do not present a Promise.race timeout as a guard against synchronous DB calls; at minimum drop the misleading 504 path.

lines: 42-64 (attr injection runs for all pages); web/src/routes/observatory/+page.server.ts:21-23 (public cache-control); confirmed unused by web/src/lib/styles/observatory.css:5
title: Observatory response is marked public but its HTML varies by per-visitor cookies (data-style/--hue) with no Vary
detail: transformPageChunk strips the inline theme <script> only for /observatory (gated by isObservatory), but the block that injects data-style="..." and style="--hue:..." onto the <html> tag (lines 52-62) runs UNCONDITIONALLY, including for /observatory, driven by the visitor's paw-style/paw-hue cookies. The observatory load sets 'cache-control: public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=86400'. A public directive permits shared caches (Cloudflare sits in front per the SSE proxy notes) to store and replay one visitor's HTML to others, yet the body differs by cookie and no Vary: Cookie is sent. Today the visible impact is nil because observatory.css explicitly 'does NOT read var(--hue) or any site token' (its own comment), so the injected attrs are inert there. But it is a latent cache-correctness defect: the moment any global selector keys off [data-style] or --hue, the public cache would serve one user's theme to everyone. It also means the zero-JS page is needlessly emitting per-user-varying markup the page cannot use.
fix: Skip the data-style/--hue injection when isObservatory (the page is intentionally theme-agnostic), so the public response is byte-identical for all visitors. If per-page theming is ever wanted on a public route, switch that route to private caching or add an explicit Vary that the CDN honors.

title: Live presence (Currently Online / In Voice Now) is bundled into the 60s range-keyed pulse cache
detail: getGuildSnapshot(guildId) (online_count, voice_users_now) is real-time presence that does not depend on the selected time window, but it is computed inside the same cached(guildKey, CACHE_TTL.medium=60_000, ...) object whose key is rangeCacheKeyParts(range,60). Consequences: (1) the UI labels these cards 'live from Discord' / 'connected to voice', yet they are stale by up to ~60s and only refresh when the minute bucket rolls or the user changes the window; (2) switching the time window pointlessly recomputes the snapshot since it shares the range-scoped key. This is a correctness/accuracy mismatch between the 'live' presentation and the caching.
fix: Pull getGuildSnapshot out of the range-keyed bundle and cache it under a window-independent key with a short TTL (e.g. CACHE_TTL.short or no cache), keyed only by guildId, so presence reflects near-real-time state regardless of the selected window.

title: Migration failure is swallowed by `|| echo`, so the bot restarts against an un-migrated schema
detail: The full deploy runs migrations as: `ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js" || echo "Migration step completed (may have warnings)"`. The migration runner scripts/migrate.ts is correctly designed to fail hard: on any migration error it logs and calls `process.exit(1)` (migrate.ts:308-311), and scripts/migrate-remote.js propagates that exit code via `process.exit(result.status || 0)` (migrate-remote.js:24). The `|| echo` in deploy.sh defeats that contract: a non-zero exit (e.g. a migration that throws, a SQLITE_BUSY because the old bot still holds data.db, or migrate-remote.js failing to find tsx) is converted to success. The deploy then proceeds to Step 6.6 (command registration) and Step 7 (`pm2 startOrRestart ecosystem.config.cjs`), starting the NEW code against the OLD schema. Because some migrations are destructive/structural (035_drop_unused_tables DROP TABLE, 028 and 067 DROP TABLE under conditions, 047/053 ADD COLUMN), the new bot can crash-loop on missing columns/tables or read a half-migrated DB. The operator only sees a soothing 'may have warnings' line. This is the central cross-file defect: deploy.sh trusts a wrapper whose carefully-propagated failure signal it then throws away.
fix: Do not swallow the migration exit code. Capture it and abort the deploy before restarting PM2, e.g.: `if ! ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js"; then echo 'ERROR: migrations failed, aborting before restart' >&2; exit 1; fi`. The acquire_deploy_lock EXIT trap will still release the lock. If a 'warnings are tolerable' mode is genuinely wanted, gate it behind an explicit flag rather than making it the default.

title: Legacy scripts/deploy.sh ships migrations/ but never runs them, restarting new code on an old schema
detail: scripts/deploy.sh builds a tarball that includes `migrations` and `scripts` (line 108) and on the remote runs only: extract -> `npm ci --omit=dev` -> `pm2 restart` (lines 123-133). There is no `node scripts/migrate-remote.js` / `migrate.ts` step anywhere (grep confirms 0 occurrences of 'migrate'). So anyone running this script (or following the older docs that reference `./deploy.sh`) deploys new code that expects new schema, but the schema is never advanced. The new bot then hits missing columns/tables. This is the inverse-yet-equivalent failure of the root deploy.sh issue and is easy to trigger because two same-named scripts exist (root `deploy.sh` with migrations, `scripts/deploy.sh` without). It also has no deploy lock and no pre-deploy DB backup, unlike the hardened root script.
fix: Either delete scripts/deploy.sh entirely (the hardened root deploy.sh supersedes it) or add the migration step before `pm2 restart` and a pre-deploy backup + lock. At minimum, have it `exec` the root deploy.sh so there is a single source of truth and no path that skips migrations.

title: Documented rollback script deploy-no-tests.sh has no deploy lock and no pre-deploy backup, yet runs migrations
detail: docs/operations/DEPLOY-AGENT.md documents the rollback procedure as `git checkout HEAD~1 && ./deploy-no-tests.sh` (DEPLOY-AGENT.md:79,125,131). deploy-no-tests.sh runs the migration step (line 25, with the same `|| echo` swallow as the root script) and `pm2 startOrRestart` but: (1) it never acquires the DEPLOY_LOCK_DIR mkdir lock that root deploy.sh uses, so it can race a concurrent `./deploy.sh` and both will scp/extract/restart simultaneously, corrupting the extract or the live WAL; (2) it takes no pre-deploy DB backup (no maybe_backup_remote_db, no Litestream check). Worse, in the documented rollback flow the code is rolled back to HEAD~1 but migrations are still applied FORWARD (the runner only goes forward and tracks via schema_migrations), so you end up with old code on a newer-or-equal schema with zero fresh backup right when you are already in an incident. A rollback path is exactly when you most need the lock and the backup.
fix: Make deploy-no-tests.sh call `acquire_deploy_lock` and `maybe_backup_remote_db` (or just `BACKUP_BEFORE_DEPLOY=1 ./deploy.sh --fast`). Update DEPLOY-AGENT.md so the rollback recipe uses the hardened script with a forced backup, and note that migrations are not auto-reverted on a code rollback.

title: Pre-deploy DB backup copies a live WAL-mode DB without a checkpoint and misreports any cp failure as 'not found'
detail: maybe_backup_remote_db does `cp ${REMOTE_PATH}/data/data.db .../data.db.${ts} 2>/dev/null && echo OK || echo 'WARNING: data.db not found'`. Two problems. (1) No WAL checkpoint before the copy: the DB runs in WAL mode (ecosystem starts the bot which opens WAL; migrate.ts also sets journal_mode=WAL), so a bare `cp` of just data.db can capture a state missing the committed pages still sitting in data.db-wal, yielding a stale or torn backup. Note the OTHER ops paths get this right: scripts/switch.sh:93 and scripts/start.sh:275,313 run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` before copying and also copy -wal/-shm. deploy.sh's backup path is the inconsistent, less-safe sibling. (2) The `2>/dev/null && ... || echo 'data.db not found'` collapses every failure mode (disk full, permission denied, I/O error) into the single misleading message 'data.db not found, skipping backup', and because maybe_backup_remote_db always `return`s success, the deploy proceeds to run destructive migrations (035 DROP TABLE) with no valid backup. This directly undermines the stated guarantee 'a botched migration can be reverted by hand' (deploy.sh:122).
fix: Before copying, run `sqlite3 ${DB} 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);'` (or copy data.db plus -wal/-shm), mirroring switch.sh/start.sh. Distinguish 'file absent' from 'copy failed': test `[ -f data.db ]` first, and on a real cp failure abort the deploy (return non-zero) instead of printing a benign-sounding warning and continuing into destructive migrations.

title: stamp-migrations version-to-name map is misaligned, so it marks the wrong (and unapplied) migrations as applied
detail: stamp-migrations.mjs hardcodes a list mapping versions to names and inserts them into schema_migrations with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. The names are wrong: it maps '047' -> 'lock_db_mode', but the real migration is migrations/047_nsfw_reviewed_tracking.ts (verified on disk and via its exported migrate047NsfwReviewedTracking). There is no 047_lock_db_mode file at all. The list is effectively shifted/invented relative to the actual migrations directory. Because the migration runner (migrate.ts:253) decides what to skip purely by `version` membership in schema_migrations, stamping version '047' makes the runner skip the real 047 migration forever, even though its column changes (nsfw_flags.reviewed_by/reviewed_at) were never applied. The stored `name` being wrong also corrupts the audit trail. The same shift affects other entries (the names do not line up with the on-disk NNN_*.ts files). This is a footgun script that, if run on a fresh or partially-migrated DB, silently desyncs tracking from reality.
fix: Generate the version/name pairs by scanning the migrations/ directory (same regex as migrate.ts: /^(\d{3})_(.+)\.ts$/) instead of a hand-maintained literal list, or delete the script. If a stamping tool must exist, have it import the scan from migrate.ts so it can never drift from the real filenames.

title: run-migration-046 tracks via a different table (migration_log) than the canonical runner (schema_migrations)
detail: run-migration-046.mjs records its completion into a `migration_log` table (lines 24-27), but the canonical runner migrate.ts and migrations/lib/helpers.ts track exclusively in `schema_migrations` (migrate.ts uses schema_migrations 8x, migration_log 0x; migration 046 itself is 046_extend_user_cache_profile.ts and calls recordMigration into schema_migrations). Consequences: (a) running this ad-hoc script does NOT mark 046 as applied in schema_migrations, so the next `./deploy.sh` will re-run migration 046 via migrate.ts; (b) it ALSO opens the DB with `new Database(dbPath)` defaulting fileMustExist:false and DB_PATH defaulting to './data/data.db' relative to cwd, so if invoked from the wrong directory it creates an empty DB and ALTERs a non-existent user_cache; (c) the `SELECT id FROM migration_log` will throw if migration_log does not exist on a given box, since nothing in the canonical schema creates it. The additive ALTERs are individually guarded by a column-existence check so re-running 046 via migrate.ts won't duplicate columns, which is the only reason this is medium and not high, but the dual-table tracking is a real inconsistency that breaks the 'applied versions' contract the whole deploy relies on.
fix: Delete run-migration-046.mjs (migration 046 is already covered by migrations/046_extend_user_cache_profile.ts run through migrate.ts). If kept for emergencies, have it write to schema_migrations via the same recordMigration helper, require fileMustExist:true, and resolve DB_PATH the same way migrate.ts does.

title: Deploy lock is not stale-safe and the EXIT-trap release runs unconditionally, including on early failures from other shells
detail: acquire_deploy_lock uses `mkdir ${DEPLOY_LOCK_DIR}` which is correctly atomic, but the lock directory carries no owner/pid/timestamp metadata. If a deploy is killed with SIGKILL (or the controlling SSH dies) after mkdir but before the EXIT trap fires, the lock dir is left behind and every subsequent deploy aborts with 'another deploy is already in progress' until someone manually `rm -rf`s it (the script even documents this manual step at lines 85-86). There is no max-age auto-break and no record of who holds it. This is a minor availability footgun rather than a data-safety one, but during an incident (when deploys are most frequent) a stale lock blocks the fix. Separately, release_deploy_lock is registered as a bare EXIT trap so it fires on any exit including the early validation `exit 1` paths after the lock is taken; that is correct, but means a second deploy that fails to ACQUIRE the lock and exits will still run the trap and `rm -rf ${DEPLOY_LOCK_DIR}` — wait, the trap is only set after a successful mkdir, so this is benign; flagging only the stale-lock gap.
fix: Write metadata into the lock (e.g. `mkdir` then `echo "$USER $$ $(date -u +%s)" > ${DEPLOY_LOCK_DIR}/owner`), and before aborting on a held lock, optionally break it if older than a threshold (e.g. 30 min) after warning. Keep the atomic mkdir as the primitive.

title: Cron-scheduled prod script imports undeclared @xenova/transformers and fetches remote model weights
detail: scripts/embed-incremental.mjs (and embed-all.mjs, embed-gold.mjs) do `import { pipeline, env } from '@xenova/transformers'`, but @xenova/transformers is NOT present in either package.json or package-lock.json (grep across both manifests and both lockfiles: 0 occurrences). The cross-file break: deploy.sh:408 ships the entire `scripts/` dir to the prod host, and scripts/quality-cron.txt:14 schedules `node scripts/embed-incremental.mjs` every 30 minutes on EC2 (/home/ubuntu/pawtropolis-tech). But the production install runs `npm ci --omit=dev` (deploy.sh:341/421/428), which can only ever install what is in the lockfile. Since the package is in NO manifest, npm never provisions it. Two possibilities, both bad: (a) the cron job has been failing every 30 min with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, logging silently to /tmp/quality-embed.log which the file itself says nobody rotates/checks; or (b) someone ran an out-of-band `npm install @xenova/transformers` directly on prod, meaning an unpinned, lockfile-untracked package runs every 30 min outside any reproducible/auditable dependency set. A prior in-repo audit (audit/2026-05-19/deps-ops-findings.md, Finding 1) flagged @xenova/transformers as carrying a HIGH-severity vuln via onnxruntime-web and removed it from package.json, but these importing scripts were left behind. Worse, embed-incremental.mjs:18 sets `env.allowLocalModels = false` and line 47 calls `pipeline('feature-extraction', 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')`, which downloads model weights from the HuggingFace CDN at runtime with no integrity/version pinning -- a remote executable-artifact fetch in a scheduled prod job.
fix: Decide intent. If the chat-quality pipeline is live: add @xenova/transformers to package.json dependencies pinned to a specific audited version (or isolate it in a dedicated workspace/package with its own lockfile), commit the lockfile so `npm ci` provisions it deterministically, and pin/vendor the model (set allowLocalModels=true with a checked-in model dir, or pin a model revision) so prod does not pull unverified weights every 30 min. If the pipeline is dead, remove embed-*.mjs and the corresponding quality-cron.txt entry. Either way, stop relying on an out-of-band manual install on prod.

lines: 18 (invoked by deploy.sh:435; tsx classified dev-only in package.json:90 / package-lock.json:7944)
title: Prod migration step runs `npx tsx`, auto-downloading an unpinned build tool against the live DB
detail: deploy.sh:435 runs `node scripts/migrate-remote.js` on the production host (via ssh_remote), and migrate-remote.js:18 does `spawnSync('npx', ['tsx', 'scripts/migrate.ts', ...], { shell: true })`. tsx is a devDependency (package.json:90; package-lock.json:7940-7944 has `"dev": true`), so the prod install via `npm ci --omit=dev` (deploy.sh:341/421/428) excludes it from node_modules. When `npx tsx` runs and tsx is not locally installed, npx fetches it from the registry on demand. The deploy ssh invocation is non-interactive (no TTY), so npx skips its 'Ok to proceed?' prompt and installs automatically. Net effect: every production migration downloads tsx (and its transitive deps) fresh from npm at an unpinned latest-matching version and executes it with full access to the production SQLite database. A compromised tsx release (or a registry MITM) would run arbitrary code on the DB host during migration. This is distinct from CI, where `npx tsx` (ci.yml:54) runs only after `npm ci` has already installed tsx locally.
fix: Make tsx available deterministically on prod for the migration path: either move tsx to dependencies, or compile the migration runner to plain JS in `dist` and invoke `node dist/.../migrate.js` so no runtime TypeScript loader is needed, or pin the exact tsx version with `npx -p tsx@<pinned> tsx ...` after verifying it is installed from the lockfile. Avoid bare `npx <tool>` on the production host.

title: Alternate `--fresh` deploy path runs `npm ci` (with devDependencies) on the production host
detail: The hardened canonical deploy (deploy.sh:341, 421, 428) correctly installs prod deps with `npm ci --omit=dev`. But the alternate remote-fresh deploy paths in scripts/start.sh:700 (`ssh ... 'cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && tar -xzf deploy.tar.gz && npm ci'`) and scripts/start.cmd:656 (identical) run plain `npm ci`, which installs the FULL devDependency tree on prod: eslint, @typescript-eslint/*, vitest, @vitest/*, tsup, tsx, prettier, @anthropic-ai/sdk, pino-pretty, etc. (package.json:76-93). Every one of those plus their transitive deps gets installed and may execute install lifecycle scripts on the production host, substantially enlarging the supply-chain attack surface for no runtime benefit (the bot runs from prebuilt dist/ via ecosystem.config.cjs and does not need the dev toolchain). The inconsistency also means dependency provisioning differs depending on which deploy entrypoint the operator uses.
fix: Change both start.sh:700 and start.cmd:656 to `npm ci --omit=dev` to match deploy.sh, or deprecate these legacy fresh-deploy paths in favor of the hardened deploy.sh so there is a single, consistent install command on prod.

lines: 67-75 (root overrides); web/package.json:28-31 (web overrides); neither appears in the matching package-lock.json root package node
title: Security `overrides` floors are not recorded in the lockfiles, so they are not enforced on re-resolution
detail: Root package.json declares overrides for known-vulnerable transitive deps (protobufjs >=7.5.8, fast-uri >=3.1.2, jws >=4.0.1, minimatch >=9.0.7, brace-expansion >=2.0.3, @tootallnate/once >=3.0.1, ws >=8.20.1), and web/package.json declares overrides (picomatch >=4.0.4, brace-expansion >=2.0.3). However the root `packages[""]` node of package-lock.json (lines 7-46) and of web/package-lock.json (lines 7-39) contain NO `overrides` key (grep: 0 matches in either lockfile). npm normally persists the resolved overrides object into the lockfile root when `npm install` is run with overrides present; its absence indicates the lockfiles were generated/updated without the overrides materialized. Currently this is benign in practice: I confirmed the presently-resolved versions all satisfy the declared floors (e.g. package-lock.json: ws 8.20.1, minimatch 10.2.5, jws 4.0.1, brace-expansion 5.0.6, fast-uri 3.1.2, protobufjs 8.4.0, @tootallnate/once 3.0.1), there are no nested duplicate copies below the floors, and `npm install --package-lock-only` reports 'up to date' / `npm ci --dry-run` exits 0 (so deploy/CI are not broken). The defect is defense-in-depth: because the floors are not captured in the lockfile, a future `npm install` that bumps a transitive dependency could resolve one of these packages below the intended security floor without the override catching it, silently reintroducing a vulnerable version. The package.json intent and the lockfile reality have diverged.
fix: Regenerate both lockfiles with the overrides applied (delete node_modules + the lockfile and run `npm install` in root and in web/, or run `npm install` so npm rewrites packages[""].overrides), then commit. Verify the lockfile root node contains the `overrides` object and that `npm ls minimatch ws jws fast-uri protobufjs brace-expansion` shows only floor-satisfying versions.

title: Quality-pipeline script imports @anthropic-ai/sdk, which is a devDependency absent from prod installs
detail: scripts/llm-label.mjs:15 does `import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk'`, but that package is declared only in devDependencies (package.json:77). It is part of the same EC2 chat-quality pipeline as the embed/score scripts (which deploy.sh:408 ships to prod). It is not in quality-cron.txt, so it is run manually rather than scheduled, which limits impact. Still, on any prod install done with `npm ci --omit=dev` (the documented deploy path) the import fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and the practical workaround tends to be an out-of-band, lockfile-untracked `npm install` on the host -- the same anti-pattern as the @xenova finding, one severity tier lower because it is not on a timer.
fix: If llm-label.mjs is meant to run on prod, move @anthropic-ai/sdk to dependencies (pinned) and commit the lockfile so `npm ci --omit=dev` provisions it; otherwise document that this script is build-host-only and must be run where devDependencies are installed. Do not rely on manual installs on the prod host.
